studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2: Theme Structure & Inheritance
## Comprehensive Study Notes — Week 1, Day 1

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Overview & Big Picture](#1-overview--big-picture)
2. [Theme Directory Structure](#2-theme-directory-structure)
3. [Core Theme Files](#3-core-theme-files)
4. [Theme Inheritance & Fallback Chain](#4-theme-inheritance--fallback-chain)
5. [Static File Fallback Resolution](#5-static-file-fallback-resolution)
6. [Module Override Directory Structure](#6-module-override-directory-structure)
7. [etc/view.xml — Image Configuration](#7-etcviewxml--image-configuration)
8. [pub/static — Compiled Output](#8-pubstatic--compiled-output)
9. [Theme-Level i18n Translation Priority](#9-theme-level-i18n-translation-priority)
10. [Magento/blank & Magento/luma Relationship](#10-magentoblank--magentoluma-relationship)
11. [Hands-On: Creating a Minimal Custom Theme](#11-hands-on-creating-a-minimal-custom-theme)
12. [Common Pitfalls & Tricky Exam Scenarios](#12-common-pitfalls--tricky-exam-scenarios)
13. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#13-quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Overview & Big Picture

Magento 2 themes control the **visual presentation layer** of a storefront. They follow a strict convention-over-configuration approach: file placement determines behavior, and a well-defined **fallback chain** means you only need to override what you change.

```
+--------------------------------------------------+
|             Request for a Theme File             |
+--------------------------------------------------+
                         |
                         v
          +-----------------------------+
          |   Custom Theme (Vendor/X)   |  <-- highest priority
          +-----------------------------+
                         |  (not found)
                         v
          +-----------------------------+
          |   Parent Theme (e.g. Luma)  |
          +-----------------------------+
                         |  (not found)
                         v
          +-----------------------------+
          |   Magento/blank             |
          +-----------------------------+
                         |  (not found)
                         v
          +-----------------------------+
          |   lib/web (global library)  |  <-- lowest priority
          +-----------------------------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- Themes live under `app/design/frontend/Vendor/theme_name/`
- The fallback chain is deterministic and hierarchical
- `pub/static/` is **never** edited directly — it is a build artifact

---

## 2. Theme Directory Structure

A complete Magento 2 theme follows this canonical layout:

```
app/design/frontend/
└── Vendor/
    └── theme_name/
        |
        +-- theme.xml                   # Theme declaration + parent
        +-- registration.php            # Component registration
        +-- composer.json               # Composer metadata (optional for local)
        |
        +-- etc/
        |   └── view.xml               # Image roles & dimensions
        |
        +-- web/                        # Static assets (CSS, JS, images, fonts)
        |   +-- css/
        |   |   +-- source/
        |   |   |   +-- _theme.less    # Theme variable overrides
        |   |   |   └── _extend.less   # Add-on styles (picked up by @magento_import)
        |   +-- images/
        |   |   └── logo.svg           # Theme logo
        |   +-- fonts/
        |   └── js/
        |
        +-- i18n/                       # Translation CSV files
        |   └── en_US.csv
        |
        +-- media/
        |   └── preview.jpg            # Admin preview thumbnail
        |
        +-- Magento_Theme/             # Module-scoped overrides
        |   +-- layout/
        |   |   └── default.xml
        |   └── templates/
        |       └── html/
        |           └── header.phtml
        |
        +-- Magento_Catalog/           # Another module override example
        |   +-- layout/
        |   |   └── catalog_product_view.xml
        |   └── templates/
        |       └── product/
        |           └── view/
        |               └── gallery.phtml
        |
        └── Magento_Checkout/
            └── layout/
                └── checkout_index_index.xml
```

**Exam focus:**
- Module overrides **must** be placed under `Magento_ModuleName/` within the theme directory
- The subdirectory name is the **module name**, not the full `Vendor_Module` format — it IS the full name (e.g., `Magento_Catalog`, not just `Catalog`)
- `web/` contains only **source** static assets, never compiled output
- Note: `styles-m.less` (at `web/css/styles-m.less`) is the mobile stylesheet entry point; a custom theme normally inherits it from the parent rather than creating its own

---

## 3. Core Theme Files

### 3.1 `theme.xml`

The primary theme declaration file. Tells Magento the theme's name, parent, and preview image.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<theme xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
       xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Config/etc/theme.xsd">
    <title>Vendor MyTheme</title>
    <parent>Magento/luma</parent>
    <media>
        <preview_image>media/preview.jpg</preview_image>
    </media>
</theme>
```

**Key attributes:**

| Element | Purpose | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `<title>` | Human-readable theme name in Admin | Yes |
| `<parent>` | Defines inheritance parent (`Vendor/theme`) | No (base themes omit it) |
| `<media><preview_image>` | Path to admin preview relative to theme root | No |

**Exam focus:**
- `<parent>` value format is `Vendor/theme_name` — same as the directory path under `app/design/frontend/`
- A theme with **no `<parent>`** is a standalone base theme
- `Magento/blank` has no parent; `Magento/luma` declares `<parent>Magento/blank</parent>`

---

### 3.2 `registration.php`

Registers the theme as a Magento component so the framework discovers it.

```php
<?php
/**
 * Theme registration file
 */
use Magento\Framework\Component\ComponentRegistrar;

ComponentRegistrar::register(
    ComponentRegistrar::THEME,           // Component type = THEME
    'frontend/Vendor/theme_name',        // Area/Vendor/theme_name
    __DIR__                              // Absolute path to theme root
);
```

**Exam focus:**
- First argument is always `ComponentRegistrar::THEME` for themes
- Second argument format: `area/Vendor/theme_name` (e.g., `frontend/Acme/mytheme`)
- Valid areas: `frontend`, `adminhtml`
- Without this file the theme will **not** appear in Admin → Content → Design → Themes

---

### 3.3 `composer.json`

Required for themes distributed via Composer/Marketplace. Optional for local themes.

```json
{
    "name": "vendor/theme-frontend-mytheme",
    "description": "Vendor MyTheme for Magento 2",
    "require": {
        "php": "~8.2.0||~8.3.0||~8.4.0",
        "magento/theme-frontend-luma": "*",
        "magento/framework": "*"
    },
    "type": "magento2-theme",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "license": ["OSL-3.0", "AFL-3.0"],
    "autoload": {
        "files": ["registration.php"]
    }
}
```

**Exam focus:**
- `"type": "magento2-theme"` tells Composer this is a Magento theme component
- `autoload.files` must include `registration.php` so Composer triggers theme registration
- For local development in `app/design/`, `composer.json` is **not required** — `registration.php` is sufficient

---

## 4. Theme Inheritance & Fallback Chain

### 4.1 How Inheritance Works

Magento 2 uses a **file-based inheritance model**. When a file is requested, Magento walks up the inheritance chain until the file is found.

```
Theme Inheritance Declaration:

  Vendor/mytheme (theme.xml: parent = Magento/luma)
       |
       v
  Magento/luma   (theme.xml: parent = Magento/blank)
       |
       v
  Magento/blank  (theme.xml: no parent)
       |
       v
  lib/web        (global JavaScript/CSS library — no theme.xml)
```

### 4.2 Full Fallback Chain for Module Templates

For a file like `Magento_Catalog/templates/product/view.phtml`:

```
1. app/design/frontend/Vendor/mytheme/Magento_Catalog/templates/product/view.phtml
   (custom theme override)

2. app/design/frontend/Magento/luma/Magento_Catalog/templates/product/view.phtml
   (parent theme override)

3. app/design/frontend/Magento/blank/Magento_Catalog/templates/product/view.phtml
   (grandparent theme override)

4. app/code/Magento/Catalog/view/frontend/templates/product/view.phtml
   (module original source)
```

### 4.3 Full Fallback Chain for Theme Web Assets

For a file like `images/logo.svg` or `css/styles-m.css`:

```
1. app/design/frontend/Vendor/mytheme/web/images/logo.svg
2. app/design/frontend/Magento/luma/web/images/logo.svg
3. app/design/frontend/Magento/blank/web/images/logo.svg
4. lib/web/images/logo.svg
```

**Exam focus:**
- Module source files (`app/code/.../view/frontend/`) are at the **bottom** of the fallback for templates
- `lib/web` is only in the fallback for **static web assets**, NOT for templates or layout XML
- Layout XML files follow the same theme fallback but are **merged**, not replaced
- Static assets are **replaced** (first match wins); Layout XML is **merged** across all found files

---

## 5. Static File Fallback Resolution

Magento resolves static files during `setup:static-content:deploy` (production) or on the fly (developer mode).

### Resolution Order (most to least specific):

```
Priority  Location
-------   --------
1         app/design/frontend/Vendor/mytheme/web/
2         app/design/frontend/Vendor/mytheme/Magento_X/web/
3         app/design/frontend/Magento/luma/web/
4         app/design/frontend/Magento/luma/Magento_X/web/
5         app/design/frontend/Magento/blank/web/
6         app/design/frontend/Magento/blank/Magento_X/web/
7         app/code/Magento/X/view/frontend/web/
8         lib/web/
```

**Exam focus:**
- Module-scoped web assets live under `Magento_X/web/` inside the theme, **not** under the theme's root `web/`
- Global theme assets live directly under `web/` in the theme root
- `lib/web` contains RequireJS, jQuery, and other shared libraries used system-wide

---

## 6. Module Override Directory Structure

This is one of the **most tested** areas. Overriding module files requires exact directory naming.

### 6.1 Template Overrides

**Module source location:**
```
app/code/Magento/Catalog/view/frontend/templates/product/listing.phtml
```

**Theme override location:**
```
app/design/frontend/Vendor/mytheme/Magento_Catalog/templates/product/listing.phtml
```

The mapping rule:
```
app/code/{Vendor}/{Module}/view/frontend/templates/{path}
                                    |
                                    v
app/design/frontend/{Vendor}/{Theme}/{Vendor}_{Module}/templates/{path}
```

### 6.2 Layout XML Overrides

**Module source location:**
```
app/code/Magento/Catalog/view/frontend/layout/catalog_product_view.xml
```

**Theme override location:**
```
app/design/frontend/Vendor/mytheme/Magento_Catalog/layout/catalog_product_view.xml
```

**Exam focus:**
- Layout XML in themes is **merged** with module layout XML — it does NOT fully replace it
- To remove a block or container, use `<referenceBlock name="block.name" remove="true"/>` or the standalone `<remove name="block.name"/>` element
- To hide without removing, use `display="false"`: `<referenceBlock name="block.name" display="false"/>`
- Template `.phtml` files in themes **do** fully replace the module version (no merging)

### 6.3 Module Web Assets (JS/CSS/Images)

**Module source:**
```
app/code/Magento/Catalog/view/frontend/web/js/product-gallery.js
```

**Theme override:**
```
app/design/frontend/Vendor/mytheme/Magento_Catalog/web/js/product-gallery.js
```

### Directory Naming Quick Reference

| Override Type | Theme Path |
|---|---|
| Templates | `Magento_Catalog/templates/` |
| Layout XML | `Magento_Catalog/layout/` |
| Web assets | `Magento_Catalog/web/` |
| Email templates | `Magento_Catalog/email/` |

---

## 7. `etc/view.xml` — Image Configuration

The `etc/view.xml` file defines **image dimension presets** used by the catalog. Every image role has a named configuration block.

### 7.1 Full Structure (based on actual Magento/blank view.xml)

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<view xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
      xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Config/etc/view.xsd">

    <media>
        <images module="Magento_Catalog">

            <!-- Product base image — no fixed dimensions (unconstrained) -->
            <image id="product_page_image_large" type="image"/>

            <!-- Product detail page (PDP) main image — 700×700 -->
            <image id="product_page_image_medium" type="image">
                <width>700</width>
                <height>700</height>
            </image>

            <!-- Product listing / category page image -->
            <image id="category_page_grid" type="small_image">
                <width>240</width>
                <height>300</height>
            </image>

            <!-- Cart/wishlist thumbnail (type is small_image, NOT thumbnail) -->
            <image id="cart_page_product_thumbnail" type="small_image">
                <width>110</width>
                <height>160</height>
            </image>

            <!-- Swatch image (type is thumbnail in blank, NOT swatch_image) -->
            <image id="product_swatch_image_small" type="thumbnail">
                <width>88</width>
                <height>110</height>
            </image>

        </images>
    </media>

</view>
```

### 7.2 Image Type Reference

These are the image **role** types used by the `type` attribute. The types available depend on which modules define them:

| Type Attribute | Used For | Example ID in Blank |
|---|---|---|
| `image` | Product detail page (PDP) main, large views | `product_page_image_large`, `product_page_image_medium` |
| `small_image` | Category/listing grid, cart thumbnails | `category_page_grid`, `cart_page_product_thumbnail` |
| `thumbnail` | Smaller UI thumbnails, swatch previews | `product_swatch_image_small` |
| `swatch_image` | Configurable product swatches (defined by `Magento_Swatches` module, NOT blank theme) | `swatch_image` (in `module-swatches/etc/view.xml`) |

**Exam focus:**
- `type` maps to the product image **role** assigned in the Admin product editor
- `id` is an arbitrary unique string used to reference the preset in layout/template code
- If a theme inherits from a parent, child `view.xml` **replaces** (not merges) parent's `view.xml`
- Missing `view.xml` in a custom theme = falls back to parent's `view.xml`
- Image dimensions are used by `Magento\Catalog\Block\Product\Image` and image resize tooling
- The `swatch_image` type is defined in the Swatches module's `view.xml`, not in the Blank theme
- An `<image>` element with no `<width>`/`<height>` children (like `product_page_image_large`) means unconstrained dimensions

### 7.3 How Images Are Resized

```
Admin uploads image -> stored in pub/media/catalog/product/
                                    |
                     On first request or during deploy:
                                    |
                     view.xml preset defines target W x H
                                    |
                     Resized cache stored in:
                     pub/media/catalog/product/cache/{hash}/
```

---

## 8. `pub/static/` — Compiled Output

### 8.1 What It Is

`pub/static/` is the **web-accessible static file directory**. It contains:
- Deployed/symlinked theme assets
- Compiled LESS → CSS
- RequireJS configuration bundles
- Merged JS files

### 8.2 Directory Structure

```
pub/static/
└── frontend/
    └── Vendor/
        └── mytheme/
            └── en_US/
                +-- css/
                |   +-- styles-m.css      # compiled from LESS
                |   └── styles-l.css
                +-- js/
                +-- images/
                +-- fonts/
                +-- requirejs-config.js   # merged RequireJS config
                └── Magento_Catalog/
                    └── js/
```

### 8.3 How It Gets Populated

| Mode | Method |
|---|---|
| **Developer** | Files are symlinked or copied on first request (slow first load) |
| **Production** | `bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy` copies/compiles everything |
| **Default** | Similar to developer but without full debug tools |

```bash
# Deploy static content for production
bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_US -f

# Deploy for specific theme only
bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_US --theme Vendor/mytheme -f

# Clear static content cache
bin/magento cache:clean
rm -rf pub/static/frontend/
```

**Exam focus:**
- **NEVER edit files in `pub/static/` directly** — they are overwritten on next deploy
- After any theme file change in developer mode, run `bin/magento cache:clean`
- After LESS changes in developer mode, you may need to delete `pub/static/frontend/` and `var/view_preprocessed/`
- `setup:static-content:deploy` reads from `app/design/` and `app/code/`, NOT from `pub/static/`

---

## 9. Theme-Level i18n Translation Priority

### 9.1 Translation Sources (Highest to Lowest Priority)

```
Priority  Source
--------  ------
1 (High)  Database (inline translation / translation table)
2         Theme i18n/ CSV   <-- higher than module!
3         Module i18n/ CSV
4 (Low)   lib/web/i18n/ CSV (global JS strings)
```

### 9.2 Theme Translation File Location

```
app/design/frontend/Vendor/mytheme/i18n/en_US.csv
```

### 9.3 CSV Format

```csv
"Add to Cart","Add to Basket"
"My Account","Your Account"
"Search","Find Products"
"Home Page","Homepage"
```

Each line: `"original string","translated/overridden string"`

**Exam focus:**
- Theme-level `i18n/en_US.csv` **overrides** module-level translations for the same string
- This is the correct way to override module strings without modifying module files
- File naming must match the locale code exactly: `en_US.csv`, `de_DE.csv`, etc.
- Theme translations are **merged** into the final translation dictionary, with theme taking priority over module
- Database translations come from the inline translation feature (Admin > Stores > Configuration > Advanced > Developer > Translate Inline) and the `translation` database table

### 9.4 Module Translation Location (for comparison)

```
app/code/Magento/Catalog/i18n/en_US.csv
```

---

## 10. Magento/blank & Magento/luma Relationship

### 10.1 Magento/blank

The **base theme** for all Magento 2 frontend themes. Has no parent.

Key characteristics:
- Provides core layout XML handles and block structure
- Contains essential LESS variables framework
- Defines default `etc/view.xml` image sizes
- Located: `vendor/magento/theme-frontend-blank/`

```xml
<!-- Magento/blank theme.xml — no parent, but HAS preview image -->
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<theme xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
       xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Config/etc/theme.xsd">
    <title>Magento Blank</title>
    <media>
        <preview_image>media/preview.jpg</preview_image>
    </media>
</theme>
```

### 10.2 Magento/luma

The **reference storefront theme** extending Blank. Built with LESS and Bootstrap-inspired grid.

Key characteristics:
- Declares `Magento/blank` as parent
- Overrides many layout XML files and templates from modules
- Contains full LESS stylesheet system under `web/css/source/`
- Located: `vendor/magento/theme-frontend-luma/`

```xml
<!-- Magento/luma theme.xml -->
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<theme xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
       xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Config/etc/theme.xsd">
    <title>Magento Luma</title>
    <parent>Magento/blank</parent>
    <media>
        <preview_image>media/preview.jpg</preview_image>
    </media>
</theme>
```

### 10.3 Recommended Custom Theme Inheritance

```
For a new project:

Vendor/mytheme → Magento/luma → Magento/blank
    (your theme)    (rich UI)      (base)

OR for a leaner theme:

Vendor/mytheme → Magento/blank
    (your theme)   (minimal base)
```

**Exam focus:**
- `Magento/luma` inherits from `Magento/blank` — this is the standard two-level chain
- You should typically extend `Magento/luma` for a fully-featured starting point
- You can extend `Magento/blank` for a custom build with minimal inherited styling
- Both `blank` and `luma` are in `vendor/magento/` (installed via Composer) — **never modify them directly**

### 10.4 Comparison Table

| Feature | Magento/blank | Magento/luma |
|---|---|---|
| Parent | None | Magento/blank |
| LESS complexity | Minimal | Full design system |
| Templates | Core only | Enhanced overrides |
| Use case | Custom builds from scratch | Standard storefronts |
| Location | `vendor/magento/theme-frontend-blank` | `vendor/magento/theme-frontend-luma` |

---

## 11. Hands-On: Creating a Minimal Custom Theme

### 11.1 Create the Directory Structure

```bash
# From Magento root
mkdir -p app/design/frontend/Acme/mytheme/etc
mkdir -p app/design/frontend/Acme/mytheme/web/css/source
mkdir -p app/design/frontend/Acme/mytheme/web/images
mkdir -p app/design/frontend/Acme/mytheme/media
mkdir -p app/design/frontend/Acme/mytheme/i18n
```

### 11.2 Create `theme.xml`

```bash
cat > app/design/frontend/Acme/mytheme/theme.xml << 'EOF'
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<theme xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
       xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Config/etc/theme.xsd">
    <title>Acme MyTheme</title>
    <parent>Magento/luma</parent>
    <media>
        <preview_image>media/preview.jpg</preview_image>
    </media>
</theme>
EOF
```

### 11.3 Create `registration.php`

```php
<?php
/**
 * Acme MyTheme - Theme Registration
 */
use Magento\Framework\Component\ComponentRegistrar;

ComponentRegistrar::register(
    ComponentRegistrar::THEME,
    'frontend/Acme/mytheme',
    __DIR__
);
```

### 11.4 Create `etc/view.xml`

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<view xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
      xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Config/etc/view.xsd">
    <media>
        <images module="Magento_Catalog">
            <image id="product_page_image_large" type="image"/>
            <image id="product_page_image_medium" type="image">
                <width>800</width>
                <height>800</height>
            </image>
            <image id="category_page_grid" type="small_image">
                <width>280</width>
                <height>350</height>
            </image>
            <image id="cart_page_product_thumbnail" type="small_image">
                <width>100</width>
                <height>100</height>
            </image>
            <image id="product_swatch_image_small" type="thumbnail">
                <width>88</width>
                <height>110</height>
            </image>
        </images>
    </media>
</view>
```

### 11.5 Create a Minimal LESS Override

```less
// app/design/frontend/Acme/mytheme/web/css/source/_theme.less
// Override Luma LESS variables

@primary__color: #e02b27;       // Brand primary color
@link__color: #1979c3;          // Link color
@font-family__base: 'Open Sans', sans-serif;
```

### 11.6 Register and Enable the Theme

```bash
# Step 1: Upgrade to register the new theme component
bin/magento setup:upgrade

# Step 2: Clean caches
bin/magento cache:clean
bin/magento cache:flush

# Step 3: In developer mode, clear static content
rm -rf pub/static/frontend/Acme/
rm -rf var/view_preprocessed/

# Step 4: Verify theme is registered
# Check Admin > Content > Design > Themes
# Or query the database:
# SELECT * FROM theme WHERE theme_path = 'frontend/Acme/mytheme';
```

### 11.7 Apply Theme via Admin

```
Admin > Content > Design > Configuration
  > Select Store View
  > Applied Theme: "Acme MyTheme"
  > Save Configuration
```

Or via CLI:

```bash
# Apply theme by its numeric ID (find the ID from the theme table or Admin)
# Note: there is NO bin/magento theme:list command — only theme:uninstall exists
bin/magento config:set design/theme/theme_id 5 --scope=stores --scope-code=default
bin/magento cache:clean
```

### 11.8 Verify Theme is Working

```bash
# Check theme appears in setup:static-content:deploy output
bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_US --theme Acme/mytheme -f

# Verify files are symlinked/copied
ls pub/static/frontend/Acme/mytheme/

# Check theme in database
mysql -u root -p magento -e "SELECT * FROM theme WHERE theme_path = 'frontend/Acme/mytheme';"
```

---

## 12. Common Pitfalls & Tricky Exam Scenarios

### Pitfall 1: Wrong Module Directory Name

```
WRONG:  app/design/frontend/Acme/mytheme/Catalog/templates/
                                         ^^^^^^^
                                         Missing vendor prefix!

CORRECT: app/design/frontend/Acme/mytheme/Magento_Catalog/templates/
                                          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
                                          Full module name: Vendor_Module
```

### Pitfall 2: Editing `pub/static/` Directly

```
NEVER do this:
  vi pub/static/frontend/Acme/mytheme/en_US/css/styles-m.css

Your changes will be WIPED on next:
  - setup:static-content:deploy
  - Cache flush in developer mode
  - setup:upgrade
```

### Pitfall 3: Layout XML Merging vs Template Replacing

```
Layout XML:
  Theme layout XML is MERGED with module layout XML.
  Both files apply. Use <referenceBlock name="..." remove="true"/>
  or <remove name="block.name"/> to remove blocks.
  Use display="false" to hide without removing.

Templates (.phtml):
  Theme template REPLACES module template entirely.
  Only one file applies — the one highest in fallback chain.
```

### Pitfall 4: Missing `setup:upgrade` After Adding Theme

```bash
# After creating a new theme, ALWAYS run:
bin/magento setup:upgrade

# This scans registration.php files and registers the theme
# Without this, the theme won't appear in Admin
```

### Pitfall 5: `view.xml` Does NOT Merge

```
Unlike layout XML, etc/view.xml is NOT merged.
A child theme's view.xml REPLACES the parent's entirely.

Implication: If you create view.xml in your theme,
you must include ALL image configurations,
not just the ones you're changing.

Solution: Copy parent's view.xml and modify it.
```

### Pitfall 6: `parent` in `theme.xml` Format

```xml
<!-- WRONG: using path separator -->
<parent>Magento\luma</parent>

<!-- WRONG: using full filesystem path -->
<parent>vendor/magento/theme-frontend-luma</parent>

<!-- CORRECT: Vendor/theme_name matching directory structure -->
<parent>Magento/luma</parent>
```

### Pitfall 7: `registration.php` Second Argument Format

```php
// WRONG: missing area prefix
ComponentRegistrar::register(
    ComponentRegistrar::THEME,
    'Acme/mytheme',         // Missing "frontend/"!
    __DIR__
);

// CORRECT: area/Vendor/theme_name
ComponentRegistrar::register(
    ComponentRegistrar::THEME,
    'frontend/Acme/mytheme',
    __DIR__
);
```

### Pitfall 8: Translation Override Scope

```
Theme i18n ONLY overrides translations for that theme's store view.
Module i18n applies globally unless overridden at theme level.

Theme i18n file: app/design/frontend/Vendor/theme/i18n/en_US.csv
This is higher priority than:
  app/code/Magento/Catalog/i18n/en_US.csv
```

### Pitfall 9: `theme:list` Does NOT Exist

```bash
# WRONG — this command does not exist:
bin/magento theme:list

# The only theme-related CLI commands are:
bin/magento theme:uninstall              # Uninstall a Composer-installed theme
bin/magento dev:source-theme:deploy      # Collect and publish source files for theme

# To find theme IDs, query the database or check Admin > Content > Design > Themes
```

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Theme Directory Structure
- [ ] Theme root: `app/design/frontend/Vendor/theme_name/`
- [ ] Required files: `theme.xml`, `registration.php`
- [ ] Optional but common: `composer.json`, `etc/view.xml`, `web/`, `i18n/`, `media/preview.jpg`
- [ ] Module overrides live under `Magento_ModuleName/` subdirectory in theme root

### `theme.xml`
- [ ] `<parent>` format is `Vendor/theme_name` (e.g., `Magento/luma`)
- [ ] Themes without `<parent>` are base themes (e.g., `Magento/blank`)
- [ ] `<title>` is what appears in Admin theme selector
- [ ] `<media><preview_image>` path is relative to theme root

### `registration.php`
- [ ] Uses `ComponentRegistrar::register(ComponentRegistrar::THEME, ...)`
- [ ] Second argument format: `frontend/Vendor/theme_name`
- [ ] Must run `bin/magento setup:upgrade` after adding a new theme
- [ ] For Composer-distributed themes, must be referenced in `composer.json` autoload

### Inheritance & Fallback Chain
- [ ] Order: Custom → Parent → Grandparent (Blank) → lib/web
- [ ] `Magento/luma` parent is `Magento/blank`; `Magento/blank` has no parent
- [ ] Templates: first match wins (replacement)
- [ ] Layout XML: all matches are merged
- [ ] `lib/web` is in the fallback for static assets only, NOT templates

### Module File Overrides
- [ ] Templates: `Magento_Catalog/templates/` (mirrors `view/frontend/templates/`)
- [ ] Layout XML: `Magento_Catalog/layout/`
- [ ] Web assets: `Magento_Catalog/web/`
- [ ] Directory name = full module name (`Magento_Catalog`, not `Catalog`)

### `etc/view.xml`
- [ ] Defines image dimension presets: `product_page_image_large` (no dimensions), `product_page_image_medium` (700×700), `category_page_grid` (240×300)
- [ ] `cart_page_product_thumbnail` is type `small_image` at 110×160 in blank (not `thumbnail`)
- [ ] `product_swatch_image_small` is type `thumbnail` at 88×110 in blank (not `swatch_image`)
- [ ] `swatch_image` type is defined by `Magento_Swatches` module, not the blank theme
- [ ] Child theme `view.xml` **replaces** parent's (no merging) — copy all entries when customizing
- [ ] Resized images cached in `pub/media/catalog/product/cache/`

### Layout XML Block Removal/Hiding
- [ ] Remove a block: `<referenceBlock name="block.name" remove="true"/>` or `<remove name="block.name"/>`
- [ ] Hide without removing: `<referenceBlock name="block.name" display="false"/>`
- [ ] `remove` and `display` attributes also work on `referenceContainer`

### `pub/static/`
- [ ] **Never edit directly** — it is a build artifact
- [ ] Populated by `bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy` in production
- [ ] Populated by symlinks/copy-on-demand in developer mode
- [ ] Clear with `rm -rf pub/static/frontend/` + `bin/magento cache:clean`

### i18n Translations
- [ ] Theme CSV: `i18n/en_US.csv` — higher priority than module translations
- [ ] Priority order (high→low): Database (inline translation) > Theme i18n > Module i18n > lib/web/i18n/
- [ ] Format: `"original","translated"` — one pair per line
- [ ] File name must match locale: `en_US.csv`, `de_DE.csv`

### Magento/blank vs Magento/luma
- [ ] `Magento/blank`: no parent, minimal base, in `vendor/magento/theme-frontend-blank`
- [ ] `Magento/luma`: parent=`Magento/blank`, full UI, in `vendor/magento/theme-frontend-luma`
- [ ] Never modify `vendor/` theme files — extend them in `app/design/`
- [ ] Extending Luma gives full LESS variable system and layout overrides

### Key CLI Commands
- [ ] `bin/magento setup:upgrade` — registers new themes/modules
- [ ] `bin/magento cache:clean` — clears application cache
- [ ] `bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_US --theme Vendor/theme -f`
- [ ] `bin/magento theme:uninstall` — uninstall Composer-installed themes (NO `theme:list` command exists)
- [ ] `bin/magento dev:source-theme:deploy` — collect and publish source files for a theme
- [ ] `rm -rf pub/static/frontend/ var/view_preprocessed/` — full static rebuild

flashcards.question: What is the correct directory path for a custom Magento 2 theme?
flashcards.answer: Custom themes live under app/design/frontend/Vendor/theme_name/. The path follows the pattern area/Vendor/theme_name. For example, a theme called 'mytheme' by vendor 'Acme' would be at app/design/frontend/Acme/mytheme/.
flashcards.hint: Think about the directory structure under app/design/ and which area frontend themes belong to.

flashcards.question: What two files are required at minimum to register a Magento 2 theme?
flashcards.answer: The two required files are theme.xml (which declares the theme name, parent theme, and preview image) and registration.php (which registers the theme as a Magento component using ComponentRegistrar::register()). Without registration.php, the theme will not appear in Admin > Content > Design > Themes.
flashcards.hint: One file declares metadata, the other makes the framework aware of the theme's existence.

flashcards.question: What is the correct format for the <parent> element value in theme.xml?
flashcards.answer: The format is Vendor/theme_name, matching the directory structure under app/design/frontend/. For example, <parent>Magento/luma</parent>. Using backslashes, full filesystem paths, or Composer package names are all incorrect formats.
flashcards.hint: It mirrors the folder names directly under the frontend design directory.

flashcards.question: What is the theme fallback chain for static web assets in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: The fallback chain for static assets is: Custom Theme web/ -> Parent Theme web/ -> Grandparent Theme (Blank) web/ -> lib/web/. Magento walks this hierarchy until the file is found. The lib/web directory (containing jQuery, RequireJS, etc.) is only in the fallback for static assets, NOT for templates or layout XML.
flashcards.hint: Think about the chain from most specific to most generic, ending at the global library directory.

flashcards.question: How do layout XML files and template (.phtml) files differ in how they handle theme overrides?
flashcards.answer: Layout XML files in themes are merged with module layout XML — both files apply, with theme instructions processed after module instructions. Template (.phtml) files in themes fully replace the module version — only the theme copy is used, with no merging. This is a critical distinction for understanding override behavior.
flashcards.hint: One type combines instructions from multiple sources, while the other uses a first-match-wins approach.

flashcards.question: What is the correct directory naming convention for overriding a module's templates in a theme?
flashcards.answer: The directory must use the full module name with underscore notation: Magento_Catalog/templates/, not just Catalog/templates/. The format is Vendor_Module. For example, to override Magento_Catalog templates, place files under app/design/frontend/Vendor/theme/Magento_Catalog/templates/.
flashcards.hint: The folder name includes both the vendor and module name joined by an underscore.

flashcards.question: What does the etc/view.xml file define in a Magento 2 theme, and how does it handle inheritance?
flashcards.answer: The etc/view.xml file defines image dimension presets used by the catalog (e.g., product_page_image_medium at 700x700, category_page_grid at 240x300). Unlike layout XML, view.xml is NOT merged — a child theme's view.xml completely replaces the parent's. If you create a view.xml in your theme, you must include ALL image configurations, not just the ones you're changing.
flashcards.hint: This file controls product image sizes and behaves differently from layout XML regarding parent-child relationships.

flashcards.question: Why should you never edit files directly in pub/static/?
flashcards.answer: The pub/static/ directory is a build artifact containing deployed/symlinked theme assets, compiled LESS to CSS, and merged JS files. Any changes made directly to files in pub/static/ are overwritten on the next setup:static-content:deploy, cache flush in developer mode, or setup:upgrade. Source files should be edited in app/design/ or app/code/ instead.
flashcards.hint: This directory is populated automatically through build processes, not manual edits.

flashcards.question: What is the second argument format for ComponentRegistrar::register() when registering a theme?
flashcards.answer: The format is area/Vendor/theme_name, for example 'frontend/Acme/mytheme'. The area prefix (frontend or adminhtml) is required. Omitting the area prefix (e.g., just 'Acme/mytheme') will cause the registration to fail and the theme will not appear in the Admin panel.
flashcards.hint: Unlike theme.xml's <parent> element, this registration path needs an additional prefix.

flashcards.question: What is the relationship between Magento/blank and Magento/luma themes?
flashcards.answer: Magento/blank is the base theme with no parent — it provides core layout XML, essential LESS variables, and default view.xml image sizes. Magento/luma extends Magento/blank (declares it as parent in theme.xml) and adds a full design system with enhanced templates and a complete LESS stylesheet system. Both are located in vendor/magento/ and should never be modified directly.
flashcards.hint: One is the minimal foundation, the other builds a complete storefront on top of it.

flashcards.question: What is the translation priority order for theme-level i18n CSV files relative to other translation sources?
flashcards.answer: The priority order from highest to lowest is: 1) Database (inline translation), 2) Theme i18n/ CSV, 3) Module i18n/ CSV, 4) lib/web/i18n/ CSV. Theme-level translations override module-level translations for the same string, making theme i18n/en_US.csv the correct way to override module strings without modifying module files.
flashcards.hint: The database always wins, but within file-based translations, the theme sits above the module level.

flashcards.question: How are static files populated in pub/static/ in developer mode versus production mode?
flashcards.answer: In developer mode, files are symlinked or copied on first request (causing a slow first page load). In production mode, files are compiled and copied by running bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy, which reads from app/design/ and app/code/ to populate pub/static/.
flashcards.hint: One mode is on-demand per request, the other requires an explicit CLI command.

flashcards.question: What CLI command is used to deploy static content for a specific theme only?
flashcards.answer: The command is: bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_US --theme Vendor/mytheme -f. The --theme flag limits deployment to the specified theme. The -f flag forces deployment even in developer mode. This command reads from app/design/ and app/code/, NOT from pub/static/.
flashcards.hint: It's the static content deploy command with a flag to scope it to one theme.

flashcards.question: Where do module-scoped web assets (JS/CSS/images) live within a theme, as opposed to global theme assets?
flashcards.answer: Module-scoped web assets live under Magento_ModuleName/web/ inside the theme directory (e.g., Magento_Catalog/web/js/product-gallery.js). Global theme assets live directly under the theme's root web/ directory (e.g., web/css/, web/images/). This distinction is important for the static file fallback resolution.
flashcards.hint: One path includes the module name folder, the other sits directly under the theme's web directory.

flashcards.question: What are the two LESS files commonly used for theme customization and what is each file's purpose?
flashcards.answer: _theme.less (located at web/css/source/_theme.less) is used to override LESS variables like colors, fonts, and spacing inherited from parent themes. _extend.less is used for add-on styles that are automatically picked up by @magento_import. The _theme.less file controls variable-based customization while _extend.less adds new style rules.
flashcards.hint: One overrides variables from the parent theme, the other extends with new CSS rules.

studyNotes.title: Day 2 — Translation & i18n
studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2 Translation & Internationalization (i18n) — Study Notes ## Table of Contents 1. [Overview & Core Concepts](#1-overview--core-concepts) 2. [Translation CSV Format](#2-translation-csv-format) 3. [File Locations](#3-file-locations) 4. [Translation Priority Chain](#4-translation-priority-chain) 5. [CLI Tools — Collecting & Packaging Phrases](#5-cli-tools--collecting--packaging-phrases) 6. [Translation in PHP & JS Templates](#6-translation-in-php--js-templates) 7. [Language Packs](#7-language-packs) 8. [Inline Translation](#8-inline-translation) 9. [JS Translation Mechanism](#9-js-translation-mechanism) 10. [Hands-On: Add a Custom Phrase to a Theme i18n CSV](#10-hands-on-add-a-custom-phrase-to-a-theme-i18n-csv) 11. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist) --- ## 1. Overview & Core Concepts Magento 2's i18n (internationalization) system allows storefront text to be replaced with locale-specific or custom translations **without modifying core code**. ``` +---------------------+ | Source String | e.g. "Add to Cart" +---------------------+ | v +---------------------+ Priority chain resolves | Translation Engine | <-- which replacement wins +---------------------+ | v +---------------------+ | Output to Browser | e.g. "Ajouter au panier" +---------------------+ ``` Key terms: - **Locale code (LL_CC):** Language + Country, e.g. `en_US`, `fr_FR`, `de_DE` - **Translation CSV:** A flat file mapping source → translated phrase - **Language Pack:** A Composer package providing one or more `LL_CC.csv` files - **Inline Translation:** Admin-side tool to override phrases stored in the database --- ## 2. Translation CSV Format Every translation file is a **plain CSV** with exactly **two columns per line**: ```csv "Original English phrase","Translated phrase" "Add to Cart","Ajouter au panier" "Home","Accueil" "Search","Rechercher" "My Account","Mon compte" "Sign In","Connexion" "Sign Out","Déconnexion" ``` ### Rules & Gotchas | Rule | Detail | |------|--------| | **Encoding** | UTF-8, no BOM | | **Quotes** | Both columns must be double-quoted | | **Escaping quotes** | Use `""` inside a quoted string — e.g. `"Say ""Hello"""` | | **One pair per line** | No multiline values | | **File name** | Must match the locale exactly — `en_US.csv`, `fr_FR.csv` | | **Case-sensitive** | `"Add to Cart"` ≠ `"add to cart"` | > **Exam focus:** > - The CSV format is `"source","translation"` — two double-quoted values per line. > - The filename must be the locale code: `LL_CC.csv`. > - UTF-8 without BOM is required. > - Internal double quotes are escaped by doubling them (`""`), not with a backslash. --- ## 3. File Locations Translations can live in **three** main locations, each serving a different purpose: ``` app/ +-- code/ | +-- Vendor/ | +-- Module/ | +-- i18n/ | +-- en_US.csv <-- Module-level translations | +-- design/ | +-- frontend/ | +-- Vendor/ | +-- theme/ | +-- i18n/ | +-- en_US.csv <-- Theme-level translations (OVERRIDE) | vendor/ +-- acme/ +-- language-fr-fr/ +-- composer.json +-- language.xml +-- registration.php +-- fr_FR.csv <-- Language pack CSV at ROOT (NOT in i18n/ subdirectory) ``` ### Location Summary Table | Location | Path Pattern | Purpose | |----------|-------------|---------| | **Module i18n** | `app/code/Vendor/Module/i18n/LL_CC.csv` | Default translations shipped with a module | | **Theme i18n** | `app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/i18n/LL_CC.csv` | Theme-specific overrides — **higher priority** than module | | **Language Pack** | `vendor/*/LL_CC.csv` (at package root, NOT in `i18n/`) | Third-party/community locale translations | | **Database** | `translation` table | Admin inline translation overrides — **highest priority** | > **Exam focus:** > - Theme `i18n/` overrides module `i18n/` for the same phrase. > - The database (inline translation) has the **absolute highest** priority. > - Both module and theme directories use the same CSV format. > - Language pack CSVs live at the **root** of the package directory, not in an `i18n/` subdirectory. The `readPackCsv()` method searches for `*.csv` at the registered component path root. --- ## 4. Translation Priority Chain When Magento resolves a translated string it walks the following chain. The code in `Magento\Framework\Translate::loadData()` calls these methods in order — each subsequent call **overwrites** previous values, so the last one loaded wins: ``` Translate::loadData() executes in this order: 1. _loadModuleTranslation() → loaded FIRST (lowest priority) 2. _loadPackTranslation() → overwrites module 3. _loadThemeTranslation() → overwrites pack 4. _loadDbTranslation() → overwrites everything (HIGHEST) ``` Effective priority (highest to lowest): ``` +-------------------------------------------+ | 1. DATABASE (Admin inline translation) | <-- HIGHEST PRIORITY +-------------------------------------------+ | v +-------------------------------------------+ | 2. THEME i18n/ | | app/design/frontend/V/T/i18n/LL_CC.csv | +-------------------------------------------+ | v +-------------------------------------------+ | 3. LANGUAGE PACK | | vendor/*/LL_CC.csv | +-------------------------------------------+ | v +-------------------------------------------+ | 4. MODULE i18n/ | | app/code/V/M/i18n/LL_CC.csv | <-- LOWEST PRIORITY +-------------------------------------------+ | v +-------------------------------------------+ | 5. FALLBACK: Return original source text | +-------------------------------------------+ ``` ### Priority Chain — Explained 1. **DB (Admin inline translation):** Stored in the `translation` database table. Overrides everything. Set via the Translate Inline editor. 2. **Theme i18n/:** The active theme's CSV. Useful for theme-specific wording changes. 3. **Language Pack:** Composer-installed locale packages. Covers broad locale translation. 4. **Module i18n/:** The module developer's default translation. Lowest priority, always overridable. 5. **Fallback:** If no match is found at any level, the **original source string** is returned as-is. > **Exam focus:** > - Memorize the order: **DB → Theme → Language Pack → Module**. > - The load ORDER in code is Module → Pack → Theme → DB, but since each overwrites previous, the **effective priority** is reversed. > - A missing translation **falls back automatically** through the chain — no error is thrown. > - DB translations are **per store view** and **per locale**. > - Theme i18n sits **above** language packs but **below** DB. --- ## 5. CLI Tools — Collecting & Packaging Phrases ### 5.1 `i18n:collect-phrases` Scans your codebase and extracts all translatable strings into a CSV file. ```bash # Scan a specific directory (e.g. a single module) bin/magento i18n:collect-phrases -o app/code/Vendor/Module/i18n/en_US.csv \ app/code/Vendor/Module # Scan entire Magento installation using --magento/-m flag bin/magento i18n:collect-phrases --magento -o i18n/en_US.csv ``` **What it scans:** | Source Type | Pattern Detected | |-------------|-----------------| | PHP files | `__('text')` and `__("text")` | | PHTML templates | `__('text')` | | JavaScript files | `$.mage.__('text')` | | XML layout files | `translate="true"` attribute | **Output format** — produces a CSV ready for translation: ```csv "Add to Cart","Add to Cart" "Home","Home" "Search","Search" ``` *(Both columns contain the source string until you fill in translations.)* > **Exam focus:** > - Command: `bin/magento i18n:collect-phrases -o ` > - The `-o` flag specifies the output file path. > - The directory path is a **positional argument**, or use `--magento`/`-m` to scan the entire Magento installation (these are mutually exclusive). > - Scans PHP, PHTML, JS, and XML sources. > - Output is a CSV with the source string in **both** columns — you translate the right column. ### 5.2 `i18n:pack` Packages a translation CSV file into a **language pack** structure. ```bash # Syntax: i18n:pack [--mode replace|merge] [--allow-duplicates] bin/magento i18n:pack app/i18n/fr_FR.csv fr_FR # With merge mode (default is replace) bin/magento i18n:pack app/i18n/fr_FR.csv fr_FR --mode merge # Allow duplicate translations bin/magento i18n:pack app/i18n/fr_FR.csv fr_FR --allow-duplicates ``` **What it does:** - Reads the source CSV - Creates/updates the language pack directory structure under `app/i18n/` - Generates `registration.php` and `composer.json` stubs for the language pack > **Exam focus:** > - `i18n:pack` takes **two positional arguments**: `` and `` — NOT flags like `-d` or `-l`. > - Optional flags: `--mode` (`-m`) for replace/merge, `--allow-duplicates` (`-d`). > - Distinct from `i18n:collect-phrases` — collect *finds* strings, pack *packages* them. --- ## 6. Translation in PHP & JS Templates ### 6.1 PHP / PHTML Templates Use the double-underscore helper method `__()`: ```php getStoreName()); } ``` ```php // In a PHTML template — both syntaxes work ``` **Placeholder notation:** - Uses `%1`, `%2`, `%3` (1-indexed), **not** `%s` or `%d` - Arguments are passed as additional parameters to `__()` > **Exam focus:** > - PHP translation function is `__('text')` — **two underscores**. > - Placeholders use `%1`, `%2` notation, not `%s`. > - `__()` is available in Block classes, Helper classes, and PHTML templates. ### 6.2 JavaScript Translation ```javascript // RequireJS module — preferred approach define(['jquery', 'mage/translate'], function ($) { 'use strict'; // Using $.mage.__ directly var message = $.mage.__('Add to Cart'); // With dynamic values (manual replacement) var greeting = $.mage.__('Hello, %1').replace('%1', customerName); }); ``` ```javascript // Using mage/translate module's return value directly // translate.js returns $.mage.__ as its default export require(['mage/translate'], function ($t) { console.log($t('My Account')); }); ``` ```html ``` > **Exam focus:** > - JS translation uses `$.mage.__('text')` — not `__()`. > - Requires the `mage/translate` RequireJS module. > - JS strings have a **separate translation mechanism** (see Section 9). > - The `$.mage.__` is defined as a proxy to `$.mage.translate.translate` in `lib/web/mage/translate.js`. > - `mage/translate` returns `$.mage.__` as its default export, so `$t` in `require(['mage/translate'], function($t) {...})` is just an alias for `$.mage.__`. --- ## 7. Language Packs Language packs are **Composer packages** that provide locale CSV files for multiple modules at once. ### 7.1 Structure of a Language Pack Language packs have CSV files at the **root** of the package directory — NOT in an `i18n/` subdirectory: ``` vendor/ +-- acme/ +-- language-fr-fr/ +-- composer.json +-- language.xml +-- registration.php +-- fr_FR.csv <-- CSV at ROOT level ``` **`language.xml`:** ```xml fr_FR acme language-fr-fr 100 ``` **`registration.php`:** ```php ` tag) A language pack can **inherit** from another pack using the `` element in `language.xml`. Strings not found in the child pack fall through to the parent. ```xml ``` > **Exam focus:** > - Language packs use Composer type `magento2-language`. > - They must include `registration.php` and `language.xml`. > - CSV files go at the **root** of the package directory — the framework searches for `*.csv` at the registered path root. > - The `` tag in `language.xml` enables **pack inheritance**. > - Language packs sit **third** in the priority chain (below theme i18n, above module i18n). > - After installing, run `setup:upgrade` then `setup:static-content:deploy `. --- ## 8. Inline Translation The inline translation tool allows non-developer admins to translate text **directly on the frontend page**. ### 8.1 Enabling Inline Translation **Admin path:** ``` Stores → Configuration → Advanced → Developer → Translate Inline ``` | Setting | Store View Scope | |---------|-----------------| | Enabled for Storefront | Yes / No | | Enabled for Admin | Yes / No | > **Important:** This setting is **store view scoped**. You must select the correct store view in the admin scope switcher before enabling. ### 8.2 How It Works ``` Admin enables Translate Inline | v Frontend pages show [Book icon] on each translatable string | v Admin clicks [Book icon] -> Edit dialog appears | v Admin submits new translation | v Translation saved to `translation` DB table | v All subsequent page loads use DB override (HIGHEST PRIORITY) ``` **Database table:** `translation` ```sql -- Structure of the translation table SELECT * FROM translation; -- Columns: key_id, string, store_id, translate, locale ``` | Column | Description | |--------|-------------| | `string` | The original source string | | `translate` | The overridden translation | | `store_id` | Which store view this applies to | | `locale` | Locale code, e.g. `en_US` | ### 8.3 Clearing Inline Translation Overrides ```bash # Clear the cache after DB changes bin/magento cache:clean translate # Or clear all caches bin/magento cache:flush ``` To remove inline translation overrides, you must either: 1. Delete rows from the `translation` table in the database 2. Use the inline editor to reset strings > **Exam focus:** > - Inline translation is enabled at: **Stores → Configuration → Advanced → Developer → Translate Inline**. > - Overrides are stored in the **`translation` database table**. > - DB translations have the **highest priority** — they override everything including theme i18n. > - This setting is **store view scoped**. > - After using inline translation, clearing the `translate` cache applies changes. --- ## 9. JS Translation Mechanism JavaScript translations have a **completely separate pipeline** from PHP translations. They are bundled into a special JSON file during **Static Content Deployment (SCD)**. ### 9.1 `js-translation.json` ``` pub/static/ +-- frontend/ +-- Vendor/ +-- Theme/ +-- en_US/ +-- js-translation.json <-- Generated during SCD ``` **Example `js-translation.json` content:** ```json { "Add to Cart": "Ajouter au panier", "My Account": "Mon compte", "Search": "Rechercher", "Home Page": "Page d'accueil" } ``` ### 9.2 How JS Translations Are Generated The `mage/translate` module depends on `mageTranslationDictionary`, which is mapped to `Magento_Translation/js/mage-translation-dictionary` in the Magento_Translation module's `requirejs-config.js`. This dictionary module loads `js-translation.json` via RequireJS `text!` plugin. ``` SCD runs: bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy fr_FR | v Magento reads all translation CSVs (module i18n + theme i18n + language packs) | v Generates js-translation.json for each locale/theme combination | v At runtime: mage/translate loads mageTranslationDictionary | v mageTranslationDictionary loads 'text!js-translation.json' | v $.mage.__() looks up strings in the loaded dictionary ``` ### 9.3 Triggering JS Translation Updates ```bash # After modifying any CSV file that contains JS-used strings: bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_US # In developer mode — clear static files and redeploy rm -rf pub/static/frontend/ bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_US -f ``` > **Exam focus:** > - JS translations are stored in `js-translation.json`, **not** in PHP translation CSV directly. > - `js-translation.json` is generated during **Static Content Deployment (SCD)**. > - `$.mage.__('text')` performs runtime lookup against this JSON dictionary. > - Changes to a CSV affecting JS strings require **re-running SCD** to take effect. > - The dictionary constant is defined as `DICTIONARY_FILE_NAME = 'js-translation.json'` in `Magento\Translation\Model\Js\Config`. > - This is the key reason JS strings require a "separate mechanism." --- ## 10. Hands-On: Add a Custom Phrase to a Theme i18n CSV ### Step 1: Identify the Source String Locate the source string in a PHTML template: ```php ``` Or add a custom string to your own template: ```php

``` ### Step 2: Create or Edit the Theme i18n CSV ```bash # Create the i18n directory if it doesn't exist mkdir -p app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/i18n/ # Create or edit the CSV file nano app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/i18n/en_US.csv ``` **`app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/i18n/en_US.csv`:** ```csv "Add to Cart","Shop Now" "Welcome to our exclusive store","Welcome to the ACME Premium Store" "Discover amazing products at unbeatable prices","Find your perfect product today" "My Account","My Profile" "Sign In","Login" ``` ### Step 3: (Optional) Collect Phrases First with CLI ```bash # Scan your theme for all translatable strings bin/magento i18n:collect-phrases \ -o app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/i18n/en_US.csv \ app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme # Review the generated file — both columns will have source strings # Edit the right column (second value) with your translations ``` ### Step 4: Clear the Translation Cache ```bash # Clear the translation cache specifically bin/magento cache:clean translate # Or flush everything bin/magento cache:flush # In developer mode — also clear generated view files bin/magento cache:clean ``` ### Step 5: Redeploy Static Content (if needed) ```bash # Required if any strings are used in JS files bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_US -f # In developer mode, this step is usually not required for PHP translations ``` ### Step 6: Verify on Frontend 1. Open browser → Navigate to the page containing the template 2. Confirm `"Add to Cart"` now reads `"Shop Now"` 3. Confirm custom strings appear correctly **Troubleshooting verification:** ```bash # Check the CSV is in the right place ls -la app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/i18n/ # Confirm no syntax errors (mismatched quotes) php -r " \$rows = array_map('str_getcsv', file('app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/i18n/en_US.csv')); foreach (\$rows as \$i => \$row) { if (count(\$row) !== 2) echo 'Error on line ' . (\$i+1) . PHP_EOL; } echo 'Validation complete' . PHP_EOL; " # Confirm cache is cleared bin/magento cache:status ``` > **Exam focus:** > - Theme i18n CSV path: `app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/i18n/LL_CC.csv` > - After editing CSV, must clear the `translate` cache: `bin/magento cache:clean translate` > - In developer mode, PHP translation changes are visible after cache clear without SCD. > - JS translation changes always require SCD re-run regardless of mode. --- ### Complete Flow Diagram ``` Developer adds __('Custom Phrase') to PHTML template | v Create/edit: app/design/frontend/V/T/i18n/en_US.csv Add line: "Custom Phrase","My Custom Translation" | v bin/magento cache:clean translate | v Browse frontend -> "My Custom Translation" appears | v (if JS string) bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_US | v JS strings updated in js-translation.json ``` --- ## Quick-Reference Checklist ### CSV Format - [ ] Format: `"Original English phrase","Translated phrase"` — two double-quoted columns per line - [ ] File name must be locale code: `LL_CC.csv` (e.g. `en_US.csv`, `fr_FR.csv`) - [ ] Encoding: UTF-8 without BOM - [ ] Internal double quotes escaped by doubling: `"Say ""Hello"""` - [ ] Case-sensitive: `"Add to Cart"` ≠ `"add to cart"` ### File Locations - [ ] Module translations: `app/code/Vendor/Module/i18n/LL_CC.csv` - [ ] Theme translations: `app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/i18n/LL_CC.csv` - [ ] Language pack translations: `vendor/*/LL_CC.csv` (at package root, NOT in `i18n/`) - [ ] DB overrides: stored in `translation` database table ### Priority Chain (highest to lowest) - [ ] **1st — DB** (Admin inline translation, stored in `translation` table) - [ ] **2nd — Theme i18n/** (`app/design/frontend/V/T/i18n/LL_CC.csv`) - [ ] **3rd — Language Pack** (`vendor/*/LL_CC.csv`) - [ ] **4th — Module i18n/** (`app/code/V/M/i18n/LL_CC.csv`) - [ ] **Fallback** — original source string returned if no match found - [ ] Load order in code: Module → Pack → Theme → DB (each overwrites previous, so DB wins) ### CLI Commands - [ ] `bin/magento i18n:collect-phrases -o ` — scans PHP/PHTML/JS/XML for `__()` calls - [ ] `bin/magento i18n:collect-phrases --magento -o ` — scan entire Magento installation - [ ] `bin/magento i18n:pack ` — package CSV into language pack (positional args, NOT flags) - [ ] `bin/magento i18n:pack` optional flags: `--mode` (`-m`) replace/merge, `--allow-duplicates` (`-d`) - [ ] `bin/magento cache:clean translate` — clear translation cache after CSV edits - [ ] `bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy ` — regenerate `js-translation.json` ### PHP Translation - [ ] `__('text')` — double underscore, used in PHP classes and PHTML templates - [ ] `__('Hello %1', $name)` — placeholders use `%1`, `%2` (1-indexed), not `%s` - [ ] Available in Block classes, Helpers, and PHTML templates ### JS Translation - [ ] `$.mage.__('text')` — used in JavaScript files - [ ] Requires `mage/translate` RequireJS module (which depends on `mageTranslationDictionary`) - [ ] `mage/translate` returns `$.mage.__` as default export — so `$t` alias works via `require(['mage/translate'], function($t) {...})` - [ ] Strings compiled into `js-translation.json` during SCD - [ ] `js-translation.json` location: `pub/static/frontend/V/T/LL_CC/js-translation.json` - [ ] JS translation changes require re-running `setup:static-content:deploy` ### Language Packs - [ ] Installed via Composer — `composer require vendor/language-pack` - [ ] Composer type: `magento2-language` - [ ] Must contain: `registration.php`, `language.xml`, and `LL_CC.csv` files **at package root** - [ ] CSV files are NOT in an `i18n/` subdirectory — `readPackCsv()` searches `*.csv` at root - [ ] `language.xml` `` tag enables pack inheritance - [ ] After install: run `setup:upgrade` then `setup:static-content:deploy ` ### Inline Translation - [ ] Enable at: **Stores → Configuration → Advanced → Developer → Translate Inline** - [ ] Setting is **store view scoped** - [ ] Overrides stored in the **`translation` database table** — highest priority - [ ] After enabling, book icons appear on frontend for each translatable string - [ ] Clear with: `bin/magento cache:clean translate` ### Key Distinctions for Exam - [ ] Theme `i18n/` **overrides** module `i18n/` but is **below** DB overrides - [ ] Missing translation falls back silently — no error thrown - [ ] JS and PHP translations use **different mechanisms** (`js-translation.json` vs CSV lookup) - [ ] `i18n:collect-phrases` **finds** strings; `i18n:pack` **packages** them - [ ] Inline translation editor writes to **DB**, not to any CSV file - [ ] SCD must be re-run after any changes that affect JS translation strings

flashcards.question: What is the translation priority chain in Magento 2, from highest to lowest?
flashcards.answer: The priority chain from highest to lowest is: 1) Database (Admin inline translation stored in the 'translation' table), 2) Theme i18n/ CSV, 3) Language Pack CSV, 4) Module i18n/ CSV. If no match is found at any level, the original source string is returned as-is. The load order in code is Module -> Pack -> Theme -> DB, but since each overwrites previous values, the effective priority is reversed.
flashcards.hint: The last one loaded wins. Think about which source is loaded last in the code to understand why it has the highest priority.

flashcards.question: What is the correct CSV format for Magento 2 translation files?
flashcards.answer: Translation CSV files use exactly two double-quoted columns per line: "Original English phrase","Translated phrase". The file must be UTF-8 encoded without BOM, the filename must match the locale code exactly (e.g., en_US.csv, fr_FR.csv), and translations are case-sensitive. Internal double quotes are escaped by doubling them (e.g., "Say ""Hello""").
flashcards.hint: Think about encoding, quoting rules, and how the filename relates to the locale.

flashcards.question: How does the PHP translation function work in Magento 2, and what placeholder notation does it use?
flashcards.answer: The PHP translation function is __() (two underscores). It uses %1, %2, %3 notation (1-indexed) for placeholders, NOT %s or %d. Arguments are passed as additional parameters: __('Hello, %1!', $customerName). It is available in Block classes, Helper classes, and PHTML templates.
flashcards.hint: The function name is very short (just two characters), and placeholders use numbers, not format specifiers.

flashcards.question: How does JavaScript translation work differently from PHP translation in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: JS translation uses $.mage.__('text') instead of __(), and requires the mage/translate RequireJS module. JS translations are compiled into a separate js-translation.json file during Static Content Deployment (SCD), not read from CSV directly at runtime. Changes to CSV files affecting JS strings require re-running SCD to regenerate js-translation.json.
flashcards.hint: JS has its own translation function, its own dictionary file format, and requires a build step to update.

flashcards.question: Where do language pack CSV files live, and how does this differ from module and theme translation files?
flashcards.answer: Language pack CSV files live at the root of the package directory (e.g., vendor/acme/language-fr-fr/fr_FR.csv), NOT in an i18n/ subdirectory. This is different from module translations (app/code/Vendor/Module/i18n/LL_CC.csv) and theme translations (app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/i18n/LL_CC.csv), which both use an i18n/ subdirectory.
flashcards.hint: Language packs place their CSV files differently than modules and themes — at the package root level.

flashcards.question: What are the three required files in a Magento 2 language pack, and what Composer type must it use?
flashcards.answer: A language pack must contain: 1) registration.php (registers the component with ComponentRegistrar::LANGUAGE), 2) language.xml (declares locale code, vendor, package, sort order, and optional inheritance via <use> tag), and 3) the locale CSV file (e.g., fr_FR.csv) at the package root. The Composer type must be 'magento2-language'.
flashcards.hint: Similar to themes, language packs need registration and declaration files, plus their translation data.

flashcards.question: What CLI command collects all translatable strings from a Magento codebase, and what does it scan?
flashcards.answer: The command is bin/magento i18n:collect-phrases -o <output_file> <directory>. It scans PHP files for __('text'), PHTML templates for __('text'), JavaScript files for $.mage.__('text'), and XML layout files for translate="true" attributes. The output is a CSV with the source string in both columns. Use --magento/-m flag to scan the entire installation instead of specifying a directory.
flashcards.hint: This command extracts phrases from four different file types across the codebase.

flashcards.question: Where is inline translation enabled in the Magento Admin, and where are the overrides stored?
flashcards.answer: Inline translation is enabled at Stores > Configuration > Advanced > Developer > Translate Inline. This setting is store view scoped, so you must select the correct store view before enabling. Overrides are stored in the 'translation' database table (not in any CSV file) and have the highest priority in the translation chain, overriding all file-based translations.
flashcards.hint: It's under the Developer section of configuration, and its storage mechanism is different from file-based translations.

flashcards.question: What is js-translation.json, where is it located, and when is it generated?
flashcards.answer: js-translation.json is a JSON dictionary file containing all translated strings used by JavaScript. It's located at pub/static/frontend/Vendor/Theme/locale/js-translation.json. It is generated during Static Content Deployment (SCD) by reading all translation CSVs. At runtime, the mage/translate module loads this dictionary, and $.mage.__() performs lookups against it.
flashcards.hint: This file bridges the gap between CSV-based translations and JavaScript's runtime needs.

flashcards.question: What cache must be cleared after editing a theme i18n CSV file, and what additional step is needed for JS strings?
flashcards.answer: After editing a theme i18n CSV, you must clear the translation cache with bin/magento cache:clean translate. For PHP translations in developer mode, this is sufficient. However, if any modified strings are used in JavaScript files, you must also re-run setup:static-content:deploy to regenerate js-translation.json, regardless of the deployment mode.
flashcards.hint: There are two types of cache clearing needed — one for server-side translations and an additional build step for client-side translations.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between i18n:collect-phrases and i18n:pack CLI commands?
flashcards.answer: i18n:collect-phrases scans the codebase and extracts all translatable strings into a CSV file (finding strings). i18n:pack takes an existing translation CSV and packages it into a language pack directory structure with registration.php and composer.json stubs. They serve complementary purposes: collect finds strings to translate, pack organizes completed translations for distribution.
flashcards.hint: One discovers what needs translating, the other structures completed translations for deployment.

flashcards.question: How does the mage/translate RequireJS module make translations available to JavaScript code?
flashcards.answer: The mage/translate module depends on mageTranslationDictionary, which is mapped to Magento_Translation/js/mage-translation-dictionary in the Magento_Translation module's requirejs-config.js. This dictionary module loads js-translation.json via the RequireJS text! plugin. The module returns $.mage.__ as its default export, so you can alias it (e.g., $t) when using require(['mage/translate'], function($t) {...}).
flashcards.hint: It works through a chain: a RequireJS module loads a dictionary, which in turn loads a JSON file generated during deployment.

flashcards.question: How does the <use> tag work in a language pack's language.xml?
flashcards.answer: The <use> tag enables language pack inheritance, allowing a child language pack to fall back to a parent pack for strings it doesn't define. The syntax is <use vendor="magento" package="language-fr-fr"/>. Strings not found in the child pack automatically fall through to the parent pack, avoiding the need to duplicate all translations.
flashcards.hint: Similar to theme inheritance, language packs can inherit from other packs for missing translations.

flashcards.question: Why does the effective translation priority appear reversed from the code load order?
flashcards.answer: In Translate::loadData(), translations are loaded in order: Module -> Pack -> Theme -> DB. Each subsequent call overwrites previous values for the same key, so the last one loaded wins. Since DB translations are loaded last, they have the highest effective priority. This overwrite mechanism is why the effective priority (DB > Theme > Pack > Module) is the reverse of the load order.
flashcards.hint: Think about what happens when you assign a variable multiple times — the last assignment is what sticks.
