studyNotes.content:
# Layout XML Fundamentals — Magento 2 Certified Study Notes --- ## Table of Contents 1. [Overview & Why Layout XML Matters](#1-overview--why-layout-xml-matters) 2. [File Locations & Load Order](#2-file-locations--load-order) 3. [Layout Handles Reference](#3-layout-handles-reference) 4. [Core Layout Instructions](#4-core-layout-instructions) - [block](#41-block) - [container](#42-container) - [referenceBlock](#43-referenceblock) - [referenceContainer](#44-referencecontainer) - [move](#45-move) - [remove](#46-remove) - [update handle](#47-update-handle) 5. [Page Layout Declarations](#5-page-layout-declarations) 6. [Tricky Behaviours & Gotchas](#6-tricky-behaviours--gotchas) 7. [Hands-On: Add a Custom Block to catalog_product_view](#7-hands-on-add-a-custom-block-to-catalog_product_view) 8. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist) --- ## 1. Overview & Why Layout XML Matters Magento 2 uses a **declarative XML-based layout system** to define the page structure without requiring PHP code changes. Instead of overriding controllers or block classes, developers compose pages by merging XML files that describe *what blocks and containers exist*, *where they live in the page tree*, and *which templates render them*. ``` Request lifecycle (simplified) +-------------------+ +----------------------+ +------------------+ | Router/Controller| --> | Layout XML Processor| --> | Rendered HTML | | fires handle(s) | | merges all files | | (Block tree -> | | e.g. catalog_ | | matching handles | | .phtml output) | | product_view | +----------------------+ +------------------+ +-------------------+ ``` Key properties of the layout system: - **Non-destructive by default** — module layout files are *merged*, not replaced - **Theme-level overrides win** — theme files are merged *after* module files - **Handle-scoped** — instructions only apply on pages where the named handle is active --- ## 2. File Locations & Load Order ### 2.1 Module Layout Directory ``` app/code/Vendor/Module/ view/ frontend/ layout/ default.xml catalog_product_view.xml ... adminhtml/ layout/ ... ``` ### 2.2 Theme Layout Directory ``` app/design/frontend/Vendor/theme/ Magento_Catalog/ layout/ catalog_product_view.xml <-- overrides/extends Magento_Catalog module file Magento_Cms/ layout/ cms_page_view.xml ``` > **Note:** In a theme, layout files are placed under a folder named after the *originating module* (e.g., `Magento_Catalog/layout/`), NOT under a generic `layout/` folder directly. ### 2.3 Merge Order (lowest → highest priority) ``` 1. Magento core module layouts 2. Third-party module layouts 3. Custom module layouts (app/code/...) 4. Parent theme layouts 5. Active child theme layouts <-- WINS on conflict ``` **Exam focus:** - Theme layout files are stored under `/Magento_Module/layout/`, **not** `/layout/` - Module layout files live at `view/frontend/layout/` - Theme files are processed *after* module files — theme changes always win --- ## 3. Layout Handles Reference A **layout handle** is a string identifier. When Magento processes a page, it collects all active handles and merges every XML file whose filename matches a handle name. | Handle | Triggered On | |---|---| | `default` | **Every page** in the storefront | | `catalog_product_view` | All Product Detail Pages (PDPs) | | `catalog_category_view` | All Category Listing Pages (CLPs) | | `cms_page_view` | Any CMS page | | `cms_index_index` | Homepage (CMS home page specifically) | | `customer_account_login` | Customer login page | | `checkout_cart_index` | Shopping cart page | | `checkout_index_index` | One-page checkout | ### 3.1 How Handles Stack On a product page, **multiple handles are active simultaneously**: ``` Active handles on a PDP: - default - catalog_product_view - catalog_product_view_type_simple (for simple products) - catalog_product_view_id_42 (product-specific handle) ``` All matching XML files are merged together for that request. **Exam focus:** - `default.xml` instructions apply to **every single page** - `cms_index_index` is the *homepage* handle — distinct from `cms_page_view` - Multiple handles are active per request; their layout files are all merged --- ## 4. Core Layout Instructions ### 4.1 `` Defines a **PHP block object** that renders a `.phtml` template. ```xml value ``` | Attribute | Description | |---|---| | `class` | Fully-qualified PHP block class | | `name` | **Unique identifier** within the layout — must be unique | | `template` | `Module::path/to/file.phtml` format | | `before` | Position: `-` = first, or name of block to appear before | | `after` | Position: `-` = last, or name of block to appear after | | `cacheable` | `true` (default) or `false` — if `false`, disables full-page cache for the **entire page** | | `as` | Alias used when calling `getChildHtml('alias')` | | `ifconfig` | Config path — block only renders if the config value is truthy | > **Warning on `cacheable="false"`:** Setting this on *any* block on a page disables FPC for that **entire page**, not just the block. > **Note:** `` does NOT have a `display` attribute. The `display` attribute is only available on `` and ``. To hide a block after it's been defined, use ``. **Exam focus:** - `name` must be **unique** across the entire merged layout for a request - Duplicate block names → **last declaration wins** (the earlier one is discarded) - `cacheable="false"` affects the **whole page's** FPC eligibility - `before="-"` means *first*, `after="-"` means *last* --- ### 4.2 `` A **structural wrapper** that renders no content itself — only wraps its children in an HTML element. ```xml ``` | Attribute | Description | |---|---| | `name` | Unique identifier | | `htmlTag` | HTML element: `div`, `section`, `article`, `aside`, `ul`, `ol`, `nav`, `header`, `footer`, `table`, `tfoot`, `h1`–`h6`, and more | | `htmlClass` | CSS class string applied to `htmlTag` | | `htmlId` | HTML `id` attribute | | `label` | Admin/developer label (not rendered in HTML) | > **Note:** A container with no `htmlTag` renders **no wrapping HTML** — it acts as a purely logical grouping node. **Exam focus:** - Containers produce no content — they only render their children (optionally wrapped in `htmlTag`) - `label` is for developer reference only — not output in HTML - A key real-world example: `product.info.main` is a `` (not a block) with `htmlTag="div"` and `htmlClass="product-info-main"` — defined in `catalog_product_view.xml` --- ### 4.3 `` Modifies an **existing block** that was already declared (in the same or another layout file). ```xml true ``` **Common uses:** - Adding child blocks to an existing parent - Changing arguments/data on an existing block - Setting `display="false"` to hide an existing block - Setting `remove="true"` to remove an existing block **Exam focus:** - `` **modifies** an existing block — it does not create a new one - If the referenced block does not exist, the instruction is silently ignored - `display` and `remove` attributes are ONLY available on `` (and ``), NOT on `` --- ### 4.4 `` Same concept as ``, but targets a **container**. ```xml ``` **Exam focus:** - `` is one of the most common patterns — it adds blocks inside the main content area - You cannot use `` to reference a ``, and vice-versa — the type must match --- ### 4.5 `` Relocates an existing block or container to a **different parent** in the layout tree. ```xml ``` | Attribute | Description | |---|---| | `element` | Name of the block/container to move (required) | | `destination` | Name of the new parent container/block (required) | | `before` | Positioning within the new parent (optional) | | `after` | Positioning within the new parent (optional) | | `as` | Optional new alias in the new parent (the XSD attribute name is `as`, not `alias`) | **Exam focus:** - `` changes the **parent** of an element — it does not duplicate it - Both `element` and `destination` must exist in the layout --- ### 4.6 `` **Permanently removes** a block or container from the layout for that request. ```xml ``` > **Critical gotcha:** `` is **irreversible within the same request**. Once removed, no subsequent `` or `` with the same name can bring it back. The removed element is gone for that page render. **Exam focus:** - `` is **permanent for the request** — cannot be undone - To conditionally hide something, use `display="false"` on a `` instead - `` takes only a `name` attribute - Alternative: `` achieves similar removal --- ### 4.7 `` **Imports** all layout instructions from another handle into the current handle's scope. ```xml ``` This merges every instruction from the `catalog_product_view_type_configurable` handle as if it were written inline. **Real-world use:** ```xml ``` ```xml ``` **Exam focus:** - `` **includes** another handle's instructions — it's a layout include/import - The included handle's XML is processed as if it were part of the current file - This is how Magento shares layout logic across multiple page types --- ## 5. Page Layout Declarations The **page layout** defines the top-level column structure of a page. It is declared in the `` root element's `layout` attribute. ### 5.1 Available Page Layouts Core page layouts registered by `Magento_Theme` (in `view/base/layouts.xml` and `view/frontend/layouts.xml`): | Layout ID | Description | |---|---| | `empty` | No columns, no header/footer — used for iframes, popups | | `1column` | Single full-width content column | | `2columns-left` | Two columns, sidebar on the **left** | | `2columns-right` | Two columns, sidebar on the **right** | | `3columns` | Three columns (left sidebar, content, right sidebar) | Page Builder module adds additional layouts (in `Magento_PageBuilder/view/frontend/layouts.xml`): | Layout ID | Description | |---|---| | `cms-full-width` | Full-width for CMS pages | | `category-full-width` | Full-width for category pages | | `product-full-width` | Full-width for product pages | > **Note:** There is NO generic `full-width` layout. The full-width layouts are Page Builder specific and scoped by entity type (`cms-full-width`, `category-full-width`, `product-full-width`). ### 5.2 Declaring Page Layout in XML **Method 1: In the page XML root element** ```xml ``` ### 5.3 Custom Page Layout Registration To register a custom page layout, create `view/frontend/layouts.xml`: ```xml ``` Then create the corresponding page_layout XML file at `view/frontend/page_layout/custom-layout.xml`. **Exam focus:** - `empty` is used for standalone pages (no header/footer/columns) - There is no generic `full-width` — Page Builder provides `cms-full-width`, `category-full-width`, `product-full-width` - Page layout is set via the `layout` attribute on the `` root tag - The `layouts.xml` XSD is `urn:magento:framework:View/PageLayout/etc/layouts.xsd` (note: `PageLayout`, not `Layout`) --- ## 6. Tricky Behaviours & Gotchas ### 6.1 `` is Permanent ``` Timeline within a single request: File A (module): --> foo exists File B (theme): --> foo GONE permanently File C (module): --> SILENTLY IGNORED ... ``` **Solution:** If you need *conditional* hiding, use: ```xml ``` This hides the block from rendering but keeps it in the layout tree, so it can be re-enabled. --- ### 6.2 Duplicate Block Names — Last One Wins ```xml ``` **Exam focus:** - Duplicate `name` attributes across merged layout files → **last one processed wins** - Theme files are processed last → theme's block definition wins over module's --- ### 6.3 `display="false"` vs `` | Feature | `display="false"` | `` | |---|---|---| | Block stays in layout tree | Yes | No | | Can be re-enabled later | Yes | No | | Template is rendered | No | No (block gone) | | `getChildHtml()` returns | Empty string | Empty string | | Reversible | Yes | **No** | | Available on | ``, `` | Standalone `` element | --- ### 6.4 `cacheable="false"` Scope ``` Page: catalog_product_view Blocks on this page: - product.info.main (container, no cacheable attr) - product.info.price cacheable (default) - vendor.custom.block cacheable="false" <-- DISABLES FPC FOR ENTIRE PAGE ``` > Even if only **one block** on a page has `cacheable="false"`, the **entire page** is excluded from Full Page Cache. Use this attribute with extreme caution. **Exam focus:** - `cacheable="false"` disables FPC for the **whole page**, not just the block - Alternative: use **Varnish ESI** or **private content (sections API)** for per-user dynamic data --- ### 6.5 Block `before` / `after` Attribute Values | Value | Meaning | |---|---| | `-` | Extreme position: `-` on `before` = **first**; `-` on `after` = **last** | | `blockName` | Position relative to the named sibling | | *(omitted)* | Position is unspecified (layout engine decides) | ```xml ``` --- ## 7. Hands-On: Add a Custom Block to catalog_product_view ### Objective Add a custom promotional banner block below the product price on all PDPs using a **theme layout override**. ### Step 1: Create the Theme Layout File ```bash # Directory structure app/design/frontend/Vendor/MyTheme/ Magento_Catalog/ layout/ catalog_product_view.xml templates/ product/ promo_banner.phtml ``` ### Step 2: Write the Layout XML **File:** `app/design/frontend/Vendor/MyTheme/Magento_Catalog/layout/catalog_product_view.xml` ```xml Free shipping on orders over $50! ``` ### Step 3: Create the Template File **File:** `app/design/frontend/Vendor/MyTheme/Magento_Catalog/templates/product/promo_banner.phtml` ```php getData('promo_text'); ?>

escapeHtml($promoText) ?>

``` > **Security note:** Always use `$block->escapeHtml()` for string output. Never echo raw data. ### Step 4: Flush Cache and Verify ```bash # Flush Magento caches (layout is a valid cache type) bin/magento cache:flush layout block_html full_page # Enable template hints for debugging (CLI command): bin/magento dev:template-hints:enable bin/magento cache:flush full_page # Force static content deploy (if needed in production) bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -f ``` ### Step 5: Verification 1. Navigate to any PDP in your browser 2. Use browser DevTools → Inspect the area below the product price 3. You should see: ```html

Free shipping on orders over $50!

``` 4. Confirm it does **not** appear on category pages (CLP) — it's scoped to `catalog_product_view` ### Step 6: Alternative — Using a Custom Module (not a theme) If placing this in a **module** instead of a theme: **File:** `app/code/Vendor/Module/view/frontend/layout/catalog_product_view.xml` ```xml ``` ```bash # Enable the module if new bin/magento module:enable Vendor_Module bin/magento setup:upgrade bin/magento cache:flush ``` ### Debugging Tips ```bash # Enable template hints via CLI: bin/magento dev:template-hints:enable bin/magento cache:flush full_page # Disable when done: bin/magento dev:template-hints:disable bin/magento cache:flush full_page # Or enable via admin: # Stores > Config > Advanced > Developer > Debug > Template Path Hints ``` **Exam focus:** - Theme layout files go in `/Magento_Catalog/layout/catalog_product_view.xml` — note the module namespace folder - `product.info.main` is a **container** (not a block) — use `` to add children to it - Use `Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template` as the block class when no custom PHP logic is needed - Always use `$block->escapeHtml()` in templates - Flush `layout`, `block_html`, and `full_page` cache after layout XML changes --- ## Quick-Reference Checklist ### File Locations - [ ] Module layout files: `app/code/Vendor/Module/view/frontend/layout/` - [ ] Theme layout files: `app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/Magento_Module/layout/` - [ ] Theme layout folder is named after the **originating module**, not a generic `layout/` root - [ ] Theme files merge **after** module files — theme always wins on conflict ### Layout Handles - [ ] `default` — fires on **every page** - [ ] `catalog_product_view` — all PDPs - [ ] `catalog_category_view` — all category pages - [ ] `cms_page_view` — any CMS page - [ ] `cms_index_index` — homepage only - [ ] `customer_account_login` — login page - [ ] `checkout_cart_index` — cart page - [ ] `checkout_index_index` — checkout page - [ ] Multiple handles are active per request; all matching files are merged ### Instructions - [ ] `` — creates a block; requires unique `name`; has `class`, `template`, `before`, `after`, `cacheable`, `as`, `ifconfig` - [ ] `` — structural wrapper; renders `htmlTag` wrapping its children; no content of its own - [ ] `` — modifies an existing block; silently ignored if block doesn't exist; has `display` and `remove` attributes - [ ] `` — modifies an existing container; also has `display` and `remove` attributes - [ ] `` — relocates a block/container to a new parent; optional `as`, `before`, `after` - [ ] `` — permanently removes a block for that request; **irreversible** - [ ] `` — imports/includes another handle's layout instructions ### Critical Gotchas - [ ] `` is **permanent** for the request — cannot re-add the block afterward - [ ] Use `display="false"` on `` for reversible/conditional hiding - [ ] `display` attribute is ONLY on `` and ``, NOT on `` or `` - [ ] Duplicate block `name` values → **last definition processed wins** - [ ] `cacheable="false"` on **any** block disables FPC for the **entire page** - [ ] `before="-"` = first position; `after="-"` = last position ### Page Layouts - [ ] `empty` — no header/footer/columns (popups, iframes) — registered in `view/base/layouts.xml` - [ ] `1column` — single content column - [ ] `2columns-left` — left sidebar + content - [ ] `2columns-right` — content + right sidebar - [ ] `3columns` — left sidebar + content + right sidebar - [ ] No generic `full-width` — Page Builder provides `cms-full-width`, `category-full-width`, `product-full-width` - [ ] Set via `layout=""` attribute on the `` root element - [ ] Custom layouts registered in `view/frontend/layouts.xml` with XSD `urn:magento:framework:View/PageLayout/etc/layouts.xsd` ### Block Attributes (from XSD `blockType`) - [ ] `name` — unique identifier; duplicate = last wins - [ ] `class` — PHP block class - [ ] `template` — `Module::path/template.phtml` format - [ ] `before` / `after` — sibling ordering (`-` = extreme position) - [ ] `cacheable` — `true` (default) or `false`; disables FPC for the whole page - [ ] `as` — alias for `getChildHtml('alias')` calls - [ ] `ifconfig` — config path; block renders only if config value is truthy ### referenceBlock Attributes (from XSD `blockReferenceType`) - [ ] `name` — required; the block to reference - [ ] `display` — `true` (default) or `false`; hides without removing - [ ] `remove` — `true` removes the block from the layout tree - [ ] `template` — override the block's template - [ ] `class` — override the block's PHP class ### Container Attributes (from XSD `containerType`) - [ ] `name` — unique identifier - [ ] `htmlTag` — wrapping HTML element (optional) - [ ] `htmlClass` — CSS classes on `htmlTag` - [ ] `htmlId` — HTML id on `htmlTag` - [ ] `label` — developer label only, not rendered ### Move Attributes (from XSD `moveType`) - [ ] `element` — required; name of block/container to move - [ ] `destination` — required; name of new parent - [ ] `as` — optional; new alias (NOT `alias`) - [ ] `before` / `after` — optional; positioning in new parent ### Hands-On Verification - [ ] Layout XML changes require flushing: `layout`, `block_html`, `full_page` caches - [ ] `bin/magento dev:template-hints:enable` — enable template path hints via CLI - [ ] `bin/magento dev:template-hints:disable` — disable template hints - [ ] `product.info.main` is a **container** — use ``, not `` - [ ] `Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template` = base block class when no custom logic needed - [ ] Always escape output in templates: `$block->escapeHtml()`, `$block->escapeUrl()`, etc.

flashcards.question: What is the default.xml layout handle and when does it apply?
flashcards.answer: The default.xml layout handle applies to every single page in the storefront. It defines the foundational structure that all other page handles build upon, including global elements like header, footer, breadcrumbs, and scripts. Any block added to default.xml will appear on all pages. It is the base handle that is always active regardless of which page is being viewed.
flashcards.hint: This handle has the broadest scope of all layout handles — it's not page-specific.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between <block> and <container> in Magento 2 layout XML?
flashcards.answer: A <block> defines a PHP block object that renders a .phtml template and produces content. A <container> is a structural wrapper that renders no content itself — it only wraps its children in an optional HTML element (via htmlTag attribute). Containers with no htmlTag act as purely logical grouping nodes. Blocks require a class and template, while containers define structure.
flashcards.hint: One produces HTML output through PHP and templates, the other only provides structural wrapping.

flashcards.question: What happens when cacheable="false" is set on any block on a page?
flashcards.answer: Setting cacheable="false" on any single block on a page disables Full Page Cache (FPC) for the entire page, not just that block. Even if only one block out of many has this attribute, the whole page is excluded from FPC. This should be used with extreme caution. Alternatives include Varnish ESI or the private content (sections) API for per-user dynamic data.
flashcards.hint: The impact is much broader than you might expect — it affects the entire page's cacheability.

flashcards.question: What does <referenceBlock> do, and what happens if the referenced block does not exist?
flashcards.answer: <referenceBlock> modifies an existing block that was already declared in the same or another layout file. It can add child blocks, change arguments, set display="false" to hide the block, or set remove="true" to remove it. If the referenced block does not exist, the instruction is silently ignored — no error is thrown.
flashcards.hint: This instruction targets blocks that already exist — it doesn't create new ones.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between <remove> and display="false" in layout XML?
flashcards.answer: <remove name="block.name"/> permanently removes a block from the layout for that request — it's irreversible and the block cannot be re-added. Setting display="false" on a <referenceBlock> hides the block from rendering but keeps it in the layout tree, so it can be re-enabled. Both result in getChildHtml() returning an empty string, but only display="false" is reversible.
flashcards.hint: One is permanent and destructive, the other is a soft toggle that preserves the block in the tree.

flashcards.question: What are the five core page layouts available in Magento 2, and which additional layouts does Page Builder add?
flashcards.answer: The five core layouts are: empty (no header/footer), 1column, 2columns-left, 2columns-right, and 3columns. Page Builder adds cms-full-width, category-full-width, and product-full-width. There is no generic 'full-width' layout — the full-width layouts are Page Builder specific and scoped by entity type. Page layout is set via the layout attribute on the <page> root element.
flashcards.hint: The core layouts define column structures, and the full-width variants are module-specific, not generic.

flashcards.question: What values do before="-" and after="-" set on a block in layout XML?
flashcards.answer: Setting before="-" positions the block first among its siblings in the parent container. Setting after="-" positions the block last among its siblings. You can also use a block name (e.g., after="product.price.final") to position relative to a specific sibling. If both before and after are omitted, the position is unspecified and determined by the layout engine.
flashcards.hint: The dash character has special meaning for extreme positioning within a container.

flashcards.question: Where do theme layout files go, and how does this differ from module layout file locations?
flashcards.answer: Theme layout files go in <theme>/Magento_Module/layout/ (e.g., app/design/frontend/Vendor/theme/Magento_Catalog/layout/catalog_product_view.xml). They are placed under a folder named after the originating module. Module layout files live at app/code/Vendor/Module/view/frontend/layout/. Theme files are processed after module files, so theme changes always take precedence.
flashcards.hint: Theme layout files need a module-namespace folder prefix, while module files use the view/frontend path.

flashcards.question: What does the <update handle=""> instruction do in layout XML?
flashcards.answer: The <update handle=""> instruction imports all layout instructions from another handle into the current handle's scope. It merges every instruction from the specified handle as if it were written inline. This is how Magento shares layout logic across multiple page types — for example, <update handle="catalog_product_view_type_configurable"/> includes configurable product-specific layout instructions.
flashcards.hint: Think of it as an include or import statement for layout XML instructions.

flashcards.question: What happens when two blocks with the same name attribute appear in merged layout files?
flashcards.answer: When duplicate block names exist across merged layout files, the last declaration processed wins and the earlier one is discarded. Since theme files are processed after module files, a block defined in a theme with the same name as a module block will replace the module's block definition entirely. Block names must be unique across the entire merged layout for a request.
flashcards.hint: Magento processes files in a specific order, and the last definition is the one that takes effect.

flashcards.question: Which layout handles are active simultaneously on a product detail page (PDP)?
flashcards.answer: On a PDP, multiple handles are active at the same time: default (every page), catalog_product_view (all PDPs), catalog_product_view_type_simple (for simple products, or the relevant product type handle), and catalog_product_view_id_42 (product-specific handle with the product's ID). All matching XML files for these handles are merged together for that request.
flashcards.hint: A single page request activates the global handle, the page-type handle, the product-type handle, and an ID-specific handle.

flashcards.question: What is the <move> instruction used for in layout XML, and what are its required attributes?
flashcards.answer: The <move> instruction relocates an existing block or container to a different parent in the layout tree. It has two required attributes: element (name of the block/container to move) and destination (name of the new parent). Optional attributes include before, after (positioning), and as (new alias). The move changes the parent — it does not duplicate the element.
flashcards.hint: This instruction changes where an element lives in the page hierarchy without creating copies.

flashcards.question: What block attributes are only available on <referenceBlock> and NOT on <block>?
flashcards.answer: The display and remove attributes are only available on <referenceBlock> (and <referenceContainer>), NOT on the initial <block> or <container> declaration. To hide a block after it's been defined, you must use <referenceBlock name="..." display="false"/>. The <block> element supports name, class, template, before, after, cacheable, as, and ifconfig — but not display or remove.
flashcards.hint: These control attributes that modify existing elements are specific to the reference instructions.

flashcards.question: What caches need to be flushed after making layout XML changes?
flashcards.answer: After layout XML changes, you should flush the layout, block_html, and full_page caches using: bin/magento cache:flush layout block_html full_page. The layout cache stores the parsed layout XML tree, block_html stores rendered block fragments, and full_page stores assembled complete pages. All three need clearing to ensure layout changes take effect.
flashcards.hint: Three specific cache types are affected by layout changes — the layout structure, rendered fragments, and complete pages.

studyNotes.title: Day 4 — Layout XML Advanced: Extending vs Overriding
studyNotes.content:
# Layout XML Advanced: Extending vs Overriding
## Magento 2 Frontend Certification Study Notes

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Core Concepts Overview](#1-core-concepts-overview)
2. [Extending Layout Files](#2-extending-layout-files)
3. [Overriding Layout Files](#3-overriding-layout-files)
4. [Page Layout Overrides](#4-page-layout-overrides)
5. [Layout File Resolution Order](#5-layout-file-resolution-order)
6. [When to Extend vs Override](#6-when-to-extend-vs-override)
7. [Default Page Layout XML](#7-default-page-layout-xml)
8. [ViewModel Injection via Layout XML](#8-viewmodel-injection-via-layout-xml)
9. [Hands-On: Overriding catalog_product_view.xml](#9-hands-on-overriding-catalog_product_viewxml)
10. [Common Pitfalls and Tricky Exam Points](#10-common-pitfalls-and-tricky-exam-points)
11. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Core Concepts Overview

Magento 2 uses an **XML-driven layout system** to define page structure. Understanding the difference between *extending* and *overriding* is critical both in day-to-day development and for the certification exam.

```
+---------------------+         +---------------------+
|   EXTEND            |         |   OVERRIDE          |
|---------------------|         |---------------------|
| Same handle name    |         | Replaces entire     |
| Adds instructions   |         | file content        |
| Original preserved  |         | Original discarded  |
| PREFERRED approach  |         | Use sparingly       |
+---------------------+         +---------------------+
```

### Two Dimensions of Layout Customization

| Dimension | Extend | Override |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| **What changes** | Adds to existing instructions | Replaces all existing instructions |
| **Upgrade safety** | Core upgrades still apply | Core upgrades are lost |
| **File placement** | `layout/` directory (module or theme) | `layout/override/` directory (theme only) |
| **Risk level** | Low | High |

---

## 2. Extending Layout Files

### What is Extension?

Extending a layout means **adding new XML instructions to an existing layout handle** without removing or replacing the original instructions. The Magento layout merge engine collects all XML files for the same handle and merges them together.

- **Exam focus:** Extending does NOT require a special directory — files placed in the standard `layout/` folder with the same handle name are automatically merged.

### File Placement for Extension

#### In a Module

```
app/code/Vendor/Module/
  view/
    frontend/
      layout/
        catalog_product_view.xml   <-- same handle name
```

#### In a Theme

```
app/design/frontend/Vendor/theme/
  Magento_Catalog/
    layout/
      catalog_product_view.xml   <-- same handle name
```

- **Exam focus:** Theme layout extension files go inside `<ThemeDir>/<Magento_Module>/layout/` — the module folder prefix is required when extending from a theme.

### Example: Extending catalog_product_view.xml

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!--
    File: app/design/frontend/Vendor/MyTheme/Magento_Catalog/layout/catalog_product_view.xml
    Purpose: EXTEND (add to) the product view page layout
-->
<page xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
      xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:View/Layout/etc/page_configuration.xsd">

    <body>
        <!-- Adding a new block to the product info column -->
        <referenceContainer name="product.info.main">
            <block class="Vendor\Module\Block\CustomInfo"
                   name="vendor.custom.info"
                   template="Vendor_Module::custom-info.phtml"
                   after="product.info.price"/>
        </referenceContainer>
    </body>

</page>
```

### How the Merge Engine Works

```
Module A: catalog_product_view.xml  ---+
Module B: catalog_product_view.xml  ---+--->  Merged Result (single handle)
Theme:    catalog_product_view.xml  ---+
```

The layout merge engine:
1. Collects all `catalog_product_view.xml` files from all active modules and the current theme
2. Processes them in **load order** (module load order, then theme files last)
3. Applies all instructions sequentially — later files can modify earlier ones

---

## 3. Overriding Layout Files

### What is an Override?

Overriding a layout file means your file **completely replaces** the original. The original file's XML instructions are entirely discarded — only your override file is used.

- **Exam focus:** Override files go in a special `override/` subdirectory inside the layout folder. This is a theme-only capability — modules cannot override layout files.

### Override Directory Structure

#### Override Base (Module) Layouts

Replaces the original file from the **module's** `view/frontend/layout/` directory:

```
app/design/frontend/Vendor/MyTheme/
  Magento_Catalog/
    layout/
      override/
        base/
          catalog_product_view.xml   <-- overrides Magento_Catalog module file
```

**Full path pattern:**
```
<theme_dir>/<Namespace_Module>/layout/override/base/<filename>.xml
```

#### Override Theme Layouts

Replaces a layout file from a **parent theme**:

```
app/design/frontend/Vendor/MyTheme/
  Magento_Catalog/
    layout/
      override/
        theme/
          Vendor/
            ParentTheme/
              catalog_product_view.xml   <-- overrides parent theme file
```

**Full path pattern:**
```
<theme_dir>/<Namespace_Module>/layout/override/theme/<Vendor>/<ParentTheme>/<filename>.xml
```

- **Exam focus:** There are exactly **two** override subdirectory types: `override/base/` (for module files) and `override/theme/<Vendor>/<ParentTheme>/` (for parent theme files). Know them both.

### Override File Example

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!--
    File: app/design/frontend/Vendor/MyTheme/Magento_Catalog/layout/override/base/catalog_product_view.xml
    Purpose: OVERRIDE (completely replace) the product view layout
    WARNING: You now own ALL content. Core upgrades will not apply.
-->
<page layout="2columns-left"
      xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
      xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:View/Layout/etc/page_configuration.xsd">

    <update handle="catalog_product_view_type_simple"/>

    <body>
        <!-- You must now define ALL required blocks yourself -->
        <referenceContainer name="content">
            <block class="Magento\Catalog\Block\Product\View"
                   name="product.info.view"
                   template="Magento_Catalog::product/view.phtml">
                <!-- child blocks... -->
            </block>
        </referenceContainer>

        <!-- Custom block added in this override -->
        <referenceContainer name="content">
            <block class="Vendor\Module\Block\CustomBanner"
                   name="vendor.custom.banner"
                   template="Vendor_Module::banner.phtml"
                   before="product.info.view"/>
        </referenceContainer>
    </body>

</page>
```

> **Corrected:** The original example used `<referenceBlock name="root">` with `<action method="setTemplate">`. `root` is a **container** (defined in empty.xml page layout), not a block — so `<referenceContainer>` must be used. The `<action>` element is also deprecated; prefer `<referenceBlock>` with `template` attribute or `<arguments>` instead.

---

## 4. Page Layout Overrides

### What are Page Layouts?

Page layouts define the **structural skeleton** of a page — the number and arrangement of columns. They differ from page configurations.

| Type | Example Files | Purpose |
|------|--------------|---------|
| **Page Layout** | `1column.xml`, `2columns-left.xml` | Column structure only |
| **Page Configuration** | `catalog_product_view.xml` | Full page content + head + body |
| **Generic Layout** | `default.xml` (in some contexts) | Reusable layout fragments |

### Base Page Layout File Locations

Page layout files are split across two locations in the Magento_Theme module:

```
<Magento_Theme_module>/view/base/page_layout/
  empty.xml                          <-- base empty page skeleton

<Magento_Theme_module>/view/frontend/page_layout/
  1column.xml                        <-- extends empty, adds header/footer
  2columns-left.xml                  <-- extends 1column, adds left sidebar
  2columns-right.xml                 <-- extends 1column, adds right sidebar
  3columns.xml                       <-- extends 1column, adds both sidebars
```

> **Corrected:** Only `empty.xml` lives in `view/base/page_layout/`. The four column layouts (`1column.xml`, `2columns-left.xml`, `2columns-right.xml`, `3columns.xml`) are in `view/frontend/page_layout/`. The original notes incorrectly placed all five in `view/base/`.

### Overriding Base Page Layout Templates

To override a base page layout in your theme, you need the `base/` subdirectory — same pattern as regular layout overrides:

```
app/design/frontend/Vendor/MyTheme/
  Magento_Theme/
    page_layout/
      override/
        base/
          1column.xml    <-- overrides the base 1column.xml page layout
```

**Full path patterns:**
```
Override module page layout:
<theme_dir>/Magento_Theme/page_layout/override/base/<filename>.xml

Override parent theme page layout:
<theme_dir>/Magento_Theme/page_layout/override/theme/<Vendor>/<ParentTheme>/<filename>.xml
```

> **Corrected:** The original notes omitted the `base/` subdirectory in the override path. Both `page_layout/override/base/` and `page_layout/override/theme/` subdirectories are confirmed in `app/etc/di.xml` (lines 1004, 1020). The pattern mirrors regular layout overrides exactly.

- **Exam focus:** Page layout overrides use `page_layout/override/base/` — NOT `layout/override/base/`. The directory is `page_layout/`, not `layout/`.

### Page Layout Override Example

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!--
    File: app/design/frontend/Vendor/MyTheme/Magento_Theme/page_layout/override/base/1column.xml
    Purpose: Override the 1-column page layout to add a custom wrapper
-->
<layout xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:View/Layout/etc/page_layout.xsd">

    <container name="root">
        <container name="after.body.start"
                   as="after.body.start"
                   before="-"
                   label="Page Top"/>
        <container name="page.wrapper"
                   as="page_wrapper"
                   htmlTag="div"
                   htmlClass="page-wrapper">
            <container name="header.container"
                       as="header_container"
                       label="Page Header Container"
                       htmlTag="header"
                       htmlClass="page-header"/>
            <container name="page.top"
                       as="page_top"
                       label="After Page Header"
                       htmlTag="div"
                       htmlClass="page-top"/>
            <container name="main.content"
                       htmlTag="main"
                       htmlId="maincontent"
                       htmlClass="page-main">
                <container name="columns.top" label="Before Main Columns"/>
                <container name="columns" htmlTag="div" htmlClass="columns">
                    <container name="main" label="Main Content Container"
                               htmlTag="div" htmlClass="column main"/>
                </container>
            </container>
            <container name="footer-container"
                       as="footer"
                       label="Page Footer Container"
                       htmlTag="footer"
                       htmlClass="page-footer"/>
        </container>
    </container>

</layout>
```

> Note: The actual `1column.xml` in Magento is much shorter — it uses `<update handle="empty"/>` to inherit the base skeleton from `empty.xml`, then adds header/footer containers via `<referenceContainer>`. This example shows the full expanded structure for illustration.

## 5. Layout File Resolution Order

Understanding how Magento resolves layout files is essential for predicting which instructions will take effect.

```
Resolution Priority (highest to lowest):
+------------------------------------------+
|  1. Theme override/base/         (wins)  |
|  2. Theme layout/ (extend)               |
|  3. Parent theme layout/                 |
|  4. Module layout/ (base)       (loses)  |
+------------------------------------------+
```

### Detailed Resolution Chain

```
Current Theme override/base/filename.xml
        |
        | (if not found, falls through)
        v
Current Theme Magento_Module/layout/filename.xml  (EXTENDS module)
        |
        | (merged with)
        v
Parent Theme Magento_Module/layout/filename.xml   (EXTENDS module)
        |
        | (merged with)
        v
Module view/frontend/layout/filename.xml          (original source)
```

- **Exam focus:** Theme layout files (in `<theme>/Magento_Module/layout/`) have **higher precedence** than module layout files. This means a theme's extension file can use `<referenceBlock>` to modify a module-defined block — even without overriding.

### Precedence Table

| Location | Type | Precedence |
|----------|------|------------|
| `<theme>/Magento_Module/layout/override/base/` | Override | **Highest** |
| `<theme>/Magento_Module/layout/override/theme/Vendor/Parent/` | Override | High |
| `<theme>/Magento_Module/layout/` | Extension | Medium-High |
| `<parentTheme>/Magento_Module/layout/` | Extension | Medium |
| `app/code/Vendor/Module/view/frontend/layout/` | Module | Base |

## 6. When to Extend vs Override

### Decision Flowchart

```
Do you need to change the existing layout?
        |
        v
   YES
        |
        v
Can you achieve the goal by ADDING
instructions (referenceBlock, etc.)?
        |
       / \
      YES  NO
      |     |
      v     v
  EXTEND  Is the original layout
          structurally incompatible?
                |
               / \
              YES  NO
              |     |
              v     v
          OVERRIDE  EXTEND
          (last     (refactor
          resort)    approach)
```

### Extend — Preferred Approach

**Use when:**
- Adding new blocks to existing containers
- Removing blocks (`<referenceBlock name="..." remove="true"/>`)
- Changing block templates or arguments
- Reordering blocks
- Adding `<update>` handles
- Changing container attributes

```xml
<!-- EXTEND: Remove a block you don't want -->
<page xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
      xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:View/Layout/etc/page_configuration.xsd">
    <body>
        <referenceBlock name="catalog.compare.sidebar" remove="true"/>
    </body>
</page>
```

```xml
<!-- EXTEND: Move a block to a different container -->
<page xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
      xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:View/Layout/etc/page_configuration.xsd">
    <body>
        <move element="catalog.compare.sidebar" destination="sidebar.additional"/>
    </body>
</page>
```

### Override — Last Resort

**Use when:**
- The original layout structure is fundamentally incompatible with your needs
- You need to change the root container structure
- Massive restructuring that would require dozens of `<move>` and `<remove>` instructions
- Building a radically different page layout

**The cost of overriding:**

```
Core upgrade released:
  - catalog_product_view.xml patched with security fix
  - Your override/base/catalog_product_view.xml: UNCHANGED
  - Result: Security fix does NOT apply to your store
```

- **Exam focus:** When you override a layout file, you become responsible for **all** its content. Magento core upgrades that patch the original file will have no effect on your store. This is the primary reason to avoid overrides.

## 7. Default Page Layout XML

### Location and Purpose

The `default.xml` handle is processed on **every page request**. It defines the foundational structure that all other page handles build upon.

The primary structural `default.xml` lives in the **module**, not the theme:

```
vendor/magento/module-theme/
  view/
    frontend/
      layout/
        default.xml          <-- the main structural default handle
```

The blank theme's `default.xml` is minimal — it only customizes the logo width:

```
app/design/frontend/Magento/blank/
  Magento_Theme/
    layout/
      default.xml            <-- extends module default, sets logo_width=170
```

- **Exam focus:** `default.xml` applies to every single page in the store. It is the base handle. Any block added to `default.xml` appears on all pages.

### Structure of default.xml (Magento_Theme module)

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!--
    vendor/magento/module-theme/view/frontend/layout/default.xml
    This is loaded on EVERY page - the base for all pages
-->
<page layout="3columns"
      xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
      xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:View/Layout/etc/page_configuration.xsd">

    <update handle="default_head_blocks"/>

    <body>
        <attribute name="id" value="html-body"/>

        <block name="require.js"
               class="Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template"
               template="Magento_Theme::page/js/require_js.phtml"/>

        <referenceContainer name="after.body.start">
            <block class="Magento\RequireJs\Block\Html\Head\Config"
                   name="requirejs-config"/>
            <block class="Magento\Framework\View\Element\Js\Cookie"
                   name="js_cookies"
                   template="Magento_Theme::js/cookie.phtml"/>
            <block class="Magento\Theme\Block\Html\Notices"
                   name="global_notices"
                   template="Magento_Theme::html/notices.phtml"/>
        </referenceContainer>

        <referenceBlock name="top.links">
            <block class="Magento\Theme\Block\Html\Header"
                   name="header" as="header" before="-">
                <arguments>
                    <argument name="show_part" xsi:type="string">welcome</argument>
                </arguments>
            </block>
        </referenceBlock>

        <!-- ... header, navigation, breadcrumbs ... -->

        <referenceContainer name="page.top">
            <block class="Magento\Theme\Block\Html\Breadcrumbs"
                   name="breadcrumbs" as="breadcrumbs"/>
        </referenceContainer>

        <referenceContainer name="main">
            <container name="content.top" label="Main Content Top"/>
            <container name="content" label="Main Content Area"/>
            <container name="content.aside" label="Main Content Aside"/>
            <container name="content.bottom" label="Main Content Bottom"/>
        </referenceContainer>

        <referenceContainer name="footer-container">
            <container name="footer" as="footer" label="Page Footer"
                       htmlTag="div" htmlClass="footer content">
                <block class="Magento\Theme\Block\Html\Footer"
                       name="copyright"
                       template="Magento_Theme::html/copyright.phtml"/>
            </container>
        </referenceContainer>

        <container name="before.body.end"
                   as="before_body_end"
                   after="-"
                   label="Before Body End"/>
    </body>

</page>
```

> **Corrected:** The original notes showed `layout="1column"` — the actual module default.xml uses `layout="3columns"`. The original also showed fabricated head elements (`<link src="jquery/jquery.cookie.js"/>`, `<meta name="format-detection">`), a wrong body attribute (`class` instead of `id`), and `Magento\Theme\Block\Html\Header` with a template attribute — the actual block uses a `show_part` argument with no explicit template. Head assets like `mage/calendar.css` are defined in the separate `default_head_blocks.xml` handle.

### Key Handles and Their Scope

| Handle | Scope | Common Use |
|--------|-------|-----------|
| `default` | Every page | Global header, footer, scripts |
| `default_head_blocks` | Every page (head only) | Global CSS/JS (viewport meta, calendar.css) |
| `catalog_product_view` | All product pages | Product detail structure |
| `catalog_category_view` | All category pages | Category listing structure |
| `cms_index_index` | Homepage only | Homepage specific blocks |
| `cms_page_view` | All CMS pages | CMS page structure |
| `customer_account` | All account pages | Account navigation |

## 8. ViewModel Injection via Layout XML

### What is a ViewModel?

A **ViewModel** is a PHP class that provides data/logic to a template **without extending** `Magento\Framework\View\Element\AbstractBlock`. This is the modern, recommended approach (replaces `Block` logic).

- **Exam focus:** ViewModels must implement `Magento\Framework\View\Element\Block\ArgumentInterface`. They are injected via layout XML arguments, not directly instantiated in templates.

### ViewModel Interface

```php
<?php
// app/code/Vendor/Module/ViewModel/ProductCustomData.php

namespace Vendor\Module\ViewModel;

use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Block\ArgumentInterface;
use Magento\Catalog\Api\ProductRepositoryInterface;

class ProductCustomData implements ArgumentInterface
{
    private ProductRepositoryInterface $productRepository;

    public function __construct(
        ProductRepositoryInterface $productRepository
    ) {
        $this->productRepository = $productRepository;
    }

    /**
     * Get custom data for template
     *
     * @param int $productId
     * @return array
     */
    public function getCustomData(int $productId): array
    {
        // Logic here — keeps Block class thin
        return [
            'extra_info' => 'Custom product data for ID: ' . $productId,
        ];
    }
}
```

### Injecting ViewModel in Layout XML

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!--
    Injecting a ViewModel via layout XML block arguments
-->
<page xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
      xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:View/Layout/etc/page_configuration.xsd">

    <body>
        <referenceContainer name="content">
            <block class="Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template"
                   name="vendor.custom.product.info"
                   template="Vendor_Module::product/custom-info.phtml">

                <arguments>
                    <!-- ViewModel injection: xsi:type="object" -->
                    <argument name="view_model"
                              xsi:type="object">
                        Vendor\Module\ViewModel\ProductCustomData
                    </argument>

                    <!-- You can also inject other argument types -->
                    <argument name="cache_lifetime"
                              xsi:type="number">86400</argument>

                    <argument name="wrapper_class"
                              xsi:type="string">custom-info-wrapper</argument>

                    <argument name="show_details"
                              xsi:type="boolean">true</argument>
                </arguments>
            </block>
        </referenceContainer>
    </body>

</page>
```

### Accessing ViewModel in Template

```php
<?php
/**
 * File: app/code/Vendor/Module/view/frontend/templates/product/custom-info.phtml
 *
 * @var \Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template $block
 * @var \Vendor\Module\ViewModel\ProductCustomData $viewModel
 */

/** @var \Vendor\Module\ViewModel\ProductCustomData $viewModel */
$viewModel = $block->getData('view_model');

// Get arguments
$wrapperClass = $block->getData('wrapper_class');   // 'custom-info-wrapper'
$showDetails  = $block->getData('show_details');    // true

// Use ViewModel method
$customData = $viewModel->getCustomData((int) $block->getProductId());
?>

<div class="<?= $block->escapeHtmlAttr($wrapperClass) ?>">
    <?php if ($showDetails): ?>
        <p><?= $block->escapeHtml($customData['extra_info']) ?></p>
    <?php endif; ?>
</div>
```

### Argument Types Reference

| `xsi:type` | PHP Type | Example Value |
|------------|----------|---------------|
| `string` | `string` | `"some text"` |
| `boolean` | `bool` | `true` / `false` |
| `number` | `int`/`float` | `42` |
| `object` | Class instance | `Vendor\Module\ViewModel\Class` |
| `array` | `array` | Contains `<item>` children |
| `null` | `null` | _(empty)_ |
| `url` | URL string | `route/path/action` |
| `helper` | Helper call | `Helper\Class::method` |
| `options` | Options array | Source model class (must implement `OptionSourceInterface`) |

> **Corrected:** Added `helper` type (confirmed in `app/etc/di.xml` at the `layoutArgumentReaderInterpreter` composite). All 9 types are registered there: `options`, `array`, `boolean`, `number`, `string`, `null`, `object`, `url`, `helper`.

- **Exam focus:** `xsi:type="object"` triggers Magento's **Object Manager / DI** to instantiate the class. The argument value is the **fully qualified class name** (FQCN). This is the standard pattern for ViewModel injection.

### ViewModel with referenceBlock (Injecting into Existing Block)

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<page xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
      xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:View/Layout/etc/page_configuration.xsd">

    <body>
        <!-- Inject ViewModel into an EXISTING block via referenceBlock -->
        <referenceBlock name="product.info.price">
            <arguments>
                <argument name="view_model"
                          xsi:type="object">
                    Vendor\Module\ViewModel\PriceDecorator
                </argument>
            </arguments>
        </referenceBlock>
    </body>

</page>
```

> Note: `product.info.price` is actually a **container** in `catalog_product_view.xml` (line 40). To inject a ViewModel, you must target a **block** — for example `product.price.final` (class `Magento\Catalog\Pricing\Render`). Containers do not render templates and cannot use ViewModels.

## 9. Hands-On: Overriding catalog_product_view.xml

### Scenario

Override `Magento_Catalog/layout/catalog_product_view.xml` in a custom theme and add a custom block to the product page.

### Step 1: Create the Theme Directory Structure

```bash
# Assuming theme: Vendor/CustomTheme
mkdir -p app/design/frontend/Vendor/CustomTheme/Magento_Catalog/layout/override/base
```

```
app/design/frontend/Vendor/CustomTheme/
  registration.php
  theme.xml
  Magento_Catalog/
    layout/
      override/
        base/
          catalog_product_view.xml   <-- your override file
      catalog_product_view.xml       <-- (optional) separate extend file
    templates/
      product/
        custom-block.phtml
```

### Step 2: Create the Override File

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!--
    File: app/design/frontend/Vendor/CustomTheme/Magento_Catalog/layout/override/base/catalog_product_view.xml

    IMPORTANT: This overrides the ENTIRE module layout file.
    You must include ALL required instructions from the original.
    Core upgrades to the original will NOT be applied here.
-->
<page layout="1column"
      xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
      xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:View/Layout/etc/page_configuration.xsd">

    <!-- Include standard product view handles -->
    <update handle="catalog_product_view_type_simple"/>
    <update handle="catalog_product_view_type_configurable"/>
    <update handle="catalog_product_view_type_grouped"/>
    <update handle="catalog_product_view_type_bundle"/>
    <update handle="catalog_product_view_type_virtual"/>
    <update handle="catalog_product_view_type_downloadable"/>

    <head>
        <css src="Magento_Catalog::css/product.css"/>
    </head>

    <body>
        <!-- Breadcrumbs: reference existing block from default.xml and set template -->
        <referenceBlock name="breadcrumbs"
                        template="Magento_Catalog::product/breadcrumbs.phtml">
            <arguments>
                <argument name="viewModel" xsi:type="object">
                    Magento\Catalog\ViewModel\Product\Breadcrumbs
                </argument>
            </arguments>
        </referenceBlock>

        <!-- Main content area -->
        <referenceContainer name="content">

            <!-- Product info main container (matches real layout structure) -->
            <container name="product.info.main"
                       htmlTag="div"
                       htmlClass="product-info-main">

                <!-- Price block -->
                <block class="Magento\Catalog\Pricing\Render"
                       name="product.price.final">
                    <arguments>
                        <argument name="price_render" xsi:type="string">product.price.render.default</argument>
                        <argument name="price_type_code" xsi:type="string">final_price</argument>
                        <argument name="zone" xsi:type="string">item_view</argument>
                    </arguments>
                </block>

                <!-- Add to cart -->
                <block class="Magento\Catalog\Block\Product\View"
                       name="product.info.addtocart"
                       template="Magento_Catalog::product/view/addtocart.phtml"/>

            </container>

            <!-- Product media container -->
            <container name="product.info.media"
                       htmlTag="div"
                       htmlClass="product media">
                <block class="Magento\Catalog\Block\Product\View\Gallery"
                       name="product.image.container"
                       template="Magento_Catalog::product/view/gallery.phtml"/>
            </container>

            <!-- *** YOUR CUSTOM BLOCK *** -->
            <block class="Vendor\Module\Block\Product\CustomBanner"
                   name="vendor.custom.product.banner"
                   template="Vendor_Module::product/custom-banner.phtml"
                   after="product.info.main">
                <arguments>
                    <argument name="view_model"
                              xsi:type="object">
                        Vendor\Module\ViewModel\ProductBanner
                    </argument>
                </arguments>
            </block>

        </referenceContainer>
    </body>

</page>
```

> **Corrected:** The original example used `Magento\Catalog\Block\Product\View\Price` — this class does not exist. The correct class is `Magento\Catalog\Pricing\Render` (confirmed in `catalog_product_view.xml:54`). Also corrected: used `Magento\Catalog\Block\Breadcrumbs` nested inside breadcrumbs block — the actual pattern is `<referenceBlock name="breadcrumbs" template="...">` with a ViewModel, since `breadcrumbs` is `Magento\Theme\Block\Html\Breadcrumbs` from `default.xml`.

### Step 3: Create the Custom Block Class

```php
<?php
// app/code/Vendor/Module/Block/Product/CustomBanner.php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vendor\Module\Block\Product;

use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template;
use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template\Context;
use Magento\Framework\Registry;

class CustomBanner extends Template
{
    private Registry $registry;

    public function __construct(
        Context $context,
        Registry $registry,
        array $data = []
    ) {
        parent::__construct($context, $data);
        $this->registry = $registry;
    }

    /**
     * Get the current product
     *
     * @return \Magento\Catalog\Model\Product|null
     */
    public function getCurrentProduct(): ?\Magento\Catalog\Model\Product
    {
        return $this->registry->registry('current_product');
    }
}
```

### Step 4: Create the Template

```php
<?php
/**
 * File: app/code/Vendor/Module/view/frontend/templates/product/custom-banner.phtml
 *
 * @var \Vendor\Module\Block\Product\CustomBanner $block
 * @var \Vendor\Module\ViewModel\ProductBanner $viewModel
 */

$product   = $block->getCurrentProduct();
$viewModel = $block->getData('view_model');
?>

<?php if ($product): ?>
<div class="vendor-custom-banner" data-product-id="<?= (int) $product->getId() ?>">
    <div class="banner-inner">
        <h3 class="banner-title">
            <?= $block->escapeHtml(__('Special offer for: %1', $product->getName())) ?>
        </h3>
        <?php if ($viewModel && $bannerHtml = $viewModel->getBannerHtml($product)): ?>
            <?= /* @noEscape */ $bannerHtml ?>
        <?php endif; ?>
    </div>
</div>
<?php endif; ?>
```

### Step 5: Better Alternative — Extend Instead of Override

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!--
    File: app/design/frontend/Vendor/CustomTheme/Magento_Catalog/layout/catalog_product_view.xml
    Purpose: EXTEND (preferred over override) — just add the custom block
-->
<page xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
      xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:View/Layout/etc/page_configuration.xsd">

    <body>
        <!-- Add custom block after existing product info wrapper -->
        <referenceContainer name="content">
            <block class="Vendor\Module\Block\Product\CustomBanner"
                   name="vendor.custom.product.banner"
                   template="Vendor_Module::product/custom-banner.phtml"
                   after="product.info.main">
                <arguments>
                    <argument name="view_model"
                              xsi:type="object">
                        Vendor\Module\ViewModel\ProductBanner
                    </argument>
                </arguments>
            </block>
        </referenceContainer>
    </body>

</page>
```

- **Exam focus:** Step 5 achieves the **exact same result** as the full override in Step 2 (adding a custom block), with a fraction of the code and **zero upgrade risk**. This is why extending is always preferred.

### Step 6: Flush Cache and Verify

```bash
# Clean layout cache
bin/magento cache:clean layout

# Full cache flush (development)
bin/magento cache:flush

# If using generated code, regenerate
bin/magento setup:di:compile
```

> **Corrected:** Removed `bin/magento dev:xml:convert` — this command converts XML files using XSL style sheets. It does not validate layout XML files.

## 10. Common Pitfalls and Tricky Exam Points

### Pitfall 1: Override Scope Limitation

```
WRONG assumption: Modules can override layout files
CORRECT:          Only THEMES can use the override/ directory
```

- **Exam focus:** Layout **overrides** are a **theme-only** feature. Modules can only **extend** (add) layout instructions.

### Pitfall 2: Core Upgrade Risk with Overrides

```
Scenario:
  - You override catalog_product_view.xml in your theme (2023)
  - Magento releases 2.4.7 with important structural changes to
    catalog_product_view.xml (2024)
  - Your override still uses the 2023 version
  - Result: Missing features, potential errors, security gaps
```

### Pitfall 3: Theme Extension Has Implicit Override Power

```xml
<!-- Theme extension file — no "override" directory needed -->
<!-- This STILL takes higher precedence than the module file -->

<!-- app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/Magento_Catalog/layout/catalog_product_view.xml -->
<page xmlns:xsi="...">
    <body>
        <!-- This runs AFTER the module's instructions, but can UNDO them -->
        <referenceBlock name="product.info.price" remove="true"/>
    </body>
</page>
```

> Note: `product.info.price` is a **container**, not a block. To remove it, use `<referenceContainer name="product.info.price" remove="true"/>`. This example demonstrates the concept — an extension file can effectively undo module instructions without needing the `override/` directory.

- **Exam focus:** A theme's regular extension file (in `<theme>/Magento_Module/layout/`) has **higher precedence** than the module's original file — even though it's not in `override/`. The difference is: extension files *add* instructions, override files *replace* the entire file.

### Pitfall 4: Wrong Directory for Page Layout Overrides

```
WRONG: Magento_Catalog/layout/override/base/1column.xml
                                            ^-- page layouts don't go in layout/

WRONG: Magento_Theme/page_layout/override/1column.xml
                                          ^-- missing base/ subdirectory

CORRECT: Magento_Theme/page_layout/override/base/1column.xml
                       ^-- uses page_layout/override/base/
```

> **Corrected:** The original notes showed the path without the `base/` subdirectory as "CORRECT". The actual override path requires `page_layout/override/base/` for module overrides and `page_layout/override/theme/Vendor/ParentTheme/` for parent theme overrides — confirmed in `app/etc/di.xml`.

### Pitfall 5: Handle Name Must Match Exactly

```
WRONG: catalog_Product_View.xml    (case mismatch)
WRONG: catalog-product-view.xml    (hyphens instead of underscores)
CORRECT: catalog_product_view.xml  (exact match, all lowercase, underscores)
```

### Pitfall 6: Missing `xsi:type` for ViewModel Argument

```xml
<!-- WRONG: Missing xsi:type — Magento won't know to instantiate the class -->
<argument name="view_model">Vendor\Module\ViewModel\MyClass</argument>

<!-- CORRECT -->
<argument name="view_model" xsi:type="object">Vendor\Module\ViewModel\MyClass</argument>
```

### Pitfall 7: ViewModel Must Implement ArgumentInterface

```php
// WRONG: Just a plain class
class MyViewModel {
    // ...
}

// CORRECT: Must implement ArgumentInterface
use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Block\ArgumentInterface;

class MyViewModel implements ArgumentInterface {
    // ...
}
```

### Summary Comparison Table

| Aspect | Extend | Override |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Directory** | `<theme>/Magento_X/layout/` | `<theme>/Magento_X/layout/override/base/` |
| **Who can do it** | Modules and Themes | Themes only |
| **Effect** | Adds instructions to merged result | Replaces entire file |
| **Core upgrades** | Still apply | **Lost — you own all content** |
| **Risk** | Low | High |
| **Preference** | **Always preferred** | Last resort only |
| **Page layouts** | N/A (use `page_layout/`) | `Magento_Theme/page_layout/override/base/` |
| **Parent theme** | Inherits automatically | `override/theme/Vendor/Parent/` |
