## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Extending Layout Files
- [ ] Place file in `<theme>/<Magento_Module>/layout/<handle-name>.xml` for theme extension
- [ ] Place file in `app/code/Vendor/Module/view/frontend/layout/<handle-name>.xml` for module extension
- [ ] Use **same handle filename** as the file you want to add instructions to
- [ ] Extension files are **merged** — original instructions are preserved
- [ ] Theme extension files have **higher precedence** than module files even without using `override/`

### Overriding Layout Files
- [ ] Only **themes** can override — not modules
- [ ] Override a **module layout**: `<theme>/Magento_Module/layout/override/base/<filename>.xml`
- [ ] Override a **parent theme layout**: `<theme>/Magento_Module/layout/override/theme/<Vendor>/<ParentTheme>/<filename>.xml`
- [ ] Override **replaces** the entire file — no merging occurs
- [ ] Core upgrades to the original file **do NOT apply** to your override
- [ ] Always prefer extending; use override as a last resort

### Page Layout Overrides
- [ ] `empty.xml` lives in `<Magento_Theme>/view/base/page_layout/`; column layouts in `view/frontend/page_layout/`
- [ ] Override module page layouts in: `<theme>/Magento_Theme/page_layout/override/base/<filename>.xml`
- [ ] Override parent theme page layouts in: `<theme>/Magento_Theme/page_layout/override/theme/<Vendor>/<Parent>/<filename>.xml`
- [ ] Use `page_layout/override/base/` — NOT `layout/override/base/` — for page layouts
- [ ] Page layouts define structural skeleton (columns), not content

### Layout File Resolution Order
- [ ] Theme `override/base/` wins over everything
- [ ] Theme `layout/` (extension) wins over module `layout/`
- [ ] Parent theme is inherited but child theme can override
- [ ] Module layout files are the base; loaded first, lowest precedence

### Default Page Layout
- [ ] `default.xml` handle is loaded on **every page**
- [ ] Structural version in `vendor/magento/module-theme/view/frontend/layout/default.xml` (sets `layout="3columns"`)
- [ ] Blank theme extends it at `Magento/blank/Magento_Theme/layout/default.xml` (only sets `logo_width`)
- [ ] Defines global elements: header, footer, breadcrumbs, `before.body.end`, etc.
- [ ] Extend `default.xml` to add blocks that appear on all pages

### ViewModel Injection
- [ ] ViewModel must implement `Magento\Framework\View\Element\Block\ArgumentInterface`
- [ ] Inject via `<argument name="view_model" xsi:type="object">FQCN</argument>` in `<arguments>` block
- [ ] Access in template: `$viewModel = $block->getData('view_model');`
- [ ] Use `xsi:type="object"` — this triggers DI/Object Manager instantiation
- [ ] Can inject into new blocks OR existing blocks via `<referenceBlock>`

### Argument Types (`xsi:type`)
- [ ] `string` — plain text value
- [ ] `boolean` — `true` or `false`
- [ ] `number` — numeric value
- [ ] `object` — class FQCN, instantiated via DI
- [ ] `array` — contains `<item>` children
- [ ] `null` — null value
- [ ] `url` — route/action path
- [ ] `helper` — helper class method call
- [ ] `options` — source model class (must implement `OptionSourceInterface`)

### Common Exam Traps
- [ ] Modules **cannot** use `override/` directories — themes only
- [ ] Override = you own ALL content; core patches don't apply
- [ ] Handle filename must match **exactly** (lowercase, underscores)
- [ ] Page layout override path uses `page_layout/override/base/`, not `layout/override/base/`
- [ ] A theme `layout/` file (non-override) STILL has higher precedence than module `layout/` files
- [ ] Missing `xsi:type="object"` on a ViewModel argument = silent failure
- [ ] ViewModel without `ArgumentInterface` = DI injection will fail

flashcards.question: What is the difference between extending and overriding a layout file in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Extending adds new XML instructions to an existing layout handle — files in the standard layout/ directory are automatically merged with the original, preserving all original instructions. Overriding completely replaces the original file — only your override file is used. Override files go in the special layout/override/base/ directory and are a theme-only capability (modules cannot override). Extending is always preferred because core upgrades still apply.
flashcards.hint: One adds to the existing instructions, the other replaces them entirely. The file location signals which approach is used.

flashcards.question: What is the correct directory path to override a module's layout file from a theme?
flashcards.answer: To override a module layout file: <theme_dir>/<Namespace_Module>/layout/override/base/<filename>.xml. To override a parent theme's layout file: <theme_dir>/<Namespace_Module>/layout/override/theme/<Vendor>/<ParentTheme>/<filename>.xml. These are the only two override subdirectory types. Modules cannot use the override/ directory — only themes can.
flashcards.hint: The key directory is override/, with two possible subdirectories depending on whether you're overriding a module or parent theme file.

flashcards.question: Why is layout extending preferred over overriding, and what is the main risk of overriding?
flashcards.answer: Extending is preferred because original instructions are preserved and core upgrades still apply to the base layout files. When you override a layout file, you become responsible for ALL its content — Magento core upgrades that patch the original file will have no effect on your store. This can result in missing features, security gaps, and potential errors after upgrades.
flashcards.hint: Think about what happens during a Magento version upgrade when the original file has been patched.

flashcards.question: What is the layout file resolution order from highest to lowest priority?
flashcards.answer: The resolution order is: 1) Theme override/base/ (highest, replaces entire file), 2) Theme layout/ extension (merged after module files), 3) Parent theme layout/ extension (merged), 4) Module view/frontend/layout/ (base, lowest priority). Theme extension files have higher precedence than module files even without using the override/ directory, because they are processed later in the merge sequence.
flashcards.hint: Override always wins, then theme extensions beat module files due to processing order.

flashcards.question: How do page layout overrides differ from regular layout overrides in terms of directory paths?
flashcards.answer: Page layout overrides use page_layout/override/base/ instead of layout/override/base/. For example: <theme>/Magento_Theme/page_layout/override/base/1column.xml. Using layout/override/base/ for page layouts is incorrect. This mirrors the regular override pattern but uses the page_layout/ directory since page layouts define structural skeletons (columns), not page content.
flashcards.hint: The directory name changes to match the type of layout file being overridden.

flashcards.question: What is a ViewModel in Magento 2, and what interface must it implement?
flashcards.answer: A ViewModel is a PHP class that provides data and logic to a template without extending AbstractBlock. It must implement Magento\Framework\View\Element\Block\ArgumentInterface, which is a marker interface with no methods to implement. ViewModels are injected via layout XML arguments using xsi:type="object" and are the modern, recommended approach for separating display logic from block classes.
flashcards.hint: It implements a marker interface from the Block namespace and is injected through XML, not PHP.

flashcards.question: How is a ViewModel injected into a block via layout XML?
flashcards.answer: A ViewModel is injected as an argument with xsi:type="object" inside the block's <arguments> element. The value is the fully qualified class name (FQCN). Example: <argument name="view_model" xsi:type="object">Vendor\Module\ViewModel\MyClass</argument>. The xsi:type="object" tells Magento to instantiate the class via the DI container. In the template, access it with $block->getData('view_model') or $block->getViewModel().
flashcards.hint: The key is the xsi:type attribute value and the argument name convention.

flashcards.question: What are the nine argument xsi:type values available in Magento 2 layout XML?
flashcards.answer: The nine types are: string (plain text), boolean (true/false), number (int/float), object (class FQCN instantiated via DI), array (contains <item> children), null (null value), url (route/action path), helper (helper class method call), and options (source model class implementing OptionSourceInterface). These are registered in app/etc/di.xml under the layoutArgumentReaderInterpreter composite.
flashcards.hint: There are nine types total, covering primitive values, class instances, and special Magento-specific types.

flashcards.question: Can modules use the layout override/ directory to override other modules' layout files?
flashcards.answer: No, layout overrides are a theme-only feature. Modules cannot use the override/ directory — they can only extend (add to) layout instructions by placing files in their own view/frontend/layout/ directory with the same handle filename. Only themes can completely replace a layout file using the override/base/ or override/theme/ subdirectories.
flashcards.hint: This is a capability reserved for themes, not modules. Modules can only add instructions.

flashcards.question: Where do the core page layout files (empty.xml, 1column.xml, etc.) live in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: empty.xml lives in Magento_Theme module's view/base/page_layout/ directory. The four column layouts (1column.xml, 2columns-left.xml, 2columns-right.xml, 3columns.xml) live in view/frontend/page_layout/. The column layouts extend empty.xml using <update handle="empty"/> to inherit the base skeleton, then add their specific container structures.
flashcards.hint: One layout is shared across areas (in view/base/), while the column-specific layouts are frontend-only.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between page layout, page configuration, and generic layout file types?
flashcards.answer: Page Layout files (like 1column.xml, 2columns-left.xml) define only the structural column skeleton of a page. Page Configuration files (like catalog_product_view.xml) define the full page content including head and body elements. Generic Layout files (like default.xml in some contexts) provide reusable layout fragments. Page layouts use page_layout.xsd schema, while page configurations use page_configuration.xsd.
flashcards.hint: Each type serves a different level of the page definition — structure, content, or reusable fragments.

flashcards.question: What happens if you omit the xsi:type="object" attribute when defining a ViewModel argument in layout XML?
flashcards.answer: Without xsi:type="object", Magento will not know to instantiate the class via the DI container. The value will be treated as a plain string containing the class name text, not an actual object instance. This results in a silent failure — the template will receive a string instead of a ViewModel object, and calling methods on it will cause errors. This is a common exam trap.
flashcards.hint: The type attribute tells Magento HOW to process the argument value — without it, no instantiation occurs.

flashcards.question: How does a theme extension file (not in override/) still take precedence over a module's layout file?
flashcards.answer: Theme extension files in <theme>/Magento_Module/layout/ are processed after module layout files in the merge sequence. Since later instructions can modify or undo earlier ones (e.g., using <referenceBlock remove="true"/>), the theme's extension effectively has higher precedence. The difference from override is that extension files add instructions to the merged result, while override files replace the entire file.
flashcards.hint: Processing order matters — theme files come after module files in the merge chain.

flashcards.question: What is the default page layout set in Magento's default.xml handle?
flashcards.answer: The module-level default.xml (in vendor/magento/module-theme/view/frontend/layout/) sets layout="3columns" on the <page> root element. This means all pages default to a three-column layout unless a more specific handle overrides this setting. Individual page types (like product pages or checkout) typically override this with their own layout attribute.
flashcards.hint: The default is wider than you might expect — it includes both sidebars.

studyNotes.title: Day 5 — phtml Templates: Creation, Customization & Security
studyNotes.content:
# phtml Templates: Creation, Customization & Security ## Table of Contents - [1. Overview & Learning Goals](#1-overview--learning-goals) - [2. Template File Locations](#2-template-file-locations) - [3. Template Override Mechanism](#3-template-override-mechanism) - [4. Template API: $block, $this, and ViewModels](#4-template-api-block-this-and-viewmodels) - [5. Output Escaping — Critical Security](#5-output-escaping--critical-security) - [6. Template Debugging with Template Hints](#6-template-debugging-with-template-hints) - [7. Hands-On Walkthrough](#7-hands-on-walkthrough) - [8. Common Pitfalls & Tricky Exam Scenarios](#8-common-pitfalls--tricky-exam-scenarios) - [9. Quick-Reference Checklist](#9-quick-reference-checklist) --- ## 1. Overview & Learning Goals Magento 2 uses **phtml** files as its templating format — PHP embedded inside HTML. Every block rendered on the frontend is associated with a phtml template file that controls its markup output. **Key skills for this topic:** - Know *where* template files live (module vs. theme) - Know *how* to override a template without touching core code - Know *which escaping method* to call and *when* - Understand the **ViewModel pattern** as the modern alternative to putting logic in blocks - Use **template hints** to debug which template is rendering which markup > **Exam focus:** The distinction between module-level templates and theme-level overrides is a foundational Magento certification concept tested heavily in frontend and developer exams. --- ## 2. Template File Locations ### 2.1 Module-Level Templates (Source / Default) ``` app/code/Vendor/Module/ └── view/ └── frontend/ └── templates/ └── example.phtml ``` - These are the **default** templates shipped with a module - Should **never be edited directly** — changes are overwritten on module updates - The `frontend` area can also be `adminhtml`, `base`, etc. ### 2.2 Theme-Level Templates (Override Location) ``` app/design/frontend/Vendor/theme/ └── Magento_Module/ └── templates/ └── example.phtml ``` - The directory name **must match the module name** exactly (e.g., `Magento_Catalog`, `Magento_Checkout`) - The relative path **inside** `templates/` must be identical to the module's original path - Magento's file fallback system picks the theme template *over* the module template automatically ### 2.3 File Resolution Order (Fallback Chain) ``` Theme (child) | v Theme (parent) | v Module (view/frontend/templates/) ``` > **Exam focus:** Theme template overrides do NOT require layout XML changes — just matching the directory structure and relative path is sufficient. ### 2.4 Nested Subdirectory Example If a module template lives at: ``` Magento_Catalog/view/frontend/templates/product/view/gallery.phtml ``` The theme override lives at: ``` app/design/frontend/Vendor/theme/Magento_Catalog/templates/product/view/gallery.phtml ``` --- ## 3. Template Override Mechanism ### 3.1 Step-by-Step: Overriding a Core Template **Step 1 — Identify the template to override** Use template hints (see Section 6) or inspect layout XML: ```xml ``` The format `ModuleName::path/to/template.phtml` is the **template identifier** used in layout XML. **Step 2 — Locate the source file** ``` vendor/magento/module-catalog/view/frontend/templates/product/view.phtml ``` **Step 3 — Copy to your theme** ```bash # Create directory in theme mkdir -p app/design/frontend/Vendor/MyTheme/Magento_Catalog/templates/product/ # Copy the file cp vendor/magento/module-catalog/view/frontend/templates/product/view.phtml \ app/design/frontend/Vendor/MyTheme/Magento_Catalog/templates/product/view.phtml ``` **Step 4 — Edit the theme copy** Make your customizations in the theme file only. The original is untouched. **Step 5 — Clear cache** ```bash bin/magento cache:clean bin/magento cache:flush ``` > **Exam focus:** You copy the template to the theme; you do NOT need to declare the override in any XML file. The fallback mechanism handles it automatically. ### 3.2 Changing a Template via Layout XML If you want a *different* template file (not just override the same path), use the `template` attribute on ``: ```xml ``` > **Note:** You may also see the older `` pattern in legacy code. This approach is **deprecated** — always prefer the `template` attribute directly on ``. --- ## 4. Template API: $block, $this, and ViewModels ### 4.1 `$block` — The Correct Variable Inside a phtml template, **`$block`** is the block instance associated with that template. ```php getProduct()->getName(); echo $block->escapeHtml($productName); ?> ``` - `$block` is available because it's a local variable in `Php::render()` (the template engine's render method), and `include` runs in the same scope - It is the instance of the block class (e.g., `Magento\Catalog\Block\Product\View`) - You can call any **public method** on the block via `$block` ### 4.2 `$this` — Deprecated but Functional ```php getProduct()->getName(); // Works but discouraged ?> ``` - In Magento 1, `$this` referred to the block instance inside templates - In Magento 2, `$this` inside a phtml refers to the **template engine** (`Magento\Framework\View\TemplateEngine\Php`), NOT the block - However, `Php::__call()` **proxies** method calls to the current block — so `$this->getProduct()` actually DOES work identically to `$block->getProduct()` for block methods - `$this` also has engine-specific methods like `$this->helper()` that are NOT available on `$block` - Using `$this` triggers the `Magento2.Templates.ThisInTemplate` PHPCS warning — core templates that use it suppress this with `// phpcs:disable Magento2.Templates.ThisInTemplate.FoundThis` > **Exam focus:** `$block` is the correct and recommended variable in Magento 2 phtml templates. While `$this` does work for block methods (via `__call` proxy), it's deprecated and triggers static analysis warnings. The key difference: `$this` is the Php engine instance; `$block` is the actual block instance. ### 4.3 ViewModel Pattern The ViewModel pattern separates **display logic** from **block classes**, keeping blocks thin. #### Why ViewModels? | Approach | Problem | |---|---| | Logic in Block class | Block classes become fat; hard to unit test; blocks are tied to layout | | Logic in Template | Mixes PHP logic with HTML markup; bad separation of concerns | | **ViewModel** | **Clean separation: Block handles rendering, ViewModel handles logic** | #### Step 1 — Create a ViewModel class ```php **Exam focus:** ViewModels **must implement** `Magento\Framework\View\Element\Block\ArgumentInterface`. This interface is a marker interface (no methods to implement) but is required for the DI system to inject it properly as a block argument. #### Step 2 — Inject ViewModel via Layout XML ```xml Vendor\Module\ViewModel\MyViewModel ``` - The argument name `view_model` is conventional but can be any string - `xsi:type="object"` tells Magento to instantiate the class via Object Manager/DI #### Step 3 — Access ViewModel in Template ```php getData('view_model'); // OR the cleaner method: $viewModel = $block->getViewModel(); // Only works if argument name is 'view_model' ?>

escapeHtml($viewModel->getCustomMessage()) ?>

``` **How `getViewModel()` works:** `getViewModel()` is a magic method call that translates to `getData('view_model')`. Magento's `\Magento\Framework\DataObject` base class generates `getX()` methods that map to `getData('x')`. So `getViewModel()` -> `getData('view_model')`. ```php // These are equivalent: $viewModel = $block->getData('view_model'); $viewModel = $block->getViewModel(); ``` > **Exam focus:** The magic getter `getViewModel()` works because Magento's DataObject maps `getX()` calls to `getData('x')`. The argument must be named `view_model` in layout XML for `getViewModel()` to work. --- ## 5. Output Escaping — Critical Security This section is **the most security-critical** part of template development. Failing to escape output correctly leads to **Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)** vulnerabilities. ### 5.1 The Golden Rule > **Never echo raw user-supplied or database-sourced data in a template without escaping.** ### 5.2 Escaping Methods Quick Reference | Method | Use Case | Escapes | |---|---|---| | `$block->escapeHtml($str)` | Text content inside HTML tags | HTML entities (`<`, `>`, `&`, `"`, `'`) | | `$block->escapeHtmlAttr($str)` | HTML attribute values | HTML attribute-safe encoding | | `$block->escapeUrl($url)` | URLs in `href`, `src`, `action` | Strips dangerous protocols + HTML-encodes | | `$block->escapeJs($str)` | Strings inside JavaScript | JS-safe escaping | | `$block->escapeCss($str)` | Values inside CSS contexts | CSS-safe escaping | > **Note:** `escapeCss()` is also available on AbstractBlock (line 944) for CSS context escaping, though it's less commonly used in templates. ### 5.3 `escapeHtml()` — Text Content ```php tag ?>

escapeHtml($block->getProductName()) ?>

getProductName() ?>

``` **What it does:** - Uses `htmlspecialchars()` with `ENT_QUOTES | ENT_SUBSTITUTE` flags - Encodes `<` -> `<`, `>` -> `>`, `&` -> `&`, `"` -> `"`, `'` -> `'` - The browser displays the encoded characters as their literal text equivalents - Prevents injected HTML/script tags from being interpreted by the browser **Allowed tags parameter:** ```php escapeHtml($content, ['b', 'strong', 'em', 'span']); ?> ``` > **Exam focus (CRITICAL TRICKY POINT):** `escapeHtml()` encodes HTML entities. **Do NOT use it on content that is supposed to render as HTML** (e.g., CMS block content, product descriptions with HTML). Using `escapeHtml()` on HTML content will display raw tags to the user instead of rendering them. ### 5.4 `escapeHtmlAttr()` — HTML Attributes ```php getCustomClass(); ?>
...
getSomeData(); ?> ... ``` **Why not just use `escapeHtml()`?** - `escapeHtmlAttr()` provides stricter encoding appropriate for attribute context - Handles single quotes and other characters that can break out of attribute values ### 5.5 `escapeUrl()` — URLs ```php getRedirectUrl(); ?> Click here
...
``` > **Exam focus (TRICKY):** `escapeUrl()` does **NOT validate** the URL — it does not check if the URL points to a safe/valid destination. It only ensures the URL value is safe to embed as an attribute value (prevents attribute injection). A URL like `javascript:alert(1)` — `escapeUrl()` will strip the `javascript:` protocol, but it does not do semantic URL validation. **What `escapeUrl()` does:** - Calls `escapeXssInUrl()` which uses `escapeScriptIdentifiers()` to remove `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `data:` protocol patterns - Then passes the result through `escapeHtml()` to encode special characters - Does NOT verify the URL resolves to anything valid ### 5.6 `escapeJs()` — Inline JavaScript Strings ```php getCustomerName(); ?> ``` **When to use:** - Only for string values embedded **inside** JavaScript string literals - Escapes `\`, `'`, `"`, newlines, and other JS-dangerous characters - Does NOT escape HTML — if the script tag is inside HTML, you may need both > **Exam focus:** Use `escapeJs()` specifically for values inside JS string contexts. For JSON output in JS, use `json_encode()` with appropriate flags or Magento's `$block->escapeJs()` depending on context. ### 5.7 Escaping Decision Tree ``` Is the output going into... +-- Inside an HTML tag (text content)? | --> escapeHtml() | +-- Inside an HTML attribute value (class, data-*, title, alt)? | --> escapeHtmlAttr() | +-- As a URL value (href, src, action, formaction)? | --> escapeUrl() | +-- Inside a JavaScript string literal? | --> escapeJs() | +-- Inside a CSS context (style attribute, inline styles)? | --> escapeCss() | +-- Should render as raw HTML (CMS content, rich text)? --> Do NOT escape (trust the source, sanitize on input) --> Or use: $block->escapeHtml($content, ['allowed', 'tags']) ``` ### 5.8 Common Escaping Mistakes #### Mistake 1: Using `escapeHtml()` on HTML Content ```php getDescription(); // Contains "

Great product

" echo $block->escapeHtml($description); // Output: <p>Great product</p> (visible as text, not rendered) // CORRECT — if you trust the source and need HTML rendered echo $description; // Only acceptable for trusted/sanitized content // BETTER — use allowed tags if you need some HTML but want protection echo $block->escapeHtml($description, ['p', 'br', 'strong', 'em', 'ul', 'li']); ?> ``` #### Mistake 2: Not Escaping URLs ```php Product Product ``` #### Mistake 3: Raw User Input ```php getRequest()->getParam('name'); echo $name; // CORRECT $name = $block->getRequest()->getParam('name'); echo $block->escapeHtml($name); ?> ``` > Note: `$block->getRequest()` is a real method on AbstractBlock (line 241) that returns the HTTP request object. #### Mistake 4: Forgetting Attribute Context ```php
``` --- ## 6. Template Debugging with Template Hints ### 6.1 What Are Template Hints? Template hints display an **overlay** on the storefront showing: - The **file path** of the phtml template being rendered - The **block class** responsible for the template This is the fastest way to identify which template file to override. ### 6.2 Enabling Template Hints via CLI ```bash # Enable template hints for the frontend bin/magento dev:template-hints:enable # Flush cache after enabling bin/magento cache:flush ``` ```bash # Disable template hints bin/magento dev:template-hints:disable # Flush cache bin/magento cache:flush ``` > **Note:** `dev:template-hints:enable` accepts NO options — it always saves to the default scope. To scope hints to a specific store view, use the admin UI or `bin/magento config:set dev/debug/template_hints_storefront 1 --scope=stores --scope-code=default`. ### 6.3 Enabling via Admin UI **Stores -> Configuration -> Advanced -> Developer -> Debug** - *Enable Template Path Hints for Storefront* -> **Yes** - *Add Block Class Type to Hints* -> **Yes** (shows block class name too) > **Note:** In production mode, Developer settings may be restricted. Template hints are intended for **development/staging** environments only. ### 6.4 URL Parameter Hints (Best Practice) To avoid showing hints to all visitors, you can enable hints only when a URL parameter is present: In Admin under **Debug**: - *Enable Hints for Storefront with URL Parameter* -> **Yes** - *Parameter Value* -> `magento` (default) Then access the storefront with `?templatehints=magento` to see hints. ### 6.5 What the Overlay Shows ``` +-----------------------------------------------------+ | app/design/frontend/Vendor/MyTheme/ | <-- Template path | Magento_Catalog/templates/product/view.phtml | | Block: Magento\Catalog\Block\Product\View | <-- Block class +-----------------------------------------------------+ | [ Product content renders here ] | +-----------------------------------------------------+ ``` > **Exam focus:** `bin/magento dev:template-hints:enable` is the CLI command to show template file paths as overlays on the storefront. It requires a `cache:flush` after enabling to take effect. --- ## 7. Hands-On Walkthrough ### 7.1 Exercise: Override a Core Template with Correct Escaping **Goal:** Override `Magento_Catalog::product/view/description.phtml` in your theme and ensure all output is correctly escaped. **Step 1 — Enable template hints to find the template** ```bash bin/magento dev:template-hints:enable bin/magento cache:flush ``` Navigate to a product page and identify the description template path from the overlay. **Step 2 — Find the source template** ```bash find vendor/magento -name "description.phtml" -path "*/product/view/*" # Result: vendor/magento/module-catalog/view/frontend/templates/product/view/description.phtml ``` **Step 3 — Create the override directory and copy** ```bash mkdir -p app/design/frontend/Vendor/MyTheme/Magento_Catalog/templates/product/view/ cp vendor/magento/module-catalog/view/frontend/templates/product/view/description.phtml \ app/design/frontend/Vendor/MyTheme/Magento_Catalog/templates/product/view/description.phtml ``` **Step 4 — View the original template** ```php helper(Magento\Catalog\Helper\Output::class)->productAttribute( $block->getProduct(), $block->getProduct()->getDescription(), 'description' ) ?> ``` > **Key observation:** The real `description.phtml` is surprisingly minimal — a single expression. It uses `$this->helper()` (a Php engine method, not available on `$block`) and `/* @noEscape */` because the helper's `productAttribute()` method handles output processing internally. The block class is `Magento\Catalog\Block\Product\View\Description` (extends `Template`). **Step 5 — Create your customized override with proper escaping** ```php getProduct(); $description = $product->getDescription(); ?>
escapeHtml(__('Description')) ?>
escapeHtml( $description, ['p', 'br', 'strong', 'em', 'ul', 'ol', 'li', 'a', 'span', 'div'] ) ?>
getProductUrl(); ?> escapeHtml(__('View Full Details')) ?> getId(); ?>
getName(); ?>
``` **Step 6 — Clear cache and test** ```bash bin/magento cache:clean bin/magento cache:flush ``` Navigate to a product page. The overlay from template hints will confirm your theme template is now being used. **Step 7 — Disable template hints after testing** ```bash bin/magento dev:template-hints:disable bin/magento cache:flush ``` ### 7.2 Exercise: ViewModel in a Custom Block **Step 1 — Create the ViewModel** ```php scopeConfig = $scopeConfig; } public function getPromoMessage(): string { return (string) $this->scopeConfig->getValue( 'vendor_module/promo/message', \Magento\Store\Model\ScopeInterface::SCOPE_STORE ); } public function isPromoEnabled(): bool { return (bool) $this->scopeConfig->isSetFlag( 'vendor_module/promo/enabled', \Magento\Store\Model\ScopeInterface::SCOPE_STORE ); } } ``` **Step 2 — Inject via layout XML** ```xml Vendor\Module\ViewModel\ProductPromo ``` **Step 3 — Access in template** ```php getViewModel(); ?> isPromoEnabled()): ?>

escapeHtml($viewModel->getPromoMessage()) ?>

``` --- ## 8. Common Pitfalls & Tricky Exam Scenarios ### 8.1 `$this` vs `$block` Summary | Variable | Magento Version | What It Refers To | Method Calls | |---|---|---|---| | `$this` | Magento 1 | Block instance | Direct | | `$this` | Magento 2 | Template engine (`Php` class) | Proxied to block via `__call()` | | `$block` | Magento 2 | Block instance (**correct**) | Direct | > Key: `$this->someBlockMethod()` works in Magento 2 because `Php::__call()` forwards calls to the current block. But `$this->helper()` is engine-specific and NOT available on `$block`. ### 8.2 Escaping Gotchas Summary | Scenario | Wrong | Correct | |---|---|---| | Product name in `

` tag | `echo $name` | `$block->escapeHtml($name)` | | Product description (HTML content) | `$block->escapeHtml($desc)` | `$block->escapeHtml($desc, ['p','br',...])` or raw (trusted) | | URL in `href` attribute | `echo $url` | `$block->escapeUrl($url)` | | Value in `data-*` attribute | `$block->escapeHtml($val)` | `$block->escapeHtmlAttr($val)` | | Value in JS string | `echo $jsVal` | `$block->escapeJs($jsVal)` | | User GET parameter | `echo $param` | `$block->escapeHtml($param)` | ### 8.3 Override Path Matching A common exam trap: the theme directory structure must **exactly match** the module's `templates/` relative path. ``` Module: Magento_Checkout/view/frontend/templates/cart/item/default.phtml ^-- starts here Theme: Magento_Checkout/templates/cart/item/default.phtml ^-- starts here (no view/frontend/ in theme path) ``` > **Exam focus:** The `view/frontend/` portion is **NOT** included in the theme path. The theme path starts directly at `templates/`. ### 8.4 `escapeUrl()` Does Not Validate ```php escapeUrl($url); // outputs empty or stripped value // But escapeUrl does NOT validate that the URL is a real destination $url = 'http://malicious-site.com/steal'; echo $block->escapeUrl($url); // outputs the URL safely encoded but still links to malicious site // --> URL validation/whitelist is a SEPARATE concern from escaping ?> ``` ### 8.5 Template Identifier Format ```xml ``` ### 8.6 The `/* @noEscape */` Comment You may see this in Magento core templates: ```php getSomeHtmlContent() ?> ``` This is a **suppression comment** telling the static code analysis tool (PHPCS) that the developer has intentionally decided not to escape this output. It does **not** actually escape or protect anything — it's a documentation/linting annotation only. > **Exam focus:** `/* @noEscape */` is a PHPCS annotation to suppress the "output not escaped" warning. It provides zero security — the developer is asserting the content is already safe. --- ## 9. Quick-Reference Checklist ### Template File Locations - [ ] Module templates: `app/code/Vendor/Module/view/frontend/templates/` - [ ] Theme overrides: `app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/Magento_Module/templates/` - [ ] Theme path does **not** include `view/frontend/` — starts directly at `templates/` - [ ] Module name in theme path must exactly match (e.g., `Magento_Catalog`) ### Template Override Rules - [ ] Copy module template to matching path in theme — no XML changes needed - [ ] Relative path inside `templates/` must be identical in both locations - [ ] To assign a different template file, use layout XML `template` attribute on `` - [ ] `` is deprecated — use `template` attribute instead - [ ] Template identifier format: `ModuleName::path/to/template.phtml` ### Template API - [ ] `$block` = block instance in Magento 2 templates (**correct**) - [ ] `$this` = Php template engine; method calls are proxied to block via `__call()`; deprecated - [ ] `$this->helper()` = engine-specific method, NOT available on `$block` - [ ] ViewModels must implement `Magento\Framework\View\Element\Block\ArgumentInterface` - [ ] Inject ViewModel via layout XML as `xsi:type="object"` argument named `view_model` - [ ] Access ViewModel in template via `$block->getViewModel()` or `$block->getData('view_model')` ### Output Escaping (Security) - [ ] **Never echo raw user input** in any template - [ ] `escapeHtml()` — for text content inside HTML tags; encodes HTML entities (`<>`, `&`, `"`, `'`) - [ ] `escapeHtml()` on HTML content -> displays raw tags as text (**wrong use case**) - [ ] `escapeHtmlAttr()` — for values inside HTML attribute quotes - [ ] `escapeUrl()` — for URLs in `href`, `src`, `action`, `formaction`; strips dangerous protocols - [ ] `escapeUrl()` does NOT validate the URL destination — separate concern - [ ] `escapeJs()` — for PHP values embedded inside JavaScript string literals - [ ] `escapeCss()` — for values inside CSS contexts - [ ] `escapeHtml($content, ['p','br',...])` — allows specified HTML tags to pass through - [ ] `/* @noEscape */` = PHPCS linting annotation only; provides zero security ### Template Debugging - [ ] `bin/magento dev:template-hints:enable` — enables file path overlay on storefront (no options) - [ ] `bin/magento dev:template-hints:disable` — disables hints - [ ] Always run `bin/magento cache:flush` after toggling hints - [ ] Admin path: Stores -> Configuration -> Advanced -> Developer -> Debug - [ ] Admin field: "Add Block Class Type to Hints" shows block class in overlay - [ ] URL parameter mode available for selective hint display - [ ] Template hints are for development/staging only — not production ### Miscellaneous - [ ] `$block->getViewModel()` works via DataObject magic getter -> maps to `getData('view_model')` - [ ] Argument name in XML must be `view_model` (underscore) for `getViewModel()` to work - [ ] `$block->getRequest()` returns the HTTP request object (AbstractBlock:241) - [ ] `bin/magento cache:clean` + `cache:flush` required after template changes in some environments - [ ] Core templates should **never be edited directly** — always override in theme

flashcards.question: What is the correct directory path for overriding a module template in a Magento 2 theme?
flashcards.answer: To override a module template, copy it to app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/Magento_Module/templates/path/to/file.phtml. The view/frontend/ portion from the module path is NOT included in the theme path — the theme path starts directly at templates/. For example, vendor/magento/module-catalog/view/frontend/templates/product/view.phtml becomes Magento_Catalog/templates/product/view.phtml in the theme.
flashcards.hint: The theme path drops the view/frontend/ segment that exists in the module's structure.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between $block and $this in a Magento 2 phtml template?
flashcards.answer: $block is the actual block instance (e.g., Magento\Catalog\Block\Product\View) and is the correct variable to use in Magento 2. $this refers to the template engine (Magento\Framework\View\TemplateEngine\Php), not the block. However, $this works for block methods because Php::__call() proxies method calls to the current block. $this also has engine-specific methods like $this->helper() that are NOT available on $block.
flashcards.hint: One is the recommended approach pointing to the block instance, the other is the template engine with a proxy mechanism.

flashcards.question: What are the five output escaping methods available in Magento 2 templates, and when should each be used?
flashcards.answer: The five methods are: escapeHtml() for text content inside HTML tags, escapeHtmlAttr() for HTML attribute values, escapeUrl() for URLs in href/src/action attributes, escapeJs() for strings inside JavaScript string literals, and escapeCss() for values inside CSS contexts. Using the wrong method for the context can leave XSS vulnerabilities or cause incorrect rendering.
flashcards.hint: Each method corresponds to a specific output context in HTML — tag content, attributes, URLs, scripts, and styles.

flashcards.question: Why is it wrong to use escapeHtml() on product descriptions that contain HTML markup?
flashcards.answer:
escapeHtml() encodes ALL HTML entities, converting tags like

to <p>. When used on HTML content (like product descriptions), it displays the raw HTML tags as visible text instead of rendering them. For content that should render as HTML, either don't escape (if the source is trusted), or use escapeHtml() with an allowed tags array: $block->escapeHtml($content, ['p', 'br', 'strong', 'em']).
flashcards.hint: This method treats HTML tags as text to display, not as markup to render.

flashcards.question: Does overriding a template in a theme require any layout XML configuration?
flashcards.answer: No, template overrides in a theme do NOT require any layout XML changes. Simply copying the template file to the matching path in your theme directory is sufficient — Magento's file fallback system automatically picks the theme template over the module template. However, if you want to assign a completely different template file (not just override), you would use the template attribute on <referenceBlock> in layout XML.
flashcards.hint: The fallback mechanism handles it based on file placement alone — no XML declaration needed.

flashcards.question: What does escapeUrl() actually do, and what does it NOT do?
flashcards.answer: escapeUrl() strips dangerous protocols (javascript:, vbscript:, data:) using escapeScriptIdentifiers(), then passes the result through escapeHtml() to encode special characters. It does NOT validate whether the URL points to a safe or valid destination — a URL like http://malicious-site.com/steal will pass through safely encoded but still link to the malicious site. URL validation/whitelisting is a separate concern from escaping.
flashcards.hint: It sanitizes the URL string for safe embedding but doesn't verify the destination.

flashcards.question: How do you enable template hints via the CLI, and what do they display?
flashcards.answer: Run bin/magento dev:template-hints:enable followed by bin/magento cache:flush. Template hints display overlays on the storefront showing the file path of each phtml template being rendered and (optionally) the block class responsible. This command accepts no options — it always saves to the default scope. To scope hints to a specific store view, use the Admin UI or bin/magento config:set.
flashcards.hint: The CLI command is simple with no flags, and it requires a cache flush to take effect.

flashcards.question: What is the template identifier format used in Magento 2 layout XML?
flashcards.answer: The format is ModuleName::relative/path/from/templates/directory.phtml. For example, Magento_Catalog::product/view.phtml resolves to vendor/magento/module-catalog/view/frontend/templates/product/view.phtml (or the theme override if it exists). The :: notation maps the module name to the view/frontend/templates/ directory automatically.
flashcards.hint: The double-colon separates the module name from the relative template path.

flashcards.question: How does the ViewModel pattern access work in a phtml template, and why does getViewModel() work?
flashcards.answer: In the template, you access the ViewModel with $block->getViewModel() or $block->getData('view_model'). The magic getter getViewModel() works because Magento's DataObject base class generates get methods that map to getData() calls — getViewModel() translates to getData('view_model'). For this to work, the argument must be named 'view_model' (with underscore) in the layout XML.
flashcards.hint: The magic getter mechanism converts camelCase method names to underscore-separated data keys.

flashcards.question: What is the /* @noEscape */ comment annotation used for in Magento 2 templates?
flashcards.answer: /* @noEscape */ is a PHPCS (static code analysis) annotation that suppresses the 'output not escaped' warning. It is a documentation/linting annotation only — it provides zero actual security and does not escape or protect anything. The developer is asserting that the content is already safe or pre-sanitized. It should be used carefully and only when the output source is trusted.
flashcards.hint: This is for the code analysis tool, not for the browser or PHP runtime.

flashcards.question: What is the correct approach for changing a block's template to a different file (not just overriding the same path)?
flashcards.answer: Use the template attribute on <referenceBlock> in layout XML: <referenceBlock name="product.info" template="Magento_Catalog::product/custom_view.phtml"/>. The older <action method="setTemplate"> pattern is deprecated and should not be used. This approach assigns a completely different template file to an existing block, rather than overriding the same-path template in the theme.
flashcards.hint: A layout XML attribute on the reference instruction handles this — no deprecated action method needed.

flashcards.question: When using escapeHtmlAttr() versus escapeHtml(), what is the key difference in usage context?
flashcards.answer:
escapeHtml() is for text content inside HTML tags (e.g.,

escapeHtml($name) ?>

). escapeHtmlAttr() is for values inside HTML attribute quotes (e.g., class, data-*, title, alt attributes). escapeHtmlAttr() provides stricter encoding appropriate for the attribute context, handling single quotes and characters that can break out of attribute values. Using escapeHtml() for attributes is technically less secure.
flashcards.hint: The context determines which method to use — content between tags versus values inside attribute quotes.

flashcards.question: What is the template fallback resolution order in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: The fallback order is: 1) Theme (child) — app/design/frontend/Vendor/theme/Magento_Module/templates/, 2) Theme (parent) — walks up the theme hierarchy, 3) Module — app/code/Vendor/Module/view/frontend/templates/. The first match wins, meaning the theme copy completely replaces the module original with no merging. This is different from layout XML which merges across the chain.
flashcards.hint: Templates use a first-match-wins approach, starting from the most specific theme.

studyNotes.title: Day 6 — Block Architecture & ViewModel Pattern
studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2: Block Architecture & ViewModel Pattern
## Study Notes — Week 1: Theme Structure, Layout XML & Templates

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Block Class Hierarchy](#1-block-class-hierarchy)
2. [AbstractBlock — Core Methods](#2-abstractblock--core-methods)
3. [Template Block — Rendering Pipeline](#3-template-block--rendering-pipeline)
4. [Block Lifecycle & Hook Methods](#4-block-lifecycle--hook-methods)
5. [Child Block Relationships](#5-child-block-relationships)
6. [Block Caching](#6-block-caching)
7. [Cache Types: block_html vs full_page](#7-cache-types-block_html-vs-full_page)
8. [ViewModel Pattern](#8-viewmodel-pattern)
9. [Injecting ViewModel via Layout XML](#9-injecting-viewmodel-via-layout-xml)
10. [Using ViewModel in a PHTML Template](#10-using-viewmodel-in-a-phtml-template)
11. [Separation of Concerns — Why ViewModel Matters](#11-separation-of-concerns--why-viewmodel-matters)
12. [Hands-On: Full Implementation Walkthrough](#12-hands-on-full-implementation-walkthrough)
13. [Common Traps & Exam Gotchas](#13-common-traps--exam-gotchas)
14. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Block Class Hierarchy

```
Magento\Framework\DataObject
        |
Magento\Framework\View\Element\AbstractBlock
        |
        +-- Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template
                |
                +-- Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template\Links
                +-- Magento\Catalog\Block\Product\View
                +-- Your\Module\Block\MyBlock   (custom)
                ... (hundreds of other concrete blocks)
```

| Class | Package | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `DataObject` | `magento/framework` | Magic getters/setters, `__call()` method |
| `AbstractBlock` | `magento/framework` | Base class — layout, caching, child blocks |
| `Template` | `magento/framework` | Adds PHTML template rendering |
| Custom blocks | your module | Business-specific data fetching |

**Exam focus:**
- `AbstractBlock` extends `DataObject` and implements `BlockInterface` — the magic `__call()` method (getters/setters) is inherited from `DataObject`
- `Template` *extends* `AbstractBlock` — it does **not** replace it
- Every block that renders a `.phtml` file **must** extend `Template` (or a subclass)
- `AbstractBlock` alone has **no** concept of a template file

---

## 2. AbstractBlock — Core Methods

```php
<?php
// Magento\Framework\View\Element\AbstractBlock (simplified)

abstract class AbstractBlock extends \Magento\Framework\DataObject implements BlockInterface
{
    // Called by layout after layout XML is fully processed
    protected function _prepareLayout() { return $this; }

    // Called just before rendering starts (inside _loadCache)
    protected function _beforeToHtml() { return $this; }

    // Override in descendants to produce HTML — NOT abstract, returns '' by default
    protected function _toHtml(): string { return ''; }

    // Public entry point — dispatches events, calls _loadCache() (which handles _beforeToHtml + _toHtml + caching), then _afterToHtml()
    public function toHtml(): string {}

    // Retrieve rendered HTML of a named child block
    public function getChildHtml(string $alias = '', bool $useCache = true): string {}

    // Magic getter — inherited from DataObject, calls getData('some_key') when you call getSomeKey()
    // public function __call(string $method, array $args) {}  <-- lives in DataObject
}
```

**Exam focus:**
- `_prepareLayout()` fires **after** the layout XML tree is fully built — safe to call `getLayout()` here
- `_beforeToHtml()` returns `$this` by convention, but the return value is **not used** by the framework — `_loadCache()` calls it as `$this->_beforeToHtml()` and discards the result
- `_toHtml()` is **not abstract** — it's a concrete protected method that returns an empty string by default. Subclasses override it.
- `_toHtml()` is **protected** — external code calls `toHtml()` (public wrapper)
- `getChildHtml($alias)` uses the **alias** defined in layout XML, not the block name

---

## 3. Template Block — Rendering Pipeline

`Template` adds the ability to associate a `.phtml` file and render it.

```php
<?php
// Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template (simplified)

class Template extends AbstractBlock
{
    // Returns the path to the current template file
    public function getTemplate(): string {}

    // Sets the template path (can also be set via layout XML)
    public function setTemplate(string $template): self {}

    // Overrides AbstractBlock::_toHtml()
    // Resolves template file, extracts $block = $this, includes the file
    protected function _toHtml(): string
    {
        // 1. Check if template is set
        // 2. Resolve full filesystem path via TemplateEnginePool
        // 3. Include the .phtml file with $block in scope
    }
}
```

### Template Path Resolution Order

```
1. Module override in current theme
   app/design/frontend/<Vendor>/<theme>/<Module_Name>/templates/

2. Parent theme (walks theme hierarchy)
   app/design/frontend/<Vendor>/<parent-theme>/<Module_Name>/templates/

3. Module fallback
   app/code/<Vendor>/<Module>/view/frontend/templates/
```

**Exam focus:**
- Inside a `.phtml`, `$block` is **always** the block object (`Template` instance or subclass)
- `getTemplate()` returns a path like `Vendor_Module::path/to/file.phtml`
- The `::` notation maps `Vendor_Module` → `view/frontend/templates/`

---

## 4. Block Lifecycle & Hook Methods

```
Layout XML parsed
      |
      v
Block objects instantiated (DI / ObjectManager)
      |
      v
_prepareLayout() called on each block
      |
      v
toHtml() triggered (by parent block or layout output)
      |
      +---> Event: view_block_abstract_to_html_before
      |
      +---> _loadCache():
      |        |
      |        +--- If NOT cacheable (lifetime === null):
      |        |      _beforeToHtml() → _toHtml() → return HTML
      |        |
      |        +--- If cacheable (lifetime > 0):
      |               Cache lookup → if HIT → return cached HTML
      |                            → if MISS → _beforeToHtml() → _toHtml()
      |                                      → Cache store → return HTML
      |
      +---> _afterToHtml($html)
      |
      +---> Event: view_block_abstract_to_html_after
      |
      v
HTML returned to caller
```

### `_prepareLayout()` — Typical Use Cases

```php
<?php

namespace Vendor\Module\Block;

use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template;

class MyBlock extends Template
{
    protected function _prepareLayout(): self
    {
        parent::_prepareLayout(); // Always call parent first!

        // Safe to interact with layout here
        $this->pageConfig->getTitle()->set(__('My Page Title'));

        // Add breadcrumbs, set head metadata, etc.
        if ($breadcrumbs = $this->getLayout()->getBlock('breadcrumbs')) {
            $breadcrumbs->addCrumb('home', [
                'label' => __('Home'),
                'link'  => $this->getBaseUrl(),
            ]);
        }

        return $this;
    }
}
```

**Exam focus:**
- Always call `parent::_prepareLayout()` — omitting it breaks the chain
- **Do NOT** call `getChildHtml()` inside `_prepareLayout()` — child blocks may not be ready
- `_prepareLayout()` is called **once** per block per request

---

## 5. Child Block Relationships

### Layout XML Definition

```xml
<!-- app/code/Vendor/Module/view/frontend/layout/catalog_product_view.xml -->
<referenceContainer name="content">
    <block class="Vendor\Module\Block\Parent" name="vendor.parent" template="Vendor_Module::parent.phtml">
        <block class="Vendor\Module\Block\Child" name="vendor.child" as="child_alias"
               template="Vendor_Module::child.phtml"/>
    </block>
</referenceContainer>
```

### Calling Child Block in PHTML

```php
<?php
// vendor/module/view/frontend/templates/parent.phtml

/** @var \Vendor\Module\Block\Parent $block */

// Renders the child block by its 'as' alias
echo $block->getChildHtml('child_alias');

// Renders ALL direct children in defined order (empty string or no argument)
echo $block->getChildHtml('');

// Renders children OF a child block (grandchildren) — NOT the same as getChildHtml()
echo $block->getChildChildHtml('child_alias');

// Get child block object without rendering
$child = $block->getChildBlock('child_alias');
```

**Exam focus:**
- `getChildHtml()` uses the **`as` attribute** (alias), NOT the `name` attribute
- If `as` is omitted, the alias defaults to the `name` value
- `getChildHtml('')` (empty string) renders **all** direct children
- `getChildChildHtml($alias)` renders the **grandchildren** (children of the child identified by `$alias`) — do not confuse with `getChildHtml()`

---

## 6. Block Caching

Block caching is controlled by **caching methods** in your block class. To participate in tag-based invalidation, a block must implement `Magento\Framework\DataObject\IdentityInterface`.

### The Caching Methods

```php
<?php

namespace Vendor\Module\Block;

use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template;
use Magento\Framework\DataObject\IdentityInterface;

class CachedBlock extends Template implements IdentityInterface
{
    /**
     * Cache lifetime in seconds.
     * null  = NOT cached (default — block renders every request)
     * 0     = NOT cached (enters cache path but _saveCache returns false)
     * 3600  = cached for 1 hour
     *
     * NOTE: This method is PROTECTED, not public.
     */
    protected function getCacheLifetime(): ?int
    {
        return 3600;
    }

    /**
     * Unique string identifier for this block's cached content.
     * Must be unique per distinct rendered output.
     */
    public function getCacheKey(): string
    {
        return 'vendor_module_myblock_' . $this->getData('product_id');
    }

    /**
     * Array of parts used to BUILD the cache key.
     * Magento sha256-hashes this array to produce the final key.
     * Prefer this over getCacheKey() — safer and more composable.
     */
    public function getCacheKeyInfo(): array
    {
        return [
            'VENDOR_MODULE_MYBLOCK',          // static prefix
            $this->_storeManager->getStore()->getId(),  // store scope
            $this->getData('product_id'),     // content-differentiating data
            (int)$this->customerSession->isLoggedIn(),  // vary by login state
        ];
    }

    /**
     * Cache tags for TAG-BASED invalidation.
     * Defined by IdentityInterface — blocks MUST implement this interface
     * to participate in tag-based cache invalidation.
     * When a product is saved, Magento invalidates all blocks
     * tagged with that product's tag — they are re-rendered next request.
     */
    public function getIdentities(): array
    {
        return [
            \Magento\Catalog\Model\Product::CACHE_TAG . '_' . $this->getData('product_id'),
            \Magento\Catalog\Model\Category::CACHE_TAG,
        ];
    }
}
```

### Caching Method Decision Matrix

| Method | Returns | Visibility | Typical Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `getCacheLifetime()` | `int\|bool\|null` | **protected** | Control TTL — `null`=not cached, `0`=not cached, `N`=N seconds |
| `getCacheKey()` | `string` | public | Manual unique key (less preferred) |
| `getCacheKeyInfo()` | `array` | public | Composable key parts (preferred; merge with parent) |
| `getIdentities()` | `array` of tags | public | Tag-based invalidation (requires `IdentityInterface`) |

**Exam focus:**
- `getCacheLifetime()` returning **`null`** = **NOT cached** — `_loadCache()` bypasses the cache entirely when lifetime is null
- `getCacheLifetime()` returning **`0`** = **NOT cached** — `_saveCache()` returns false when `!$this->getCacheLifetime()` is truthy
- `getCacheLifetime()` returning a **positive integer** = cached for that many seconds
- `getCacheLifetime()` is **`protected`**, not public
- If `getCacheLifetime()` is not overridden, the parent returns `null` → **NOT cached by default** — blocks must explicitly opt in to caching
- `getCacheKeyInfo()` is **preferred** over `getCacheKey()` — Magento sha256-hashes the array internally
- `getIdentities()` requires implementing `Magento\Framework\DataObject\IdentityInterface` — it is NOT a method on AbstractBlock itself

---

## 7. Cache Types: `block_html` vs `full_page`

```
+---------------------------+  +---------------------------+
|        block_html         |  |         full_page          |
|---------------------------|  |---------------------------|
| Cache type: block_html    |  | Cache type: full_page     |
| Scope: individual block   |  | Scope: entire HTTP resp.  |
| Tags: block identities    |  | Tags: entity tags (prod.) |
| Lifetime: getCacheLifetime|  | Lifetime: FPC config      |
| Bypassed by: hole-punch   |  | Bypassed by: private ESI  |
+---------------------------+  +---------------------------+
            |                              |
            v                              v
  Stored in: cache backend       Stored in: Varnish / cache
  (Redis / File)                 backend (Redis / File)
```

| Feature | `block_html` | `full_page` |
|---|---|---|
| Cache type code | `block_html` | `full_page` |
| What is cached | Block HTML fragment | Entire page response |
| Invalidation method | `getIdentities()` tags | Entity save events |
| Developer control | Block class methods | HTTP headers + Varnish VCL |
| Private content | N/A | Uses private content API |
| Flush command | `cache:clean block_html` | `cache:clean full_page` |

```bash
# Flush only block HTML cache
bin/magento cache:clean block_html

# Flush only Full Page Cache
bin/magento cache:clean full_page

# Flush both
bin/magento cache:clean block_html full_page
```

**Exam focus:**
- These are **two separate** cache systems — flushing FPC does **not** flush `block_html`
- A block implementing `IdentityInterface` with `getIdentities()` participates in **both** caching systems
- `block_html` stores **rendered fragments**; `full_page` stores **assembled pages**
- Hole-punching (private content via `customer-data`) bypasses FPC, not `block_html`

---

## 8. ViewModel Pattern

### The Problem ViewModel Solves

```
BAD PATTERN (mixing concerns):
+----------------------------------+
|  Block\MyBlock extends Template  |
|  - _prepareLayout()              |
|  - getProductCollection()  <-- business logic in block = bad
|  - getFormattedPrice()     <-- presentation logic mixed in
|  - getCacheKeyInfo()             |
|  - toHtml()                      |
+----------------------------------+

GOOD PATTERN (separated concerns):
+----------------------------------+    +---------------------------+
|  Block\MyBlock extends Template  |    |  ViewModel\MyViewModel    |
|  - _prepareLayout()              |    |  - getProductCollection() |
|  - getCacheKeyInfo()             |    |  - getFormattedPrice()    |
|  - toHtml()                      |    |  implements               |
|                                  |    |  ArgumentInterface        |
+----------------------------------+    +---------------------------+
         |                                         |
         +------- injected via layout XML ---------+
         |
         v
   phtml template uses $block->getViewModel()->someMethod()
```

### ViewModel Class Structure

```php
<?php

namespace Vendor\Module\ViewModel;

use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Block\ArgumentInterface;
use Magento\Catalog\Api\ProductRepositoryInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Pricing\Helper\Data as PriceHelper;

class ProductInfo implements ArgumentInterface  // <-- REQUIRED interface
{
    private ProductRepositoryInterface $productRepository;
    private PriceHelper $priceHelper;

    public function __construct(
        ProductRepositoryInterface $productRepository,
        PriceHelper $priceHelper
    ) {
        // Normal DI constructor injection — no ObjectManager!
        $this->productRepository = $productRepository;
        $this->priceHelper = $priceHelper;
    }

    /**
     * Business logic lives here — NOT in the block
     */
    public function getProductById(int $productId): ?\Magento\Catalog\Api\Data\ProductInterface
    {
        try {
            return $this->productRepository->getById($productId);
        } catch (\Magento\Framework\Exception\NoSuchEntityException $e) {
            return null;
        }
    }

    public function getFormattedPrice(float $price): string
    {
        return $this->priceHelper->currency($price, true, false);
    }

    public function getFeaturedProducts(): array
    {
        // Complex collection logic here — keeps block clean
        return [];
    }
}
```

**Exam focus:**
- ViewModel **must implement** `Magento\Framework\View\Element\Block\ArgumentInterface`
- `ArgumentInterface` is a **marker interface** — it has **no methods** to implement
- ViewModel has **no rendering responsibility** — no `toHtml()`, no template access
- ViewModel uses **constructor DI** just like any other service class
- ViewModel is **not** a block — it cannot call `getLayout()`, `getChildHtml()`, etc.

## 9. Injecting ViewModel via Layout XML

```xml
<!-- app/code/Vendor/Module/view/frontend/layout/cms_index_index.xml -->
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<page xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
      xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:View/Layout/etc/page_configuration.xsd">
    <body>
        <referenceContainer name="content">
            <block class="Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template"
                   name="vendor.module.myblock"
                   template="Vendor_Module::my_template.phtml">
                <arguments>
                    <!--
                        'view_model' is the conventional argument name.
                        type="object" tells Magento to instantiate via DI.
                        The value is the fully-qualified class name.
                        Note: Magento's own Template.php docblock uses 'viewModel' (camelCase).
                        Both 'view_model' and 'viewModel' work — the community commonly uses snake_case.
                    -->
                    <argument name="view_model" xsi:type="object">
                        Vendor\Module\ViewModel\ProductInfo
                    </argument>

                    <!-- You can inject additional arguments too -->
                    <argument name="product_id" xsi:type="string">42</argument>
                    <argument name="show_price" xsi:type="boolean">true</argument>
                </arguments>
            </block>
        </referenceContainer>
    </body>
</page>
```

### Argument Types Reference

| `xsi:type` | PHP type | Example value |
|---|---|---|
| `string` | `string` | `hello world` |
| `boolean` | `bool` | `true` / `false` |
| `number` | `int`/`float` | `42` |
| `object` | class instance | `Vendor\Class\Name` |
| `array` | `array` | Nested `<item>` elements |
| `null` | `null` | (empty) |
| `init_parameter` | constant value | `Magento\Store\Model\Store::DEFAULT_STORE_ID` |

**Exam focus:**
- The argument name `view_model` is **conventional**, not enforced — but it's the community standard
- `type="object"` causes Magento to resolve via the **DI container** (respects `di.xml` preferences)
- Arguments defined here are retrieved via `$block->getData('view_model')` OR `$block->getViewModel()`
- The magic getter `getViewModel()` maps to `getData('view_model')` — underscore/camelCase conversion applies (inherited from `DataObject::__call()`)

## 10. Using ViewModel in a PHTML Template

```php
<?php
// app/code/Vendor/Module/view/frontend/templates/my_template.phtml

/**
 * @var \Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template $block
 * @var \Vendor\Module\ViewModel\ProductInfo $viewModel
 */

// Method 1: getViewModel() — magic getter for 'view_model' argument (via DataObject::__call)
$viewModel = $block->getViewModel();

// Method 2: getData() — explicit, works for any argument name
$viewModel = $block->getData('view_model');

// Method 3: get data values set in layout XML
$productId = (int)$block->getData('product_id');     // from xsi:type="string"
$showPrice = (bool)$block->getData('show_price');    // from xsi:type="boolean"

// Use ViewModel methods — business logic stays out of template
$product = $viewModel->getProductById($productId);
?>

<?php if ($product): ?>
<div class="product-info">
    <h2><?= $block->escapeHtml($product->getName()) ?></h2>

    <?php if ($showPrice): ?>
    <span class="price">
        <?= /* @noEscape */ $viewModel->getFormattedPrice((float)$product->getPrice()) ?>
    </span>
    <?php endif; ?>
</div>
<?php endif; ?>
```

### Escaping Rules (Exam Critical)

```php
<?php
// ALWAYS escape user-facing or database content
echo $block->escapeHtml($userInput);           // for HTML context
echo $block->escapeHtmlAttr($attributeValue);  // for HTML attribute values
echo $block->escapeUrl($url);                  // for href/src attributes
echo $block->escapeJs($jsString);              // for inline JavaScript
echo $block->escapeCss($cssString);            // for inline CSS

// @noEscape annotation — use when output is pre-sanitized HTML
echo /* @noEscape */ $viewModel->getFormattedPrice($price);  // returns safe HTML
?>
```

**Exam focus:**
- `$block` is **always** available in `.phtml` — it is the block instance itself
- `$block->getViewModel()` is the **magic getter** equivalent of `$block->getData('view_model')` — the magic getter lives in `DataObject`, which `AbstractBlock` extends
- **Never** call business logic directly in the template — use ViewModel methods
- `/* @noEscape */` tells static analysis the output is safe — still use it carefully

## 11. Separation of Concerns — Why ViewModel Matters

### Anti-Pattern (Logic in Block)

```php
<?php
// BAD: Business logic inside a block
namespace Vendor\Module\Block;

use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template;
use Magento\Catalog\Model\ResourceModel\Product\CollectionFactory;

class ProductList extends Template
{
    private CollectionFactory $collectionFactory;

    public function __construct(
        Template\Context $context,
        CollectionFactory $collectionFactory,  // injected into block directly
        array $data = []
    ) {
        $this->collectionFactory = $collectionFactory;
        parent::__construct($context, $data);
    }

    // BAD: Data retrieval logic lives in block
    public function getProducts(): array
    {
        $collection = $this->collectionFactory->create();
        $collection->addAttributeToSelect('*')
                   ->addFieldToFilter('status', 1)
                   ->setPageSize(10);
        return $collection->getItems();
    }
}
```

### Correct Pattern (ViewModel)

```php
<?php
// GOOD: Block stays thin — only rendering concern
namespace Vendor\Module\Block;

use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template;

class ProductList extends Template
{
    // Block constructor only needs Context — no business dependencies
    public function __construct(
        Template\Context $context,
        array $data = []
    ) {
        parent::__construct($context, $data);
    }

    // Override only layout/cache related methods if needed
    public function getCacheKeyInfo(): array
    {
        return [
            'VENDOR_MODULE_PRODUCT_LIST',
            $this->_storeManager->getStore()->getId(),
        ];
    }
}
```

```php
<?php
// GOOD: All business logic in ViewModel
namespace Vendor\Module\ViewModel;

use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Block\ArgumentInterface;
use Magento\Catalog\Model\ResourceModel\Product\CollectionFactory;

class ProductList implements ArgumentInterface
{
    private CollectionFactory $collectionFactory;

    public function __construct(CollectionFactory $collectionFactory)
    {
        $this->collectionFactory = $collectionFactory;
    }

    public function getProducts(): array
    {
        $collection = $this->collectionFactory->create();
        $collection->addAttributeToSelect('*')
                   ->addFieldToFilter('status', 1)
                   ->setPageSize(10);
        return $collection->getItems();
    }
}
```

**Exam focus:**
- ViewModel keeps the block's **constructor signature minimal** — easier to override via plugins/preferences
- Logic in a block class **cannot be cleanly unit tested** without rendering context
- ViewModel is a **plain PHP class** — fully testable with PHPUnit, no Magento bootstrap needed
- This pattern is the **Magento recommended approach** since Magento 2.2

### Directory Structure

```
app/code/Vendor/Module/
|-- etc/
|   +-- module.xml
|-- registration.php

### Step 1: ViewModel Class

```php
<?php
// app/code/Vendor/Module/ViewModel/HelloViewModel.php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vendor\Module\ViewModel;

use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Block\ArgumentInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Stdlib\DateTime\TimezoneInterface;

class HelloViewModel implements ArgumentInterface
{
    private TimezoneInterface $timezone;

    public function __construct(TimezoneInterface $timezone)
    {
        $this->timezone = $timezone;
    }

    public function getGreeting(): string
    {
        $hour = (int)$this->timezone->date()->format('G');

        if ($hour < 12) {
            return 'Good morning';
        } elseif ($hour < 18) {
            return 'Good afternoon';
        } else {
            return 'Good evening';
        }
    }

    public function getCurrentDate(): string
    {
        return $this->timezone->date()->format('l, F j, Y');
    }
}
```

### Step 2: Block Class (thin — minimal responsibility)

```php
<?php
// app/code/Vendor/Module/Block/HelloBlock.php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vendor\Module\Block;

use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template;
use Magento\Framework\DataObject\IdentityInterface;

class HelloBlock extends Template implements IdentityInterface
{
    /**
     * Block only handles caching and layout integration.
     * Data retrieval = ViewModel's job.
     *
     * NOTE: getCacheLifetime() is PROTECTED.
     */
    protected function getCacheLifetime(): ?int
    {
        return 300; // 5 minutes
    }

    public function getCacheKeyInfo(): array
    {
        return [
            'VENDOR_MODULE_HELLO',
            $this->_storeManager->getStore()->getId(),
        ];
    }

    /**
     * getIdentities() requires implementing IdentityInterface.
     */
    public function getIdentities(): array
    {
        return ['vendor_module_hello'];
    }
}
```

**Exam focus:**
- `module:enable` → `setup:upgrade` → `cache:clean` is the standard new module workflow
- In **developer mode**, static content deploy is automatic — not needed for `.phtml` changes
