flashcards.answer: A mixin file must return a function that accepts the target module and returns the modified version: define([], function(){ return function(Target){ return Target.extend({...}); }; }). The most common mistake is forgetting the outer function wrapper — returning the extended component directly instead of a function that receives the target. Without the wrapper, the target module is not in scope.
flashcards.hint: There must be two levels of return — the outer function and the inner extension.

flashcards.question: How do observableArray mutations differ from regular array mutations in Knockout.js?
flashcards.answer: Observable array mutations (.push(), .pop(), .remove()) must be called on the observable directly (this.cartItems.push(item)), not on the unwrapped array. Calling mutations on this.cartItems() returns the plain JS array, and pushing to it would NOT trigger UI updates. Also, .remove() is a KO-specific method not available on plain arrays — it accepts a value or predicate function.
flashcards.hint: Call array methods on the observable function itself, not on the unwrapped result.

flashcards.question: Why must ko.computed() receive 'this' as a second argument?
flashcards.answer: When using 'this' inside a computed function to access observables (e.g., this.firstName() + this.lastName()), the second argument binds the correct 'this' context. Without it, 'this' inside the function body would be undefined or window, causing the computed to fail. The pattern is ko.computed(function(){ return this.prop(); }, this). For ko.pureComputed with read/write, use the 'owner' property instead.
flashcards.hint: JavaScript function context is not automatically inherited — it must be explicitly bound.

flashcards.question: What are the links, imports, and exports properties in a uiElement component, and how do they differ?
flashcards.answer: These are component communication mechanisms in defaults. 'links' provides two-way synchronization between this component's property and another component's property. 'imports' provides one-way sync FROM another component TO this component. 'exports' provides one-way sync FROM this component TO another. They use the syntax '${ $.provider }:data.value' to reference other components' properties by name.
flashcards.hint: Three communication directions: bidirectional, inbound-only, and outbound-only.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between the 'if' and 'visible' bindings in Knockout.js?
flashcards.answer: The 'visible' binding shows or hides an element using CSS display (the element stays in the DOM). The 'if' binding conditionally adds or removes the element from the DOM entirely — when false, the element and its children are completely removed. 'ifnot' is the inverse of 'if'. Use 'visible' for simple show/hide toggling; use 'if' when you need to prevent rendering or release resources.
flashcards.hint: One toggles CSS visibility; the other physically adds or removes DOM nodes.

studyNotes.title: Day 11 — jQuery Widgets & JS Translations

flashcards.question: What is the difference between _create and _init in a jQuery widget?
flashcards.answer: _create runs exactly ONCE when the widget is first instantiated — use it for DOM manipulation, event binding, and one-time setup. _init runs after _create AND on every subsequent re-initialization — use it for state reset and rendering based on current options. If you put event binding in _init, you risk binding the same listener multiple times. Always bind events in _create.
flashcards.hint: One is a one-shot constructor; the other is called repeatedly on re-initialization.

flashcards.question: What are the differences between data-mage-init and x-magento-init for widget initialization?
flashcards.answer: data-mage-init is an HTML attribute on the target element (this.element = that element), uses single quotes as outer delimiter, and is for one element at a time. x-magento-init is a <script type='text/x-magento-init'> tag that uses a CSS selector to target elements, works with dynamically loaded content, supports the '*' selector for non-DOM components, and can match multiple elements with one declaration.
flashcards.hint: One is an attribute on the element; the other is a separate script tag with a selector.

flashcards.question: How do JavaScript translations work in Magento 2, and what functions are used?
flashcards.answer: JS translations use $.mage.__('string') or $t('string') (from mage/translate module) — both are functionally equivalent. They look up the string in an in-memory dictionary populated from js-translation.json. If the key is missing or the value is empty, the original string is returned without error. Translation keys are case-sensitive and must exactly match.
flashcards.hint: Two equivalent functions read from a JSON dictionary file, with graceful fallback to the original string.

flashcards.question: How is js-translation.json generated and where is it located?
flashcards.answer: js-translation.json is generated during Static Content Deploy (bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy). It is located at pub/static/{area}/{vendor}/{theme}/{locale}/js-translation.json. Changes to translation CSV files require re-running SCD to update the JSON. The file contains a flat key-value JSON object mapping original strings to their translations.
flashcards.hint: It is a build artifact generated from CSV source files during deployment.

flashcards.question: What are the key differences between PHP translations and JavaScript translations in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: PHP __() reads from an in-memory dictionary (module CSVs -> language packs -> theme CSVs -> DB translation table, with DB having highest priority). JS $.mage.__() reads from js-translation.json (a flat JSON file). They are completely independent systems — DB changes do NOT affect JS translations. PHP translations are live (no deploy needed); JS translations require SCD re-run.
flashcards.hint: Different storage mechanisms, different update processes, no cross-pollination between them.

flashcards.question: What does the x-magento-init '*' selector do?
flashcards.answer: The '*' selector in x-magento-init initializes a JavaScript component without binding it to any specific DOM element. It is used for pure JavaScript components that do not need a DOM reference — such as global analytics scripts, page-level configuration, or data models. The component receives null or no element reference instead of a jQuery-wrapped DOM node.
flashcards.hint: Sometimes a component needs to run globally without being attached to any specific HTML element.

flashcards.question: Why should you use this._on() instead of $(el).on() for event binding in jQuery widgets?
flashcards.answer: this._on() automatically cleans up event bindings when the widget is destroyed (_destroy), preventing memory leaks. It also automatically binds the 'this' context to the widget instance without needing manual .bind(this). Both support event delegation. Using raw $(el).on() requires manual cleanup and explicit context binding, making it error-prone.
flashcards.hint: The widget factory method handles cleanup and context automatically.

flashcards.question: How do you trigger re-processing of widget initializations after injecting AJAX content?
flashcards.answer: After injecting new HTML via AJAX, fire the 'contentUpdated' event on the parent container: $container.trigger('contentUpdated'). This triggers Magento to re-scan the new content and apply widget bindings from both data-mage-init attributes and x-magento-init script blocks within the injected HTML. Without this event, dynamically added widgets will not initialize.
flashcards.hint: A specific jQuery event tells Magento to look for new widget declarations in updated DOM content.

flashcards.question: What is the correct JSON quoting format for data-mage-init attributes?
flashcards.answer: data-mage-init must use single quotes as the HTML attribute delimiter with standard JSON (double quotes) inside: data-mage-init='{"Module/js/widget": {"option": "value"}}'. Using double quotes outside will break the HTML attribute parsing. You can also use HTML entities (") for inner quotes, but the single-quote approach is standard.
flashcards.hint: HTML attributes normally use double quotes, so the JSON wrapper must use the other kind.

flashcards.question: How does the i18n:collect-phrases command work, and what does the --magento flag change?
flashcards.answer: bin/magento i18n:collect-phrases scans files for translatable strings. Without --magento, it requires a directory argument and produces a flat CSV. With --magento, it scans the entire Magento root directory and enables contextual (module-aware) output. Both modes scan PHP, PHTML, JS, HTML, and XML files — the --magento flag does NOT control which file types are scanned, only the scope and output format.
flashcards.hint: The flag changes the scan scope and output format, not which file types are included.

flashcards.question: Why must _setOption always call this._super(key, value) in a jQuery widget?
flashcards.answer: _setOption handles runtime option updates. Calling this._super(key, value) ensures the jQuery UI internal option store is updated before your custom logic runs. Without it, the option change is not properly recorded, and this.options will still hold the old value. After calling _super, you can add custom logic like re-rendering the widget.
flashcards.hint: The parent method updates the internal options storage that your widget relies on.

flashcards.question: How are jQuery widget instances stored and accessed after initialization?
flashcards.answer: Widget instances are stored in jQuery's .data() using a camelCase version of the namespaced name: mage.widgetName becomes 'mageWidgetName', vendor.greetingWidget becomes 'vendorGreetingWidget'. You can access the instance via $(el).data('mageWidgetName') or call public methods using the plugin syntax: $(el).widgetName('methodName', args).
flashcards.hint: The namespace and widget name are concatenated into camelCase for the data key.

flashcards.question: What is the widget namespace convention in Magento 2, and why does it matter?
flashcards.answer: Widgets are declared as $.widget('namespace.widgetName', {...}). Core Magento widgets use the 'mage' namespace (e.g., mage.accordion), while custom widgets should use a vendor-specific namespace. The namespace is not decorative — it defines the jQuery plugin name. mage.accordion becomes callable as $(el).accordion(). The namespace prevents collisions between different vendors' widgets.
flashcards.hint: The first part of the dot-separated name controls how the widget is accessed as a jQuery plugin.

flashcards.question: What happens when a translation key is missing or has an empty string value in js-translation.json?
flashcards.answer: Both cases return the original string unchanged — no error or exception is thrown. If 'Cancel' maps to an empty string '' in the JSON, $.mage.__('Cancel') returns 'Cancel' (the original). If a key is not in the JSON at all, the original string is also returned. This graceful fallback means untranslated strings display in their original language rather than causing errors.
flashcards.hint: The translation system has a silent fallback that always produces usable output.

flashcards.question: What is the full translation pipeline from writing JS code to a translated string appearing in the browser?
flashcards.answer: 1) Developer writes $.mage.__('My Phrase') in JS code. 2) Run i18n:collect-phrases to discover strings. 3) Translator fills in the CSV: 'My Phrase','Ma Phrase'. 4) Place CSV in module i18n/ directory. 5) Run setup:static-content:deploy for the target locale. 6) js-translation.json is generated with the mapping. 7) When a user visits the site in that locale, $.mage.__('My Phrase') returns the translation.
flashcards.hint: Seven steps from code to browser, involving collection, translation, deployment, and runtime lookup.

studyNotes.title: Day 12 — JavaScript Architecture & Module Best Practices

flashcards.question: What is the difference between define() and require() in Magento 2's AMD/RequireJS system?
flashcards.answer: define() creates a reusable module that exports a value (object, function, etc.) and can be consumed by other modules. require() consumes modules for one-time use without creating a named export. define() is used for libraries and components, while require() is used for entry-point code that just needs to run.
flashcards.hint: One creates something reusable, the other just runs code that depends on modules.

flashcards.question: Where does the requirejs-config.js file live in a Magento 2 module, and what configuration options does it support?
flashcards.answer: The requirejs-config.js file lives in view/frontend/ (or view/adminhtml/) within a module. It supports map (alias to path mapping), paths (override file paths), shim (wrap non-AMD libraries with deps and exports), and config.mixins (extend existing JS components). All requirejs-config.js files from modules and themes are merged at deploy time with theme configs winning.
flashcards.hint: Think about the view directory structure and the four main configuration keys.

flashcards.question: Why does Magento coding standard require 'use strict' at the top of every AMD factory function?
flashcards.answer: 'use strict' prevents accidental global variable creation by throwing a ReferenceError when an undeclared variable is assigned. Without it, a typo like mistypedVar = 'value' silently creates window.mistypedVar, polluting the global scope. This enforces proper variable declaration and catches bugs early during development.
flashcards.hint: Consider what happens when you accidentally assign to a variable that was never declared with var/let/const.

flashcards.question: How does dependency injection work in Magento 2 JavaScript AMD modules, and what is the critical rule about dependency array position?
flashcards.answer: Dependencies are declared in an array as the first argument to define(), and the AMD loader injects them as arguments to the factory function. The critical rule is that argument positions must match dependency array positions — argument #1 receives dependency #1 regardless of the argument name. If you have fewer arguments than dependencies, the extra dependencies become undefined.
flashcards.hint: The order in the array and the order of the function parameters are tightly coupled.

flashcards.question: What is mage/storage and why is it preferred over $.ajax() for REST API calls in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: mage/storage is a thin wrapper around $.ajax() that provides sensible defaults for REST API calls: it sets contentType to 'application/json' and global to true by default. It offers a cleaner API with storage.get(), storage.post(), storage.put(), and storage.delete() methods. Each method returns a jQuery Deferred/Promise. It does NOT automatically inject auth tokens — frontend REST auth relies on PHP session cookies.
flashcards.hint: Think about what default settings make REST calls easier, and how storefront authentication actually works.

flashcards.question: What happens when two AMD modules have a circular dependency in RequireJS, and how do you fix it?
flashcards.answer: When two modules depend on each other circularly, RequireJS resolves it by providing an empty object {} for one of them — this is a silent failure with no error thrown. Calling methods on the empty object results in 'is not a function' errors. The fix is to either extract shared logic into a third module, or use lazy require() inside a function body so the dependency is resolved only when called, by which time both modules are fully loaded.
flashcards.hint: RequireJS doesn't throw an error — it silently gives one module an empty object.

flashcards.question: What is the correct way to use translation strings inside an AMD module in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: You should explicitly include mage/translate as a dependency and alias it as $t, then use $t('Your string') for translations. While $.mage.__() also works if jQuery is loaded, it is fragile and not the recommended approach. The explicit import of mage/translate ensures the translation function is always available and follows Magento coding standards.
flashcards.hint: There are two ways to translate in JS, but one requires an explicit dependency declaration and is the recommended pattern.

flashcards.question: How do Knockout observables work in Magento checkout models like quote and customer, and what is the common pitfall?
flashcards.answer: The checkout models use Knockout observables for data like quote.totals(), quote.shippingAddress(), and customer.isLoggedIn(). These are functions that must be called with parentheses () to get their current value. The common pitfall is accessing them without parentheses (e.g., quote.totals instead of quote.totals()), which returns the observable function itself instead of the data, leading to undefined property access errors.
flashcards.hint: Observables look like properties but they are actually functions — you need to invoke them.

flashcards.question: What is mage/utils/wrapper used for in Magento 2 JavaScript, and why is it preferred over direct function overriding?
flashcards.answer: mage/utils/wrapper is used to extend existing functions non-destructively using wrapper.wrap(). It takes the original function and a wrapper function that receives the original as its first argument, allowing you to add logic before/after the original call. This is preferred because it works with the mixin pattern, preserving the original behavior while adding extensions — avoiding the risks of completely overriding a module.
flashcards.hint: Think about wrapping a function so you can call the original while adding your own logic before and after.

flashcards.question: What is the merge order for requirejs-config.js files in Magento 2, and which one wins?
flashcards.answer: RequireJS configuration files from all modules and themes are merged at deploy time following the order: lib (core library) -> module -> theme. Since theme configurations are merged last, theme-level requirejs-config.js settings take the highest priority and override module-level configurations.
flashcards.hint: The merge follows a fallback hierarchy similar to other Magento assets, where more specific levels override less specific ones.

flashcards.question: In Magento 2, what are the three JS optimization settings available for production, and where are they configured?
flashcards.answer: The three settings are: Merge JS Files, Enable JS Bundling, and Minify JS Files. They are configured under Stores > Configuration > Advanced > Developer > JavaScript Settings. In development mode, all three should be set to No for debugging. In production mode, all three should be set to Yes for optimal performance. RequireJS bundling combines multiple AMD modules into fewer HTTP requests.
flashcards.hint: These three settings control how JavaScript files are combined, bundled, and compressed in production.

flashcards.question: How does the shim configuration in requirejs-config.js work, and when is it needed?
flashcards.answer: The shim configuration is used to wrap non-AMD (legacy) libraries so they can be used as AMD dependencies. It specifies deps (the library's own dependencies, like jQuery) and exports (the global variable name the library creates). This makes legacy scripts that pollute the global scope compatible with RequireJS's dependency management system.
flashcards.hint: Some older libraries don't use define() and instead attach themselves to the window object.

flashcards.question: Where should Grunt themes be registered in Magento 2, and what configuration properties does each theme entry require?
flashcards.answer: Grunt themes are registered in dev/tools/grunt/configs/themes.js. Each theme entry requires: area (e.g., 'frontend'), name (e.g., 'Vendor/theme'), locale (e.g., 'en_US'), files (array of CSS entry points like 'css/styles-m' and 'css/styles-l'), and dsl (typically 'less'). The key name in the config object is what you use with Grunt commands like grunt less:mytheme.
flashcards.hint: This file maps simple key names to full theme path configurations for Grunt to compile.

flashcards.question: How does the data-mage-init attribute dispatch to a JavaScript module, and what export types does it support?
flashcards.answer: When data-mage-init loads a module, mage/apply/main.js checks the export type: if the module returns a function, it calls fn(config, element); if it returns an object, it looks for obj[componentPath]; if neither, it checks if $(element)[componentName] exists as a jQuery widget and calls it. It does NOT automatically call an init() method — plain object modules need to return a function or use the require() approach with manual initialization.
flashcards.hint: The dispatch depends on what the module returns — a function, an object, or a jQuery widget.

flashcards.question: How does REST API authentication work for storefront AJAX calls in Magento 2, and how does it differ for logged-in customers vs guests?
flashcards.answer: Storefront REST API authentication relies on PHP session cookies that the browser sends automatically with every AJAX request — no explicit Authorization header is needed. For logged-in customers, the URL pattern is /rest/V1/carts/mine/items where the session identifies the customer. For guests, a masked cart ID is used in the URL: /rest/V1/guest-carts/:maskedCartId/items, with the masked ID available via window.checkoutConfig or the quote model.
flashcards.hint: The browser handles authentication automatically through cookies, but the URL pattern differs for guests.

studyNotes.title: Day 13 — Admin Theme Configuration
studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2 Admin Theme Configuration — Study Notes

## Table of Contents
- [1. Overview: Theme Assignment Scopes](#1-overview-theme-assignment-scopes)
- [2. Applying Themes via Admin: Content → Design → Configuration](#2-applying-themes-via-admin-content--design--configuration)
- [3. Theme Assignment Hierarchy & Granularity](#3-theme-assignment-hierarchy--granularity)
- [4. Theme Activation: Cache & Deployment](#4-theme-activation-cache--deployment)
- [5. Design Schedules (EE Only)](#5-design-schedules-ee-only)
- [6. Custom Design per Category](#6-custom-design-per-category)
- [7. Custom Design per Product](#7-custom-design-per-product)
- [8. Custom Design per CMS Page](#8-custom-design-per-cms-page)
- [9. User Agent Rules (Deprecated)](#9-user-agent-rules-deprecated)
- [10. Hands-On: Apply a Theme to a Store View](#10-hands-on-apply-a-theme-to-a-store-view)
- [11. Tricky Concepts & Common Pitfalls](#11-tricky-concepts--common-pitfalls)
- [12. Quick-Reference Checklist](#12-quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Overview: Theme Assignment Scopes

Magento 2 allows themes to be assigned at **three scope levels**, following the standard Magento scope hierarchy:

```
Website
  |
  +-- Store (Store Group)
        |
        +-- Store View  <-- most granular
```

| Scope | Granularity | Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| **Website** | Broadest | One theme across all stores and views |
| **Store (Group)** | Middle | Different theme per store group |
| **Store View** | Most granular | Different theme per locale/language view |

> **Exam focus:** Store View is the **most granular** scope for theme assignment. A theme assigned at a lower scope always **overrides** a theme set at a higher scope.

---

## 2. Applying Themes via Admin: Content → Design → Configuration

### Navigation Path

```
Admin Panel
  --> Content
    --> Design
      --> Configuration
```

### Step-by-Step Process

1. Navigate to **Content → Design → Configuration**
2. The grid displays all **Website / Store / Store View** rows
3. Click **Edit** on the desired scope row
4. Under **Default Theme**, select the theme from the **Applied Theme** dropdown
5. Click **Save Configuration**
6. Flush cache and re-deploy static content (see [Section 4](#4-theme-activation-cache--deployment))

### What the Configuration Grid Shows

```
+------------------+----------------+------------------+
|  Scope           |  Applied Theme |  Edit Link       |
+------------------+----------------+------------------+
|  Default         |  Magento/luma  |  [Edit]          |
|  Main Website    |  Magento/luma  |  [Edit]          |
|   Main Store     |  Magento/luma  |  [Edit]          |
|    Default View  |  Magento/luma  |  [Edit]          |
|    French View   |  Vendor/custom |  [Edit]          |
+------------------+----------------+------------------+
```

> **Exam focus:** The path is **Content → Design → Configuration** (not Stores → Configuration). This is distinct from the system configuration path.

---

## 3. Theme Assignment Hierarchy & Granularity

### Inheritance & Override Rules

```
Default (Global)
    |
    v
Website scope assignment
    |
    v
Store scope assignment
    |
    v
Store View scope assignment  <-- wins if set
```

- If a Store View has no explicit theme, it **inherits** from the Store
- If a Store has no explicit theme, it inherits from Website
- If Website has no explicit theme, it falls back to the Default row

> **Exam focus:** Scope inheritance in theme assignment mirrors all other Magento configuration scope inheritance. **More specific scope wins.**

### The "Default" Row

The **Default** row in Design Configuration applies globally to all scopes that do not have an override. It is NOT the same as "Default Store View."

---

## 4. Theme Activation: Cache & Deployment

After saving a theme assignment, additional steps are required before the new theme is visible.

### Production Mode

```bash
# Step 1: Flush the Magento cache
php bin/magento cache:flush

# Step 2: Deploy static content for the theme
php bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -f

# Optional: deploy for a specific locale only
php bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_US -f

# Optional: deploy for a specific theme only
php bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy --theme Vendor/themename -f
```

### Developer Mode

In developer mode, static files are generated on-the-fly, but you still need:

```bash
# Flush cache
php bin/magento cache:flush

# If using Grunt for LESS compilation:
grunt exec:<theme>
grunt less:<theme>

# Or clean and recompile everything:
grunt clean
grunt exec
grunt less
```

### Summary Table

| Mode | Action Required |
|---|---|
| **Production** | `cache:flush` + `setup:static-content:deploy` |
| **Developer** | `cache:flush` (files regenerate on request) |
| **Developer + Grunt** | `cache:flush` + `grunt exec` + `grunt less` |

> **Exam focus:** In **production mode**, simply saving the theme in admin is **not enough** — you MUST run `cache:flush` AND `setup:static-content:deploy`. In developer mode, cache flush is generally sufficient.

---

## 5. Design Schedules

Design Schedules allow a different theme to be applied automatically for a specific date range. This feature is available in **both Open Source (CE) and Adobe Commerce (EE)** — the admin controllers are in `module-backend` (core) and the `design_change` table is in `module-theme` (core).

### Navigation Path

```
Admin Panel
  --> Content
    --> Design
      --> Schedule
```

### How Design Schedules Work

```
Regular Theme Assignment (always active)
        |
        v
  [Date Range Start] -----> Design Schedule Theme (overrides regular)
        |                            |
        |                    Holiday theme active
        |                            |
  [Date Range End]  <----- Design Schedule Expires
        |
        v
Regular Theme Assignment (resumes automatically)
```

### Creating a Design Schedule

1. Navigate to **Content → Design → Schedule**
2. Click **Add Design Change**
3. Configure:
   - **Store**: Select the store view
   - **Custom Design**: Select the temporary theme
   - **Date From**: Start date of the schedule
   - **Date To**: End date of the schedule
4. Save

### Key Behavior

- The schedule **activates automatically** at the configured date/time
- **No cache flush is needed** when the schedule activates or expires
- The scheduled theme **overrides** the regular theme assignment for that period
- Once the end date passes, the regular theme assignment **automatically resumes**

> **Exam focus:** Design schedules are available in **both CE and EE** (the admin route and `design_change` DB table are in core modules `module-backend` and `module-theme`). They override regular theme assignments during the scheduled period. **No cache flush is required** when the schedule activates — this is a critical exam differentiator.

### Example Use Case

```
Normal: Magento/luma assigned to Main Website Store View
Schedule: Dec 20 - Jan 5 --> Vendor/holidaytheme
Result:
  Dec 19 --> luma displays
  Dec 20 --> holidaytheme activates automatically (no cache flush)
  Jan 5  --> holidaytheme expires, luma resumes automatically
```

---

## 6. Custom Design per Category

You can apply a custom theme or layout to an **individual category page** without affecting the rest of the site.

### Navigation Path

```
Admin Panel
  --> Catalog
    --> Categories
      --> [Select Category]
        --> Design tab
```

### Fields Available

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use Parent Category Settings** | Inherit design from parent category |
| **Apply Design to Products** | Also apply this design to products in this category |
| **Custom Design** | Select a theme to override for this category |
| **Active From / To** | Date range for the custom design |
| **Page Layout** | Override the page layout (1 column, 2 columns left, etc.) |
| **Layout Update XML** | Raw XML snippet to modify layout on category pages |

### Layout Update XML Example

```xml
<referenceContainer name="sidebar.main">
    <block class="Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template"
           name="custom.category.banner"
           template="Vendor_Module::category/banner.phtml"/>
</referenceContainer>
```

> **Exam focus:** The **Custom Design** field in a category's Design tab applies only to that **category listing page (CLP)**. If **Apply Design to Products** is checked, it also applies to product pages **within** that category. Layout Update XML is **validated at save time**.

---

## 7. Custom Design per Product

Individual products can have custom layout modifications applied specifically to their **Product Detail Page (PDP)**.

### Navigation Path

```
Admin Panel
  --> Catalog
    --> Products
      --> [Select Product]
        --> Design tab
```

### Fields Available

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Custom Layout Update** | Dropdown to select a pre-defined custom layout file (newer approach) |
| **Custom Layout Update XML** | Raw XML layout snippet applied only to this product's PDP |

### Custom Layout Update XML Example

```xml
<!-- Modern approach: use the template attribute directly on referenceBlock -->
<referenceBlock name="product.info.sku" template="Vendor_Module::product/custom-sku.phtml"/>

<!-- Legacy approach: <action> still works but is not recommended -->
<!-- <referenceBlock name="product.info.sku">
    <action method="setTemplate">
        <argument name="template" xsi:type="string">
            Vendor_Module::product/custom-sku.phtml
        </argument>
    </action>
</referenceBlock> -->
```

### Another Example: Remove a Block on a Specific PDP

```xml
<!-- Note: product.info.stock.sku is a CONTAINER (not a block), so use referenceContainer -->
<referenceContainer name="product.info.stock.sku" remove="true"/>
```

### Validation Behavior

- XML in the **Custom Layout Update XML** field is **validated at save time**
- Invalid XML will prevent the product from saving
- The XML acts as an inline layout update merged with the product page layout handles

> **Exam focus:** Custom Layout Update XML on a **product** applies **only to that product's PDP** — it does not affect any other pages or products. The XML is **validated at save time** (not at render time). This is a common exam question.

---

## 8. Custom Design per CMS Page

CMS Pages support similar custom design options to categories and products.

### Navigation Path

```
Admin Panel
  --> Content
    --> Pages
      --> [Select CMS Page]
        --> Design tab
```

### Fields Available

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Layout** | Override page layout (Empty, 1 column, 2 columns left, 2 columns right, 3 columns) |
| **Custom Layout Update XML** | XML snippet applied to this specific CMS page's layout |

### CMS Page Layout Override Example

```xml
<referenceContainer name="content">
    <block class="Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template"
           name="cms.fullwidth.banner"
           template="Vendor_Module::cms/fullwidth-banner.phtml"
           before="-"/>
</referenceContainer>
```

### Removing the Sidebar on a Specific CMS Page

```xml
<referenceContainer name="sidebar.main" remove="true"/>
<referenceContainer name="sidebar.additional" remove="true"/>
```

> **Exam focus:** CMS Page custom layout XML applies **only to that specific CMS page**. The **Layout** field (1 column, 2 columns, etc.) is a separate control from the XML. Both are found on the **Design tab** of the CMS page editor. XML is validated at save time.

### Comparison Table: Custom Design Locations

| Entity | Tab | XML Field Name | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Category** | Design | Layout Update XML | Category listing page |
| **Product** | Design | Custom Layout Update XML | Product detail page only |
| **CMS Page** | Design | Custom Layout Update XML | That CMS page only |

---

## 9. User Agent Rules (Deprecated)

### What They Were

User Agent Rules allowed different themes to be applied based on the **user agent string** of the browser/device — effectively enabling theme switching for mobile vs. desktop.

### Navigation Path (Legacy)

```
Content --> Design --> Configuration --> [Edit scope]
  --> User Agent Rules section
```

### Current Status

- **Deprecated** in newer versions of Magento 2 / Adobe Commerce
- The recommended modern approach for responsive design is a **responsive theme** (e.g., Blank/Luma are responsive by default)
- User Agent Rules are considered a legacy feature and unlikely to be heavily tested in current exams, but awareness of their existence and deprecation is expected

> **Exam focus:** User Agent Rules are **deprecated**. Know they existed for applying themes per **device type/browser**, but the modern approach is **responsive themes**. You may see a question asking about their status.

---

## 10. Hands-On: Apply a Theme to a Store View

### Scenario

Apply a custom theme (`Vendor/customtheme`) to the "French Store View" while leaving the default store view using `Magento/luma`.

### Step 1: Navigate to Design Configuration

```
Admin --> Content --> Design --> Configuration
```

### Step 2: Edit the Target Store View

- Locate the **French Store View** row in the grid
- Click **Edit**

### Step 3: Assign the Theme

- Under **Default Theme** section
- Set **Applied Theme** dropdown to `Vendor/customtheme`
- Click **Save Configuration**

### Step 4: Flush Cache (All Modes)

```bash
php bin/magento cache:flush
```

### Step 5a: Deploy Static Content (Production Mode)

```bash
php bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy fr_FR --theme Vendor/customtheme -f
```

### Step 5b: Grunt Compile (Developer Mode with Grunt)

```bash
cd <magento_root>
# Grunt uses the simple key name from dev/tools/grunt/configs/themes.js
# NOT the Vendor_ThemeName format. Register your theme with a simple key first.
grunt exec:customtheme
grunt less:customtheme
```

### Step 6: Verify

1. Open a browser and navigate to the storefront
2. Switch to the **French Store View** using the store switcher
3. Verify the custom theme is rendering (check header/footer/fonts specific to `Vendor/customtheme`)
4. The default store view should still show `Magento/luma`

### Verification via CLI

```bash
# Check the deployed theme files exist
ls pub/static/frontend/Vendor/customtheme/fr_FR/

# Check the configuration in the database (advanced)
php bin/magento config:show design/theme/theme_id --scope=stores --scope-code=french_store_view
```

---

## 11. Tricky Concepts & Common Pitfalls

### Pitfall 1: Design Schedule Does NOT Require Cache Flush on Activation

```
Common Wrong Answer: "Flush cache when the holiday theme schedule activates"
Correct Answer:      "No cache flush needed — schedule activates automatically"
```

> **Exam focus:** This is one of the most tested "tricky" facts. Design schedule transitions happen **without any manual cache clearing**.

---

### Pitfall 2: Custom Layout XML is Validated at Save Time, NOT Render Time

```
Scenario: Admin enters invalid XML in Custom Layout Update XML field
Result:   Magento PREVENTS saving the entity (product/category/CMS page)
          An error is shown immediately in the admin UI
```

> **Exam focus:** Validation is at **save time**. The product/category/page **cannot be saved** with invalid XML.

---

### Pitfall 3: "Content → Design → Configuration" vs "Stores → Configuration → Design"

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Content → Design → Configuration** | Assign themes per scope (Website/Store/Store View) |
| **Stores → Configuration → General → Design** | System-level design settings (HTML head, header, footer defaults) |

These are **different admin sections** with different purposes.

> **Exam focus:** Theme assignment is under **Content → Design → Configuration**, NOT under Stores → Configuration.

---

### Pitfall 4: Design Schedule Availability

```
Design Schedule is available in BOTH CE and EE.
The admin controllers are in module-backend (core) and the
design_change table is in module-theme (core).
```

---

### Pitfall 5: Scope Override Direction

```
Wrong assumption: "Website scope theme overrides Store View theme"
Correct behavior: "Store View theme OVERRIDES Website theme"
More specific = more priority
```

---

### Summary of Key "Tricky" Facts

| Fact | Answer |
|---|---|
| Most granular theme scope | Store View |
| Design schedule availability | Both CE and EE (core feature) |
| Cache flush needed for schedule activation | No |
| XML validation timing | At save time |
| User Agent Rules status | Deprecated |
| Production theme deployment command | `setup:static-content:deploy` |
| Navigation path for theme assignment | Content → Design → Configuration |

---

## 12. Quick-Reference Checklist

### Theme Assignment
- [ ] Theme assignment path: **Content → Design → Configuration**
- [ ] Three scope levels: **Website → Store → Store View** (Store View is most granular)
- [ ] More specific scope **overrides** less specific scope
- [ ] The "Default" row is a global fallback, NOT the same as "Default Store View"

### Theme Activation After Assignment
- [ ] **Production mode**: `php bin/magento cache:flush` + `php bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -f`
- [ ] **Developer mode**: `php bin/magento cache:flush` (files regenerate on-demand)
- [ ] **Developer + Grunt**: `cache:flush` + `grunt exec:<theme>` + `grunt less:<theme>`

### Design Schedules
- [ ] Path: **Content → Design → Schedule**
- [ ] Available in **both CE and EE** (core modules: `module-backend` controllers, `module-theme` DB table `design_change`)
- [ ] Overrides regular theme assignment for the configured date range
- [ ] **No cache flush required** when schedule activates or expires — automatic
- [ ] Configured per store view with date from/to and theme selection

### Custom Design per Entity
- [ ] **Category**: Catalog → Categories → Design tab → Layout Update XML (applies to CLP)
- [ ] **Category**: "Apply Design to Products" checkbox extends design to products in that category
- [ ] **Product**: Catalog → Products → Design tab → Custom Layout Update XML (applies to PDP only)
- [ ] **CMS Page**: Content → Pages → Design tab → Layout field + Custom Layout Update XML
- [ ] All three entities: XML is **validated at save time** — invalid XML prevents saving

### Layout XML Snippets
- [ ] Custom Layout Update XML uses standard Magento layout XML syntax (`<referenceBlock>`, `<referenceContainer>`, `<block>`, etc.)
- [ ] Scoped **only** to that specific entity (product/category/page) — not global
- [ ] Common operations: add blocks, remove blocks, change templates, move blocks

### User Agent Rules
- [ ] **Deprecated** in newer Magento 2 / Adobe Commerce versions
- [ ] Used to apply different themes based on device/browser user agent string
- [ ] Modern replacement: **responsive themes** (Luma/Blank are responsive by default)

### Key Differentiators for Exam
- [ ] Content → Design → **Configuration** (theme assignment) vs. Stores → Configuration → Design (system design settings) — these are **different paths**
- [ ] Design schedule: **no cache flush** needed on activation ← most tested tricky fact
- [ ] Custom Layout XML: validated at **save time**, not render time ← second most tested tricky fact
- [ ] Design schedules are available in **both CE and EE** (core feature)
- [ ] Store View scope **wins** over Website scope in theme assignment
- [ ] User Agent Rules = **deprecated** — know this for exam

flashcards.question: What is the most granular scope at which a theme can be assigned in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Store View is the most granular scope for theme assignment. Magento follows the hierarchy Website > Store (Store Group) > Store View. A theme assigned at a more specific (lower) scope always overrides a theme set at a higher scope. If no theme is set at the Store View level, it inherits from Store, then Website, then the Default global row.
flashcards.hint: Think about Magento's standard three-level scope hierarchy.

flashcards.question: What is the correct admin navigation path to assign a theme per scope in Magento 2, and how does it differ from the design system settings?
flashcards.answer: Theme assignment is done under Content > Design > Configuration, where you select the scope row and set the Applied Theme dropdown. This is different from Stores > Configuration > General > Design, which controls system-level design settings like HTML head, header, and footer defaults. These are two separate admin sections with different purposes — a common exam trap.
flashcards.hint: The path starts with 'Content' not 'Stores' — and there are two different design-related areas in the admin.

flashcards.question: After assigning a new theme in the Magento 2 admin, what additional steps are needed before it becomes visible in production mode?
flashcards.answer: In production mode, you must run cache:flush to clear the Magento cache and then setup:static-content:deploy to compile and deploy the new theme's static assets. Simply saving the theme in admin is not enough. In developer mode, only cache:flush is needed because static files are regenerated on-demand. With Grunt in developer mode, you also need grunt exec and grunt less for the theme.
flashcards.hint: Saving alone is insufficient — there are two CLI commands needed in production mode.

flashcards.question: How do Design Schedules work in Magento 2, and do they require a cache flush when they activate?
flashcards.answer: Design Schedules allow a different theme to be applied automatically for a specific date range. They are configured under Content > Design > Schedule. The critical point is that no cache flush is needed when a schedule activates or expires — the transition is fully automatic. The scheduled theme overrides the regular theme assignment during the configured period, and the regular theme resumes automatically when the schedule expires.
flashcards.hint: The schedule transitions happen without any manual intervention — not even cache management.

flashcards.question: Are Design Schedules available in both Magento Open Source (CE) and Adobe Commerce (EE)?
flashcards.answer: Yes, Design Schedules are available in both CE and EE. The admin controllers are in module-backend (core) and the design_change database table is in module-theme (core). This is a common exam trap — many assume it's an EE-only feature, but it is a core feature available in all editions.
flashcards.hint: Check which core modules contain the controllers and database tables for this feature.

flashcards.question: How can you apply a custom theme or layout to an individual category page in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Navigate to Catalog > Categories > select a category > Design tab. There you can set a Custom Design (theme override), a Page Layout (1 column, 2 columns, etc.), and Layout Update XML. The design applies only to that category listing page (CLP). Checking 'Apply Design to Products' extends the design to product pages within that category. The Layout Update XML is validated at save time — invalid XML prevents saving.
flashcards.hint: There is a Design tab on the category editor with both theme and layout XML options.

flashcards.question: When is Custom Layout Update XML validated in Magento 2 — at save time or at render time?
flashcards.answer: Custom Layout Update XML is validated at save time, not at render time. If you enter invalid XML in the Custom Layout Update XML field on a product, category, or CMS page, Magento prevents the entity from being saved and shows an error immediately in the admin UI. This applies to all three entity types (product, category, CMS page).
flashcards.hint: The validation happens before the data reaches the database, not when the page is displayed to customers.

flashcards.question: What is the scope of Custom Layout Update XML on a product in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Custom Layout Update XML on a product applies only to that specific product's Product Detail Page (PDP). It does not affect any other pages, products, or the category listing page. The XML is found on the Design tab of the product editor in Catalog > Products. It uses standard Magento layout XML syntax with referenceBlock, referenceContainer, and block directives.
flashcards.hint: The layout change is scoped to just one page — the individual product page where it is configured.

flashcards.question: What is the status of User Agent Rules in Magento 2, and what is the modern replacement?
flashcards.answer: User Agent Rules are deprecated in newer versions of Magento 2 / Adobe Commerce. They were used to apply different themes based on the user agent string of the browser/device (e.g., mobile vs desktop). The modern replacement is responsive themes — Magento's default themes (Blank and Luma) are responsive by default. You may see a question about their status on the exam.
flashcards.hint: This feature for device-specific theme switching has been replaced by a CSS-based approach.

flashcards.question: What is the 'Default' row in the Design Configuration grid, and how does it differ from 'Default Store View'?
flashcards.answer: The Default row in Content > Design > Configuration applies globally as a fallback to all scopes that do not have their own theme override. It is NOT the same as the 'Default Store View.' It is the global baseline — if a Website, Store, or Store View does not have an explicit theme assignment, they inherit from this Default row.
flashcards.hint: This is a global fallback, not tied to any specific store view.

flashcards.question: How does the CMS page Design tab differ from the category and product Design tabs in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: CMS pages have a Layout field (to choose 1 column, 2 columns, 3 columns, or Empty layout) and a Custom Layout Update XML field, both on the Design tab at Content > Pages. Unlike categories, CMS pages do not have a Custom Design (theme override) field or an 'Apply Design to Products' checkbox. Unlike products, CMS pages include the Layout dropdown. The XML applies only to that specific CMS page.
flashcards.hint: CMS pages have a page layout selector that categories and products handle differently.

flashcards.question: In Magento 2's scope override system for theme assignment, which scope wins — Website or Store View?
flashcards.answer: Store View scope wins over Website scope. In Magento's scope hierarchy, more specific scopes always override less specific ones. The priority order from lowest to highest is: Default (global) < Website < Store (Store Group) < Store View. If a Store View has an explicit theme assignment, it overrides anything set at the Website or Store level.
flashcards.hint: More specific scopes take priority — think about which level is closest to the customer.

flashcards.question: When deploying a theme assigned to a specific store view in production mode, what is the full CLI workflow?
flashcards.answer: After saving the theme assignment in Content > Design > Configuration, you need to: 1) Run cache:flush to clear the Magento cache, and 2) Run setup:static-content:deploy with the appropriate locale and optionally the --theme flag (e.g., bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy fr_FR --theme Vendor/customtheme -f). In developer mode with Grunt, the workflow is cache:flush followed by grunt exec:themename and grunt less:themename.
flashcards.hint: The static content deploy command can be filtered by both locale and theme name.

flashcards.question: What Grunt command syntax do you use to watch a specific theme for changes, and how does it differ from watching all themes?
flashcards.answer: Use grunt watch:themename (colon syntax) to watch a specific theme, and grunt watch (no suffix) to watch all registered themes. The colon syntax is used, NOT a --theme flag. The watch command monitors source LESS files and automatically re-runs grunt less when a change is detected, providing a fast feedback loop during development without manual recompilation.
flashcards.hint: The theme name is appended after a colon, not passed as a flag.

flashcards.question: How does the 'Apply Design to Products' checkbox work in a category's Design tab?
flashcards.answer: When 'Apply Design to Products' is checked on a category's Design tab, the custom design settings (theme override, page layout, layout update XML) apply not only to the Category Listing Page (CLP) but also to all Product Detail Pages (PDPs) for products within that category. Without this checkbox, the custom design only affects the category listing page itself. This provides a way to apply design changes across an entire product group without editing each product individually.
flashcards.hint: There is a checkbox that extends category-level design changes down to the product pages within it.

studyNotes.title: Day 14 — Transactional Email Customization
studyNotes.content:
# Transactional Email Customization in Magento 2 ## Study Notes — Week 3: Admin Config, CLI & Final Prep --- ## Table of Contents 1. [Overview & Architecture](#1-overview--architecture) 2. [Accessing & Managing Email Templates](#2-accessing--managing-email-templates) 3. [Template Variable Syntax](#3-template-variable-syntax) 4. [Header & Footer Templates](#4-header--footer-templates) 5. [Creating a Custom Email Template](#5-creating-a-custom-email-template) 6. [Email Logo Configuration](#6-email-logo-configuration) 7. [Store-Specific Email Assignment](#7-store-specific-email-assignment) 8. [Email Preview](#8-email-preview) 9. [Inline CSS & HTML Best Practices](#9-inline-css--html-best-practices) 10. [Template Compilation vs. PHTML](#10-template-compilation-vs-phtml) 11. [Hands-On Walkthrough](#11-hands-on-walkthrough) 12. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist) --- ## 1. Overview & Architecture Magento 2 transactional emails are HTML messages triggered by system events (order placement, shipment, invoice, password reset, etc.). They use a dedicated templating engine that is **separate** from the standard PHTML / UI-Component rendering pipeline. ``` +-------------------------------+ | System Event Triggered | | (e.g., order placed) | +---------------+---------------+ | v +-------------------------------+ | Magento\Framework\Mail | | TransportBuilder | | (assembles template + vars) | +---------------+---------------+ | v +-------------------------------+ | Template Engine | | (Magento\Email\Model\ | | Template\Filter) | | Processes: {{var}}, {{block}}| | {{trans}}, {{depend}}, etc. | +---------------+---------------+ | v +-------------------------------+ | Mail Transport | | (SMTP / sendmail) | +-------------------------------+ ``` ### Key Components | Component | Path / Class | |---|---| | Template model | `Magento\Email\Model\Template` | | Template filter | `Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter` | | Transport builder | `Magento\Framework\Mail\Template\TransportBuilder` | | Default template files | `/view/frontend/email/*.html` | | Admin override storage | Database (`email_template` table) | - **Exam focus:** Default email templates live as `.html` files inside module `view/frontend/email/` directories, **not** in `templates/` like PHTML files. - **Exam focus:** When you save a customized template through the Admin, it is stored in the **database**, overriding the file-based default. --- ## 2. Accessing & Managing Email Templates ### Navigation Path ``` Admin Panel -> Marketing -> Communications -> Email Templates ``` ### What You Can Do Here - **View** all custom (database-stored) templates - **Add New Template** — load a default template as a starting point - **Edit** an existing custom template - **Preview** a template with sample data - **Delete** a custom template (reverts to the module default) ### Loading a Default Template When clicking **Add New Template**, you choose a **Template** from the dropdown (e.g., *New Order Confirmation*), select a **Locale**, and click **Load Template**. Magento reads the source `.html` file from the module and populates the editor. ``` Admin -> Marketing -> Email Templates -> Add New Template -> Template: "New Order Confirmation" -> Locale: English (United States) -> [Load Template] ``` - **Exam focus:** You **load** a default template first before customizing — you do not edit the original `.html` file via the Admin UI. Editing source files directly is possible but not recommended for production. - **Exam focus:** The original file-based templates are **never modified** by Admin saves; the DB record takes precedence. --- ## 3. Template Variable Syntax Magento email templates use a **custom directive syntax** processed by `Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter`. This is **not** Twig, Smarty, or standard PHP — it is Magento-specific. ### 3.1 `{{var}}` — Simple Variable Output Outputs the value of a variable passed to the template. Variables are **auto-escaped** by default (the `|escape` modifier is applied implicitly). Use `|raw` to output unescaped HTML. ```html Order Number: {{var order.increment_id}} Hello, {{var order.getCustomerFirstname()}}! Shipping to: {{var order.getShippingAddress().getCity()}} Store Name: {{var store.frontend_name}} {{var formattedShippingAddress|raw}} {{var order_data.email_customer_note|escape|nl2br}} ``` **Syntax rules:** - Uses dot notation for property/method access - Method calls include `()` - No `$` prefix — variables are referenced by name only - `|raw` disables the default auto-escaping — required for variables containing HTML - `|escape` is applied by default; `|nl2br` converts newlines to `
` - **Exam focus:** `{{var order.increment_id}}` — no parentheses for direct property access. `{{var order.getCustomerFirstname()}}` — parentheses required for method calls. ### 3.2 `{{trans}}` — Translation Wrapper Wraps a string in Magento's translation engine so it can be localized. Also auto-escaped by default. ```html {{trans "Thank you for your order."}} {{trans "%customer_name, your order #%increment_id has been placed." customer_name=$order_data.customer_name increment_id=$order.increment_id}} {{trans 'You can check the status of your order by logging into your account.' account_url=$this.getUrl($store,'customer/account/',[_nosid:1]) |raw}} ``` **Key notes:** - Strings inside `{{trans}}` are extracted into `i18n/*.csv` translation files. - Variable substitution uses `%varname` placeholders and named parameters. - Always wrap user-visible static text in `{{trans}}` for i18n compliance. - **Exam focus:** `{{trans "Label"}}` is for **translatable strings**, not for outputting dynamic values. Use `{{var}}` for dynamic data. ### 3.3 `{{block}}` — Render a Block Renders a full Magento block class inside the email. ```html {{block class='Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template' template='Magento_Sales::email/order/items.phtml'}} ``` **When to use:** - Complex HTML structures that require PHP logic - Reusing existing block/template combinations - Rendering order item tables, totals, etc. - **Exam focus:** `{{block}}` renders a **PHP block class** + PHTML template; `{{var}}` simply outputs a value. They are **not** interchangeable. ### 3.4 `{{depend}}` — Conditional Output Renders content only if a variable is truthy (non-null, non-empty, non-zero). ```html {{depend order_data.is_not_virtual}}

{{trans "Shipping details are included below."}}

{{/depend}} {{depend store_phone}} {{trans 'or call us at %store_phone' store_phone=$store_phone |raw}} {{/depend}} ``` ### 3.5 `{{if}}` / `{{else}}` / `{{/if}}` — If/Else Logic ```html {{if shipping_msg}}

{{var shipping_msg}}

{{/if}} {{if order.getCustomerIsGuest()}}

{{trans "You checked out as a guest."}}

{{else}}

{{trans "You are logged in as"}} {{var order.getCustomerEmail()}}

{{/if}} ``` ### 3.6 `{{layout}}` — Include a Layout Handle Processes a layout XML handle and outputs the result. ```html {{layout handle="sales_email_order_items" order_id=$order_id area="frontend"}} ``` ### 3.7 `{{config path=""}}` — Output Config Value Retrieves a system configuration value. ```html {{config path="general/store_information/name"}} ``` - **Exam focus:** `{{config path="..."}}` is used to pull **system configuration values** directly into templates without needing a passed variable. ### Complete Syntax Summary Table | Directive | Purpose | Example | |---|---|---| | `{{var name}}` | Output variable value (auto-escaped) | `{{var order.increment_id}}` | | `{{trans "text"}}` | Translatable string (auto-escaped) | `{{trans "Order Confirmation"}}` | | `{{block class=''}}` | Render block+template | `{{block class='...' template='...'}}` | | `{{depend varname}}` | Show if var is truthy | `{{depend order_data.is_not_virtual}}` | | `{{if expr}}` | Conditional | `{{if shipping_msg}}` | | `{{layout handle=""}}` | Render layout handle | `{{layout handle="..." order_id=$order_id}}` | | `{{config path=""}}` | Config value | `{{config path="general/.../name"}}` | --- ## 4. Header & Footer Templates ### 4.1 Header Template **File location:** ``` vendor/magento/module-email/view/frontend/email/header.html -- OR -- app/design/frontend///Magento_Email/email/header.html (theme override) ``` **Default Admin template name:** `Magento_Email::header.html` The header template is included at the top of every transactional email using: ```html {{template config_path="design/email/header_template"}} ``` **The actual header.html renders the logo directly using `{{var}}` directives** — there is no separate block/phtml for the logo. The `AbstractTemplate` model populates `logo_url`, `logo_alt`, `logo_width`, and `logo_height` variables automatically. ```html {{inlinecss file="css/email-inline.css"}}
``` **Key details:** - Uses `{{css}}` and `{{inlinecss}}` directives (unique to email templates) for CSS loading - Default logo width is **180px** when no custom width is configured - `{{var template_styles|raw}}` injects CSS from the Template Styles admin field - Logo variables are populated by `AbstractTemplate::addEmailVariables()` — a protected method on the model, not a block ### 4.2 Footer Template **File location:** ``` vendor/magento/module-email/view/frontend/email/footer.html -- OR -- app/design/frontend///Magento_Email/email/footer.html ``` **Default Admin template name:** `Magento_Email::footer.html` Included at the bottom of every email: ```html {{template config_path="design/email/footer_template"}} ``` **The actual default footer is minimal:** ```html

{{trans "Thank you, %store_name" store_name=$store.frontend_name}}!

``` **Note:** The default footer does **not** contain a copyright notice, unsubscribe link, or store address. It simply closes the HTML structure with a "Thank you" message. The Luma theme override adds more content (About Us, Customer Service links, phone, hours, address) but still no unsubscribe link. If you need an unsubscribe link, it must be added as a customization. - **Exam focus:** Header is referenced via `{{template config_path="design/email/header_template"}}` and footer via `{{template config_path="design/email/footer_template"}}`. These config paths point to the template IDs set in Admin → Content → Design → Configuration. ### 4.3 `{{template}}` Directive A special directive for **including another template** (typically header/footer): ```html {{template config_path="design/email/header_template"}} ``` This resolves the template ID stored at that config path and renders it inline. --- ## 5. Creating a Custom Email Template ### Step-by-Step Process #### Step 1: Navigate to Email Templates ``` Admin -> Marketing -> Communications -> Email Templates -> Add New Template ``` #### Step 2: Load the Default Template ``` Template: New Order Confirmation (Magento_Sales) Locale: English (United States) [Load Template] ``` #### Step 3: Configure Template Properties | Field | Description | |---|---| | Template Name | Internal identifier (e.g., *Custom Order Confirmation*) | | Template Subject | Email subject line — supports `{{var}}` directives | | Template Content | Full HTML body of the email | | Template Styles | CSS that will be auto-inlined by the template engine | ```html {{trans "Your %store_name order confirmation" store_name=$store.frontend_name}} ``` #### Step 4: Modify the Template Content ```html {{template config_path="design/email/header_template"}}

{{trans "Thank you, %name!" name=$order_data.customer_name}}

{{trans "Your order number is:"}} {{var order.increment_id}}

{{depend order_data.is_not_virtual}}

{{trans "Estimated delivery: 3-5 business days"}}

{{/depend}}
{{layout handle="sales_email_order_items" order_id=$order_id area="frontend"}} {{template config_path="design/email/footer_template"}} ``` #### Step 5: Save the Template Click **Save Template**. The template is now stored in the database. #### Step 6: Assign the Template ``` Admin -> Stores -> Configuration -> Sales -> Sales Emails -> Order -> New Order Confirmation Template [Select: "Custom Order Confirmation"] -> [Save Config] ``` - **Exam focus:** Custom templates must be **assigned** in Sales Emails configuration to take effect — saving the template alone does not activate it. - **Exam focus:** Assignment is done under **Stores → Configuration → Sales → Sales Emails**, NOT in the Email Templates grid itself. ### Sales Emails Configuration Paths | Email Type | Config Path | |---|---| | New Order | Sales → Sales Emails → Order → New Order Confirmation Template | | Order Comment | Sales → Sales Emails → Order Comments → Order Comment Email Template | | New Invoice | Sales → Sales Emails → Invoice → New Invoice Template | | New Shipment | Sales → Sales Emails → Shipment → New Shipment Template | | New Credit Memo | Sales → Sales Emails → Credit Memo → New Credit Memo Template | Full admin path: ``` Stores -> Configuration -> Sales -> Sales Emails ``` --- ## 6. Email Logo Configuration ### Setting the Transactional Email Logo ``` Admin -> Content -> Design -> Configuration -> [Select Store View row] -> Edit -> Transactional Emails -> Logo Image: [Upload image] -> Logo Image Alt: [Alt text] -> Logo Width: [px] -> Logo Height: [px] ``` ### Logo Specifications | Setting | Default / Notes | |---|---| | Max file size | Determined by PHP `upload_max_filesize` | | Default logo width | **180px** (hardcoded fallback in header.html when no width is configured) | | Supported formats | PNG, GIF, JPG | | Storage location | `pub/media/email/logo/` | | Config path | `design/email/logo` | - **Exam focus:** The email logo is configured under **Content → Design → Configuration → Transactional Emails**, NOT under Marketing → Email Templates. - **Exam focus:** The default logo width is **180px** (set in header.html as the fallback). Width and height fields in the admin accept any pixel value — there is no hard maximum. - **Exam focus:** This logo is **separate** from the storefront theme logo (`header_logo_src`). ### How the Logo is Rendered The logo is rendered **directly in header.html** using `{{var}}` directives — there is no separate phtml template for the email logo. The `AbstractTemplate` model's `addEmailVariables()` method populates the variables: ```html ``` The variables `logo_url`, `logo_alt`, `logo_width`, `logo_height` are populated by: ``` Magento\Email\Model\AbstractTemplate::addEmailVariables() → getLogoUrl() reads design/email/logo config and falls back to theme default → getLogoAlt() reads design/email/logo_alt config and falls back to store name ``` --- ## 7. Store-Specific Email Assignment Magento supports assigning **different email templates per store view**, enabling multi-brand or multi-language setups. ### Configuration Scoping ``` Admin -> Stores -> Configuration -> [Scope dropdown: Select Store View] -> Sales -> Sales Emails -> Order -> New Order Confirmation Template [Select custom template for this store view] [Save Config] ``` ### How Scope Works ``` Global (Default Config) | +-- Website | +-- Store View <-- template override applied here ``` - **Default config** applies to all stores unless overridden. - **Website-level** override applies to all store views in that website. - **Store view-level** override applies only to that specific store view. - **Exam focus:** Email template assignment respects **Magento's standard config scope hierarchy**: Default → Website → Store View. - **Exam focus:** To assign a store-view-specific template, you MUST change the **scope selector** in Stores → Configuration before saving — otherwise you overwrite the global setting. ### Practical Multi-language Setup ``` Default (English): standard-order-confirm | +-- French Store View: order-confirm-fr | +-- German Store View: order-confirm-de ``` Each template has its own translated subject and body using `{{trans}}` combined with the appropriate locale `i18n/*.csv` files. --- ## 8. Email Preview ### Using the Admin Preview ``` Admin -> Marketing -> Communications -> Email Templates -> [Click template row] -> Preview ``` Or during editing: ``` Admin -> Marketing -> Communications -> Email Templates -> [Edit template] -> Preview Template (button) ``` ### What Preview Shows - Rendered HTML with directives processed - Sample/mock data for variables (not real order data by default) - Logo as uploaded - Header and footer included ### Limitations of Admin Preview | Limitation | Detail | |---|---| | No real order data | Variables like `{{var order.increment_id}}` show empty or sample values | | CSS rendering | Preview is in a browser — real email clients may render differently | | No mobile view | Browser preview only | - **Exam focus:** The Admin preview renders the template in the browser but does **not** use real transaction data — it shows mock/empty variable values. - **Exam focus:** For accurate rendering testing, use a service like **Litmus** or **Email on Acid**, or send a test email. ### Sending a Test Email There is no native "Send Test Email" button in Magento 2 Admin out of the box. Common approaches: 1. Place a test order on the storefront 2. Use a third-party module (e.g., MageWorx Email Templates) 3. Trigger via CLI/programmatic dispatch --- ## 9. Inline CSS & HTML Best Practices ### Why Inline CSS Is Required Most email clients (Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail) **strip ` $99.00 $99.00 ``` ### Table-Based Layout Use `` for layout — **not** CSS Grid or Flexbox: ```html

{{trans "Order Confirmation"}}

{{trans "Thank you for your purchase, %name!" name=$order_data.customer_name}}

``` ### Magento's Built-in CSS Inlining Magento 2 includes a CSS inlining feature for email templates. CSS placed in the **Template Styles** field in the Admin is automatically inlined by the template engine using the `Pelago\Emogrifier` library. Additionally, the header.html uses the `{{inlinecss}}` directive to inline CSS from `css/email-inline.css`. ``` Admin -> Marketing -> Email Templates -> Edit -> Template Styles: [CSS here is auto-inlined] -> Template Content: [HTML here receives inlined styles] ``` - **Exam focus:** Magento uses **Emogrifier** to automatically inline CSS from the Template Styles field into the HTML content. You do not need to manually inline styles if using this field. - **Exam focus:** Even with auto-inlining, `

flashcards.question: Where do default email template files live in a Magento 2 module, and what file extension do they use?
flashcards.answer: Default email template files live in <Module>/view/frontend/email/ directories and use the .html file extension. They are NOT in the templates/ directory like PHTML files. When customized through the Admin UI, the modified template is stored in the database (email_template table), overriding the file-based default. The original .html files are never modified by Admin saves.
flashcards.hint: Email templates are in a different subdirectory than PHTML templates, and they use a different file extension.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between {{var}} and {{trans}} directives in Magento 2 email templates?
flashcards.answer: {{var}} outputs a dynamic variable value (e.g., {{var order.increment_id}}) and is auto-escaped by default. {{trans}} wraps static text for translation/localization (e.g., {{trans "Thank you for your order."}}). {{trans}} strings are extracted into i18n/*.csv files. Use {{var}} for dynamic data and {{trans}} for user-visible static text that needs to be translatable.
flashcards.hint: One is for dynamic values from the system, the other is for translatable static strings.

flashcards.question: How do you include the header and footer in a Magento 2 transactional email template?
flashcards.answer: The header is included using {{template config_path="design/email/header_template"}} and the footer using {{template config_path="design/email/footer_template"}}. These directives resolve the template ID stored at that config path in the admin and render it inline. The config paths point to template IDs set in Admin > Content > Design > Configuration.
flashcards.hint: A special directive resolves a config path to find which template to include.

flashcards.question: After creating a custom email template in the admin, what additional step is required to make it active for order confirmation emails?
flashcards.answer: The custom template must be explicitly assigned in the Sales Emails configuration. Navigate to Stores > Configuration > Sales > Sales Emails > Order > New Order Confirmation Template and select the custom template from the dropdown. Saving the template alone in Marketing > Email Templates does not activate it. After assigning, flush the cache with bin/magento cache:flush.
flashcards.hint: Creating the template and assigning it are two separate steps in different admin sections.

flashcards.question: Where is the transactional email logo configured in Magento 2, and what is its default width?
flashcards.answer: The email logo is configured under Content > Design > Configuration > [Store View] > Transactional Emails section, with fields for Logo Image, Logo Image Alt, Logo Width, and Logo Height. The default logo width is 180px, hardcoded as a fallback in header.html. The logo is stored in pub/media/email/logo/ and is separate from the storefront theme logo (header_logo_src).
flashcards.hint: The email logo configuration is under Content, not Marketing, and has a specific pixel fallback width.

flashcards.question: Can you use PHP tags (<?php ?>) inside Magento 2 email templates?
flashcards.answer: No, you cannot use PHP tags inside email .html templates. Email templates use Magento's custom directive syntax processed by Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter. You must use {{var}}, {{block}}, {{trans}}, {{if}}, {{depend}}, {{config}}, and {{layout}} directives instead. If you need complex PHP logic, use the {{block class='...' template='...'}} directive to render a PHP block with a PHTML template.
flashcards.hint: Email templates have their own rendering engine that is completely separate from the PHP template engine.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between {{var order.increment_id}} and {{var order.getCustomerFirstname()}} in email template syntax?
flashcards.answer: {{var order.increment_id}} accesses a direct property using dot notation — no parentheses are needed. {{var order.getCustomerFirstname()}} calls a method on the object and requires parentheses. This is a key syntax distinction: properties use dot notation without parentheses, while method calls must include parentheses. Both are auto-escaped by default.
flashcards.hint: One accesses a data property directly, the other invokes a method — look at the parentheses.

flashcards.question: Why must email templates use inline CSS and table-based layouts?
flashcards.answer: Most email clients (Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail) strip <style> blocks and ignore external stylesheets. CSS must be applied as inline style attributes for consistent rendering. Similarly, CSS Grid and Flexbox are not supported by email clients, so table-based layouts must be used. Magento uses the Emogrifier library to automatically inline CSS from the Template Styles admin field into the HTML content.
flashcards.hint: Email clients have far more limited CSS support than web browsers.

flashcards.question: How does the {{config path="..."}} directive work in Magento 2 email templates?
flashcards.answer: The {{config path="..."}} directive retrieves a system configuration value and outputs it directly in the email template. For example, {{config path="general/store_information/name"}} outputs the store name. This allows templates to pull configuration values without needing them to be passed as template variables, making templates more dynamic and reducing the need for custom variable passing.
flashcards.hint: This directive reads directly from Magento's system configuration using the standard config path format.

flashcards.question: What does the |raw modifier do in email template variables, and when should you use it?
flashcards.answer: The |raw modifier disables the default auto-escaping that Magento applies to {{var}} and {{trans}} output. By default, variables are auto-escaped (the |escape modifier is applied implicitly). Use |raw when the variable contains HTML that should be rendered as-is, such as {{var formattedShippingAddress|raw}}. Without |raw, HTML tags in the variable would be displayed as plain text.
flashcards.hint: By default, output is sanitized for security — this modifier bypasses that for trusted HTML content.

flashcards.question: What are the key differences between email templates (.html) and PHTML templates (.phtml) in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Email templates use .html extension and {{var}}, {{trans}}, {{if}} directives processed by Template\Filter; PHTML uses .phtml extension with standard PHP (<?= $block->getName() ?>). Email uses {{block class=''}} for block rendering; PHTML uses $block->getChildHtml(). Email templates are admin-editable and stored in the database when customized; PHTML files are filesystem-only. Email output is auto-escaped by default; PHTML requires manual $block->escapeHtml().
flashcards.hint: They use completely different rendering engines, syntax, storage mechanisms, and escaping behavior.

flashcards.question: How does email template scope assignment work in a multi-language Magento 2 setup?
flashcards.answer: Email template assignment respects Magento's standard config scope hierarchy: Default > Website > Store View. Different templates can be assigned per store view by changing the scope selector in Stores > Configuration before saving. This enables multi-language setups where each store view (e.g., French, German) can have its own translated template. You MUST change the scope selector before saving — otherwise you overwrite the global setting.
flashcards.hint: The scope dropdown in the configuration area is critical — missing it affects all stores.

flashcards.question: What does the Admin email template preview show, and what are its limitations?
flashcards.answer: The Admin preview renders the email template in the browser with directives processed, showing the logo, header/footer, and CSS styling. However, it uses mock/empty variable values — not real transaction data — so {{var order.increment_id}} shows empty or sample values. The preview also cannot simulate how different email clients render the HTML. For accurate testing, use services like Litmus or Email on Acid, or place a test order.
flashcards.hint: The preview processes the template engine but lacks real data and email-client fidelity.

flashcards.question: What is the {{block}} directive used for in Magento 2 email templates, and how is it different from {{var}}?
flashcards.answer: The {{block}} directive renders a full Magento PHP block class with a PHTML template inside the email, for example: {{block class='Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template' template='Magento_Sales::email/order/items.phtml'}}. It is used for complex HTML structures that require PHP logic. {{var}} simply outputs a single variable value. They are not interchangeable — {{block}} executes PHP code while {{var}} just displays data.
flashcards.hint: One outputs a simple value, the other instantiates a PHP class and renders a full template.

flashcards.question: What is the navigation path for managing email templates in the Magento 2 admin, and what operations can you perform there?
flashcards.answer: Navigate to Admin > Marketing > Communications > Email Templates. From there you can: view all custom (database-stored) templates, add a new template by loading a default template as a starting point, edit existing custom templates, preview templates with sample data, and delete custom templates (which reverts to the module default). When adding a new template, you select the base template and locale, then click Load Template to populate the editor.
flashcards.hint: The path goes through Marketing, not Content or Stores.

studyNotes.title: Day 15 — CLI Commands for Frontend Development
studyNotes.content:
# CLI Commands for Frontend Development — Study Notes ## Table of Contents 1. [Overview & Context](#1-overview--context) 2. [Static Content Deployment (SCD)](#2-static-content-deployment-scd) 3. [Cache Management Commands](#3-cache-management-commands) 4. [Template Hints & Debug Tools](#4-template-hints--debug-tools) 5. [Deploy Mode Commands](#5-deploy-mode-commands) 6. [Grunt Workflow for Local Development](#6-grunt-workflow-for-local-development) 7. [Developer Mode vs Production Mode Asset Handling](#7-developer-mode-vs-production-mode-asset-handling) 8. [SCD Flags & Advanced Options](#8-scd-flags--advanced-options) 9. [pub/static Directory Structure](#9-pubstatic-directory-structure) 10. [Hands-On Lab Reference](#10-hands-on-lab-reference) 11. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist) --- ## 1. Overview & Context Frontend development in Magento 2 involves a **compilation pipeline** that transforms raw source files (LESS, XML layout, templates) into browser-ready static assets.
