The CLI is the primary mechanism for triggering and controlling this pipeline in all deploy modes. ``` Source Files Compilation Pipeline Output ----------- -------------------- ------ app/design/.../web/css/ bin/magento SCD or pub/static/ source/_theme.less ----> Grunt less:theme ----> frontend/ vendor/.../web/css/ (LESS -> CSS) Magento/luma/ source/ (file fallback copy) en_US/ app/design/.../templates/ (require.js config) css/styles-m.css app/code/.../templates/ (HTML minification opt.) js/... ``` **Key principle:** The *deploy mode* dictates whether assets are compiled **on demand** (developer) or **pre-compiled** (production). Every frontend developer must understand this distinction to avoid stale-asset debugging nightmares. --- ## 2. Static Content Deployment (SCD) ### 2.1 Core Command Syntax ```bash bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy [options] [locale...] ``` | Component | Purpose | |-----------|---------| | `setup:static-content:deploy` | The full command name | | `[locale...]` | One or more locale codes (e.g., `en_US`, `fr_FR`) | | `[options]` | Flags to control themes, force, jobs, etc. | - **Exam focus:** SCD compiles LESS into CSS, copies static files from source directories into `pub/static/`, and generates an aggregated `requirejs-config.js` (merged from all module configs) and deployment versioning files. ### 2.2 Most Important SCD Flags ```bash # Force deploy even in developer mode bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -f # Deploy specific locale(s) bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_US # Deploy specific theme + locale bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -f -t Magento/luma en_US # Deploy multiple locales at once bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_US fr_FR de_DE # Deploy all themes for a specific area bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -a frontend en_US # Set number of parallel jobs (performance) bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -j 4 en_US # Exclude a theme from deployment bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy --exclude-theme Magento/blank en_US ``` | Flag | Long Form | Description | |------|-----------|-------------| | `-f` | `--force` | Deploy in any mode, including developer | | `-t` | `--theme` | Limit to specific theme(s) | | `-l` | `--language` | Limit to specific language(s) — alternative to positional locale args | | `-a` | `--area` | `frontend`, `adminhtml`, or `all` | | `-s` | `--strategy` | Deployment strategy: `quick` (default), `standard`, `compact` | | `-j` | `--jobs` | Parallel job count (default: **0** — single process) | | | `--no-html-minify` | Skip HTML minification of `.phtml` source templates | | | `--exclude-theme` | Skip a specific theme | | | `--exclude-area` | Skip `frontend` or `adminhtml` | - **Exam focus:** `-t` filters by **theme**, `-f` is the **force** flag required when running SCD in developer mode. Without `-f`, SCD throws an error in developer mode. ### 2.3 Most Common Real-World Examples ```bash # Full production deploy (all locales configured in admin) bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy # CI/CD pipeline: Luma theme, US English only bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -f -t Magento/luma en_US # Custom theme, multiple locales bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -f -t Vendor/custom en_US fr_FR # Admin area only bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -a adminhtml en_US # Debug run — no minification, verbose output bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy --no-html-minify -v en_US ``` ### 2.4 What SCD Actually Does (Step-by-Step) ``` Step 1: Read deployment configuration (app/etc/config.php -> themes, locales, areas) Step 2: For each theme/locale/area combination: | +-> Collect all static files via fallback mechanism | (theme -> parent theme -> module -> lib/web) | +-> Process LESS files | (compile to CSS using built-in PHP LESS compiler) | +-> Copy/symlink files to pub/static/ | (developer mode uses symlinks by default) | (production mode copies physical files) | +-> Generate aggregated requirejs-config.js | (merges all module-level requirejs-config.js files) | +-> Generate deployed_version.txt (cache-busting) | +-> Optionally minify source .phtml templates | (to var/view_preprocessed/, unless --no-html-minify) Step 3: Write deployment version (Unix timestamp) to pub/static/deployed_version.txt ``` - **Exam focus:** In **production mode**, SCD copies actual files. In **developer mode**, it creates **symlinks** by default (which is why `-f` is rarely needed in dev — assets are generated on page load instead). --- ## 3. Cache Management Commands ### 3.1 Clean vs Flush | Command | Action | When to Use | |---------|--------|-------------| | `cache:clean` | Invalidates & removes **Magento-managed** cache entries | After config/layout/template changes | | `cache:flush` | **Empties entire cache storage** (Redis DB, file dir, etc.) | When you suspect backend cache corruption | - **Exam focus:** `cache:clean` is **selective** — it only cleans Magento's own entries. `cache:flush` is **destructive** — it purges the entire storage backend, potentially affecting other applications sharing the same Redis instance. ### 3.2 Command Syntax ```bash # Clean ALL caches bin/magento cache:clean # Clean specific cache types (space-separated) bin/magento cache:clean layout block_html # Clean frontend-relevant cache types bin/magento cache:clean layout block_html full_page translate # Flush ALL cache storage bin/magento cache:flush # Enable/disable specific cache types bin/magento cache:enable full_page bin/magento cache:disable block_html # Check cache status bin/magento cache:status ``` ### 3.3 Frontend-Relevant Cache Types | Cache Type Code | What It Stores | Flush After | |-----------------|---------------|-------------| | `layout` | Processed XML layout handles | Layout XML changes | | `block_html` | Rendered block HTML output | Template / block changes | | `full_page` | Full page cache (FPC) | Any visible frontend change | | `translate` | Translation strings | i18n CSV file changes | | `config` | Merged config XML | `config.xml`, `system.xml` changes | | `collections` | DB collection results | Model / data changes | ```bash # Typical frontend developer workflow after template changes bin/magento cache:clean layout block_html full_page # After adding a new translation bin/magento cache:clean translate # Nuclear option when something is inexplicably broken bin/magento cache:flush ``` - **Exam focus:** Know the **specific cache type codes** — `layout`, `block_html`, `full_page` are the three most commonly tested for frontend work. --- ## 4. Template Hints & Debug Tools ### 4.1 Template Hints Commands Template hints overlay **red borders and file paths** on every block, showing exactly which `.phtml` file and block class rendered each section. ```bash # Enable template hints for frontend bin/magento dev:template-hints:enable # Disable template hints bin/magento dev:template-hints:disable ``` **Note:** The CLI command accepts **no options** — it always saves to the `default` scope (scope ID 0). To enable template hints for a specific store view, use the **Admin UI** instead: *Stores > Configuration > Advanced > Developer > Debug > Enabled Template Path Hints for Storefront*. The admin route allows per-store-view scoping. After enabling, **clear the block_html cache** for hints to appear: ```bash bin/magento cache:clean block_html ``` - **Exam focus:** Template hints can be scoped **per store view** via the Admin UI. The CLI command, however, always affects the **default** scope. In Admin UI, they live under: *Stores > Configuration > Advanced > Developer > Debug*. ### 4.2 What Template Hints Show ``` +--------------------------------------------------+ | [Magento_Catalog::product/view.phtml] | | Block: Magento\Catalog\Block\Product\View | | | | +----------------------------------------------+| | | [Magento_Catalog::product/view/media.phtml] || | | Block: Magento\Catalog\Block\Product\View... || | +----------------------------------------------+| +--------------------------------------------------+ ``` Each block displays: 1. **Template file path** (module::path/to/file.phtml) 2. **PHP Block class** responsible for the block ### 4.3 Additional Dev Tools ```bash # Enable/disable JS bundling bin/magento config:set dev/js/enable_js_bundling 1 # Enable/disable CSS merging bin/magento config:set dev/css/merge_css_files 0 # Enable/disable JS merging bin/magento config:set dev/js/merge_files 0 # Enable/disable minification (developer debugging) bin/magento config:set dev/js/minify_files 0 bin/magento config:set dev/css/minify_files 0 ``` --- ## 5. Deploy Mode Commands ### 5.1 Setting Deploy Mode ```bash # Switch to developer mode bin/magento deploy:mode:set developer # Switch to production mode bin/magento deploy:mode:set production # Switch to default mode bin/magento deploy:mode:set default # Check current mode bin/magento deploy:mode:show # Skip static content deployment when switching to production bin/magento deploy:mode:set production --skip-compilation ``` - **Exam focus:** `deploy:mode:set production` **automatically runs SCD and DI compilation** unless `--skip-compilation` is passed. `deploy:mode:set developer` **does NOT** run SCD — assets are generated on demand. ### 5.2 Mode Comparison Table | Feature | Developer Mode | Production Mode | Default Mode | |---------|---------------|-----------------|--------------| | LESS compilation | On page load | Pre-compiled via SCD | On page load | | Static file serving | Symlinks / on-demand | Physical files in pub/static | Physical files | | Error display | Full stack traces | Logged, not displayed | Varies | | SCD required | No (use `-f` if forced) | **Yes — mandatory** | Optional | | DI compilation | Not required | Required | Optional | | Performance | Slow (compiles on request) | Fast (pre-compiled) | Moderate | | `pub/static` symlinks | Yes | No (copies) | No | ### 5.3 Mode-Specific Behavior for Frontend Assets ``` DEVELOPER MODE request flow: Browser Request | v Magento checks pub/static/ for file | +-- File exists? --> Serve it | +-- File missing? --> Fallback mechanism: Check theme -> parent theme -> module -> lib/web Compile LESS if needed Create symlink in pub/static/ Serve file PRODUCTION MODE request flow: Browser Request | v Nginx/Apache serves pub/static/ directly (Magento PHP not involved — pure static serving) If file missing -> 404 (SCD must be re-run) ``` - **Exam focus:** In production mode, if `pub/static/` is missing or stale after a code change, users see **404 errors for CSS/JS** — this is why SCD must be run as part of every production deployment. --- ## 6. Grunt Workflow for Local Development ### 6.1 Why Grunt? Grunt provides a **faster iteration loop** than full SCD for frontend developers: - SCD recompiles everything (slow, 30s–5min+) - Grunt only recompiles **your theme's changed LESS files** (fast, 2–10s) ### 6.2 Prerequisites Setup ```bash # Install Node.js dependencies (from Magento root) npm install # Install Grunt CLI globally (if not already installed) npm install -g grunt-cli # Verify Grunt is available grunt --version ``` ### 6.3 Grunt Configuration Files ``` Magento Root/ Gruntfile.js <- Main Grunt config (do not modify) dev/tools/grunt/ configs/ themes.js <- Theme definitions (ADD YOUR THEME HERE) tasks/ ... package.json <- Node dependencies ``` **Adding your theme to `dev/tools/grunt/configs/themes.js`:** ```javascript module.exports = { blank: { area: 'frontend', name: 'Magento/blank', locale: 'en_US', files: [ 'css/styles-m', 'css/styles-l' ], dsl: 'less' }, luma: { area: 'frontend', name: 'Magento/luma', locale: 'en_US', files: [ 'css/styles-m', 'css/styles-l' ], dsl: 'less' }, // Add your custom theme: mytheme: { area: 'frontend', name: 'Vendor/mytheme', locale: 'en_US', files: [ 'css/styles-m', 'css/styles-l', 'css/email', 'css/email-inline' ], dsl: 'less' } }; ``` ### 6.4 Core Grunt Commands ```bash # 1. Clean compiled static files for a theme # Removes: pub/static/frontend////css/ grunt clean: grunt clean:luma grunt clean:mytheme # 2. Copy/execute static file fallback for a theme # Copies files from source dirs into pub/static/ grunt exec: grunt exec:luma # 3. Compile LESS to CSS for a theme # Reads themes.js config -> compiles specified .less files grunt less: grunt less:luma # 4. Watch for file changes and auto-recompile # Monitors source LESS files; re-runs less on change grunt watch # Watch a specific theme only (use colon syntax, not --theme flag) grunt watch:luma ``` ### 6.5 Typical Grunt Development Workflow ```bash # Step 1: One-time setup (new theme or after composer update) grunt clean:mytheme grunt exec:mytheme grunt less:mytheme # Step 2: Clear Magento caches bin/magento cache:clean layout block_html # Step 3: Start watching for changes grunt watch # Now: edit your .less files in app/design/... # Grunt auto-recompiles -> browser refresh shows changes ``` - **Exam focus:** The **correct order** for Grunt tasks is `clean` → `exec` → `less`. Skipping `exec` before `less` can result in outdated source files being compiled. ### 6.6 Grunt vs SCD Comparison | Aspect | Grunt | SCD (`bin/magento`) | |--------|-------|----------------------| | Speed | Fast (2–10s per theme) | Slow (30s–10min+ all themes) | | Scope | One theme at a time | All themes (or filtered) | | Requires Magento? | No (Node.js only) | Yes | | Use case | Local development | Staging/Production deployment | | Handles adminhtml? | No | Yes | | Minification control | Via Gruntfile | Via `--no-html-minify` flag | | Watch capability | Yes (`grunt watch`) | No | --- ## 7. Developer Mode vs Production Mode Asset Handling ### 7.1 The Critical Distinction ``` +---------------------+---------------------------+---------------------------+ | | DEVELOPER MODE | PRODUCTION MODE | +---------------------+---------------------------+---------------------------+ | SCD required? | NO - assets on demand | YES - mandatory | | After CSS change | Refresh browser | Run SCD + cache:clean | | After JS change | Refresh browser | Run SCD + cache:clean | | After template chg | cache:clean block_html | cache:clean block_html | | LESS compilation | PHP less compiler on req | Pre-compiled by SCD/Grunt | | pub/static files | Symlinks to source | Physical copies | | Page load speed | Slow (compiles on demand) | Fast (pre-compiled) | | Debugging | Easy (full errors) | Hard (errors in log only) | +---------------------+---------------------------+---------------------------+ ``` ### 7.2 Tricky Exam Scenarios **Scenario 1:** You changed a LESS file in developer mode. What do you need to do? > **Answer:** Just refresh the browser. Magento auto-compiles LESS on the next page load. No SCD needed. **Scenario 2:** You changed a LESS file in production mode. What do you need to do? > **Answer:** Run `bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy` (optionally filtered by theme/locale), then `bin/magento cache:clean layout block_html full_page`. **Scenario 3:** You ran `bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy` in developer mode and got an error. > **Answer:** Add the `-f` (force) flag: `bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -f en_US` **Scenario 4:** You need to debug which template is rendering a block. > **Answer:** Run `bin/magento dev:template-hints:enable`, then `bin/magento cache:clean block_html`, then refresh. - **Exam focus:** **Developer mode does NOT require SCD** — this is the single most tested concept in this topic. Assets are generated **on-demand** with a performance penalty. --- ## 8. SCD Flags & Advanced Options ### 8.1 The `--no-html-minify` Flag ```bash # Without --no-html-minify (default in production) bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_US # Result: source .phtml templates are minified to var/view_preprocessed/ # With --no-html-minify (useful for debugging/staging) bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy --no-html-minify en_US # Result: source .phtml templates are NOT minified — full formatting preserved ``` **What gets minified without this flag:** Source `.phtml` template files throughout the codebase are minified and stored in `var/view_preprocessed/`. This is where Magento reads templates from at runtime. The minified versions have whitespace removed: ```html

escapeHtml($product->getName()) ?>

escapeHtml($product->getName()) ?>

``` **Important:** `.phtml` files are NOT copied to `pub/static/` — they remain in the filesystem and are processed by PHP. The `--no-html-minify` flag controls whether their minified copies go to `var/view_preprocessed/`. It does **NOT** affect CSS or JS minification (those are controlled by `dev/css/minify_files` and `dev/js/minify_files` config settings). - **Exam focus:** `--no-html-minify` prevents HTML whitespace removal from **source template files**. Use it when you need readable source in browser DevTools inspector. It does **NOT** affect CSS/JS minification. ### 8.2 Content Version & Cache Busting ```bash # SCD writes a Unix timestamp to: cat pub/static/deployed_version.txt # Output: 1702390445 (Unix timestamp) # This version is referenced in HTML as: # ``` Every SCD run **updates this version string**, forcing browsers to download fresh assets (cache busting). ### 8.3 Deployment Strategies ```bash # Quick strategy (DEFAULT) - minimal file operations, fastest bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -s quick en_US # Standard strategy - full file copy bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -s standard en_US # Compact strategy - shared base, less disk usage bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -s compact en_US ``` | Strategy | Behavior | Best For | |----------|----------|----------| | `quick` | Minimal file operations (DEFAULT) | CI/CD speed optimization | | `standard` | Full deployment per locale | Maximum compatibility | | `compact` | Shared parent, locale-specific overrides | Multi-locale production | --- ## 9. pub/static Directory Structure ### 9.1 Understanding the Output Structure ``` pub/static/ deployed_version.txt <- Cache-busting version string (Unix timestamp) .htaccess <- Rewrite rules for versioned URLs frontend/ Magento/ luma/ en_US/ css/ styles-m.css <- Compiled from LESS (mobile styles) styles-l.css <- Compiled from LESS (desktop styles) print.css js/ ... images/ ... fonts/ ... Magento_Catalog/ <- Module-specific assets (namespaced) js/ css/ templates/ <- Knockout .html templates (NOT .phtml files) requirejs-config.js <- Aggregated AMD module configuration js-translation.json <- Translation strings for JS adminhtml/ Magento/ backend/ en_US/ ... ``` **Note:** `.phtml` files are NOT stored in `pub/static/`. The `templates/` directories inside `pub/static/` contain **Knockout JS `.html` templates** — these are static web assets used by the frontend JS framework, not PHP templates. ### 9.2 Fallback Chain Written to pub/static When SCD (or on-demand compilation) resolves a file, it follows this priority: ``` Priority (highest -> lowest) for modular files: 1. app/design/frontend////web/ 2. app/design/frontend///web/ (parent theme) 3. vendor///view/frontend/web/ (module, area-specific) 4. vendor///view/base/web/ (module, base area) Priority for non-modular (theme-level) files: 1. app/design/frontend///web/ 2. app/design/frontend//web/ (parent theme) 3. lib/web/ (Magento core lib) ``` **Note:** The fallback resolves recursively through the entire parent theme chain (e.g., custom → luma → blank). Both `view/frontend/web/` and `view/base/web/` are checked for modules — `base` serves as a catch-all for assets shared between frontend and adminhtml areas. - **Exam focus:** Understanding the fallback chain is essential — SCD resolves this chain and **copies the winning file** to `pub/static/`. In developer mode, a **symlink** is created instead. --- ## 10. Hands-On Lab Reference ### 10.1 Lab: Deploy SCD for Specific Theme + Locale ```bash # 1. Check current deploy mode bin/magento deploy:mode:show # 2. Switch to developer mode (for safe testing) bin/magento deploy:mode:set developer # 3. Remove existing pub/static for clean comparison rm -rf pub/static/frontend/Magento/luma/en_US/ # 4. Run SCD for Luma theme, en_US locale bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -f -t Magento/luma en_US # 5. Observe output ls -la pub/static/frontend/Magento/luma/en_US/ # 6. Check if files are symlinks (developer mode) or copies file pub/static/frontend/Magento/luma/en_US/css/styles-m.css # 7. Now switch to production mode bin/magento deploy:mode:set production --skip-compilation # 8. Run SCD again bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -t Magento/luma en_US # 9. Check again - now physical copies, not symlinks file pub/static/frontend/Magento/luma/en_US/css/styles-m.css # 10. Compare output sizes (production has more files due to minification) du -sh pub/static/frontend/Magento/luma/en_US/ ``` ### 10.2 Lab: Full Frontend Developer Workflow ```bash # Scenario: You modified a LESS file and need to see changes in production # 1. Edit your LESS file vi app/design/frontend/Vendor/theme/web/css/source/_custom.less # 2. Redeploy static content for your theme only bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -t Vendor/theme en_US # 3. Clear affected caches bin/magento cache:clean layout block_html full_page # 4. Verify the CSS file was updated ls -la pub/static/frontend/Vendor/theme/en_US/css/ cat pub/static/frontend/Vendor/theme/en_US/css/styles-m.css | grep -i "custom" ``` ### 10.3 Lab: Enable Template Hints ```bash # 1. Ensure developer mode bin/magento deploy:mode:set developer # 2. Enable template hints (always saves to default scope) bin/magento dev:template-hints:enable # 3. Clear block cache so hints appear bin/magento cache:clean block_html # 4. Visit storefront - red borders show template paths # 5. Disable when done bin/magento dev:template-hints:disable bin/magento cache:clean block_html ``` ### 10.4 Lab: Grunt Workflow ```bash # 1. Ensure themes.js has your theme configured cat dev/tools/grunt/configs/themes.js # 2. Full clean and recompile cycle grunt clean:luma grunt exec:luma grunt less:luma # 3. Clear Magento caches bin/magento cache:clean layout block_html # 4. Start watching (use colon syntax for specific theme) grunt watch:luma # 5. In another terminal, edit a LESS file echo ".test { color: red; }" >> app/design/frontend/Magento/luma/web/css/source/_extend.less # 6. Grunt auto-compiles - check output # [Running "less:luma" task] ... Done. ``` --- ## Quick-Reference Checklist ### Static Content Deployment (SCD) - [ ] `bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy` — deploy all configured locales/themes - [ ] `-f` flag = **force** — required to run SCD in **developer mode** - [ ] `-t Vendor/theme` flag = limit to **specific theme** - [ ] `en_US` positional arg = limit to **specific locale** - [ ] `-l` flag = limit to **specific language(s)** (alternative to positional args) - [ ] `-a frontend|adminhtml` = limit to **specific area** - [ ] `-s quick|standard|compact` = deployment **strategy** (default: `quick`) - [ ] `-j 4` = run with **4 parallel jobs** (default: **0** = single process) - [ ] `--no-html-minify` = skip HTML minification of `.phtml` source templates (to `var/view_preprocessed/`) - [ ] SCD output goes to `pub/static/frontend////` - [ ] SCD updates `pub/static/deployed_version.txt` for cache busting ### Cache Commands - [ ] `cache:clean` = removes **Magento-managed** cache entries (selective) - [ ] `cache:flush` = empties **entire cache storage** (destructive) - [ ] Key cache types: `layout`, `block_html`, `full_page`, `translate`, `config` - [ ] After template change: `cache:clean block_html` - [ ] After layout XML change: `cache:clean layout` - [ ] After any frontend change: `cache:clean layout block_html full_page` ### Template Hints - [ ] `bin/magento dev:template-hints:enable` — shows template paths overlaid on blocks - [ ] Always follow with `bin/magento cache:clean block_html` to see effect - [ ] CLI command has **no options** — always saves to `default` scope - [ ] For per-store-view control, use **Admin UI**: Stores > Config > Advanced > Developer > Debug - [ ] Shows: template file path + PHP block class ### Deploy Mode - [ ] `deploy:mode:set developer` — assets on demand, no SCD needed - [ ] `deploy:mode:set production` — **SCD mandatory**, runs automatically unless `--skip-compilation` - [ ] `deploy:mode:set default` — intermediate mode (valid but rarely used) - [ ] `deploy:mode:show` — check current mode - [ ] Developer mode: pub/static uses **symlinks**; production mode: **physical file copies** - [ ] Developer mode: **LESS compiled on page load** (slow); production: pre-compiled (fast) ### Developer vs Production Mode — THE KEY DISTINCTIONS - [ ] **Developer mode:** SCD NOT needed — assets generated on-demand per request - [ ] **Production mode:** SCD MUST be run after any JS/CSS/template change - [ ] **Developer mode:** page load is slower due to on-demand compilation - [ ] **Developer mode + SCD:** must use `-f` (force) flag or command fails - [ ] **Production mode:** missing pub/static files = user-visible 404 errors ### Grunt Commands (Local Development) - [ ] `grunt clean:` — remove compiled CSS for theme from pub/static - [ ] `grunt exec:` — copy static source files for theme (file fallback) - [ ] `grunt less:` — compile LESS to CSS for theme - [ ] `grunt watch` — auto-recompile LESS on file change (all themes) - [ ] `grunt watch:` — watch specific theme (colon syntax, NOT `--theme` flag) - [ ] Correct order: `clean` → `exec` → `less` - [ ] Configure themes in `dev/tools/grunt/configs/themes.js` - [ ] Grunt is **faster** than SCD for local dev (single theme, not all themes) - [ ] Grunt requires `npm install` first; `grunt-cli` installed globally ### Key File Locations - [ ] `pub/static/` — all compiled/deployed static assets (CSS, JS, images, fonts, Knockout templates) - [ ] `var/view_preprocessed/` — minified .phtml templates (NOT in pub/static) - [ ] `pub/static/deployed_version.txt` — cache-busting version string (Unix timestamp) - [ ] `dev/tools/grunt/configs/themes.js` — Grunt theme configuration - [ ] `Gruntfile.js` — Grunt task definitions (Magento root) - [ ] `app/design/frontend///web/` — theme source assets ### Tricky Exam Points - [ ] `--no-html-minify` affects **source .phtml templates** only (minified to `var/view_preprocessed/`, NOT pub/static) - [ ] `cache:flush` can affect **other apps** sharing the same Redis instance - [ ] `cache:clean` is safe — only removes Magento's own cache entries - [ ] Template hints CLI always targets **default scope** — per-store-view requires Admin UI - [ ] `deploy:mode:set production` runs SCD automatically (unless `--skip-compilation`) - [ ] In developer mode, symlinks in pub/static point to actual source files - [ ] SCD must be re-run after adding new JS/CSS files, not just changes to existing ones - [ ] Default SCD strategy is `quick` — use `standard` for maximum compatibility

flashcards.question: What is the full command syntax for Static Content Deployment (SCD) in Magento 2, and what does the -f flag do?
flashcards.answer: The syntax is: bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy [options] [locale...]. The -f (--force) flag is required to run SCD in developer mode — without it, SCD throws an error in developer mode. In production mode, -f is not needed. SCD compiles LESS into CSS, copies static files to pub/static/, generates the aggregated requirejs-config.js, and creates the deployed_version.txt cache-busting file.
flashcards.hint: There is a flag needed specifically for developer mode, and the command takes locale codes as positional arguments.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between cache:clean and cache:flush in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: cache:clean is selective — it only invalidates and removes Magento-managed cache entries, leaving other applications sharing the same storage untouched. cache:flush is destructive — it empties the entire cache storage backend (Redis DB, file directory, etc.), potentially affecting other applications sharing the same Redis instance. Use cache:clean for routine config/layout/template changes; use cache:flush when you suspect cache corruption.
flashcards.hint: One targets only Magento's own cache entries, the other wipes the entire storage backend.

flashcards.question: What are the three most important cache type codes for frontend development in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: The three most important frontend cache types are: layout (processed XML layout handles — flush after layout XML changes), block_html (rendered block HTML output — flush after template/block changes), and full_page (full page cache/FPC — flush after any visible frontend change). The typical command after frontend template changes is: bin/magento cache:clean layout block_html full_page.
flashcards.hint: Think about what needs to be regenerated when you change layout files, templates, or anything visible on the storefront.

flashcards.question: How do you enable template hints via the CLI, and what scope does the CLI command affect?
flashcards.answer: Use bin/magento dev:template-hints:enable to enable and dev:template-hints:disable to disable. The CLI command accepts no options and always saves to the default scope (scope ID 0). For per-store-view template hints, you must use the Admin UI at Stores > Configuration > Advanced > Developer > Debug. After enabling, you must clear the block_html cache with bin/magento cache:clean block_html for hints to appear.
flashcards.hint: The CLI command is simple but limited in scope — the admin offers more granular control.

flashcards.question: What happens when you run deploy:mode:set production, and what does the --skip-compilation flag do?
flashcards.answer: Running deploy:mode:set production automatically runs both SCD (Static Content Deployment) and DI (Dependency Injection) compilation unless you pass the --skip-compilation flag. In contrast, deploy:mode:set developer does NOT run SCD — assets are generated on demand. Use deploy:mode:show to check the current mode. The --skip-compilation flag is useful when you want to handle SCD and DI compilation separately.
flashcards.hint: Switching to production mode triggers a complete build pipeline by default.

flashcards.question: In developer mode, what happens when a static file is requested that doesn't exist in pub/static/?
flashcards.answer: Magento uses a fallback mechanism: it checks the theme, then parent theme, then module, then lib/web directories. If the file is a LESS file, it compiles it on the fly. It then creates a symlink in pub/static/ pointing to the source file and serves the result. This is why developer mode doesn't require SCD — assets are generated on-demand per request, though with a performance penalty.
flashcards.hint: The system has a cascading search through multiple directories and creates links to the source rather than copies.

flashcards.question: What is the correct order of Grunt commands for a full theme recompilation?
flashcards.answer: The correct order is: grunt clean:<theme> (removes compiled CSS from pub/static), then grunt exec:<theme> (copies/executes static file fallback to pub/static), then grunt less:<theme> (compiles LESS to CSS). Skipping exec before less can result in outdated source files being compiled. After these commands, also run bin/magento cache:clean layout block_html. For ongoing development, use grunt watch to auto-recompile on file changes.
flashcards.hint: Clean first, then prepare the source files, then compile — order matters.

flashcards.question: What does the --no-html-minify flag do in SCD, and does it affect CSS/JS minification?
flashcards.answer: The --no-html-minify flag prevents HTML whitespace removal from source .phtml template files. Without this flag, .phtml templates are minified and stored in var/view_preprocessed/. This flag does NOT affect CSS or JS minification — those are controlled separately by dev/css/minify_files and dev/js/minify_files config settings. Use this flag when you need readable HTML in browser DevTools for debugging.
flashcards.hint: This flag only affects template files, not stylesheets or scripts — those have their own config settings.

flashcards.question: How does the pub/static/deployed_version.txt file work for cache busting in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Every SCD run writes a Unix timestamp to pub/static/deployed_version.txt. This version string is embedded in static asset URLs as 'version' followed by the timestamp (e.g., /pub/static/version1702390445/frontend/.../styles-m.css). When SCD runs again with new assets, the timestamp changes, creating new URLs that force browsers to download fresh files instead of serving cached versions.
flashcards.hint: The version number changes with each deployment, making all asset URLs unique.

flashcards.question: What are the three SCD deployment strategies available via the -s flag, and which is the default?
flashcards.answer: The three strategies are: quick (default on-premise, fastest with minimal file operations), standard (full deployment per locale, slowest but most compatible), and compact (shared base with locale-specific overrides, less disk usage). Quick uses aggressive symlinks and sharing. Standard deploys all theme/locale combinations fully independently. Compact reuses shared base files across locales to reduce redundancy.
flashcards.hint: The default strategy prioritizes speed, while the others trade speed for completeness or disk efficiency.

flashcards.question: What is the key difference between developer mode and production mode regarding static file handling in pub/static/?
flashcards.answer: In developer mode, pub/static/ uses symlinks pointing to the actual source files, and LESS is compiled on page load — no SCD is needed. In production mode, pub/static/ contains physical file copies that are pre-compiled by SCD. If pub/static/ is missing or stale in production mode, users see 404 errors for CSS/JS. Production mode serves static files directly through the web server without involving Magento PHP.
flashcards.hint: One mode creates shortcuts to source files, the other creates independent copies.

flashcards.question: What is the static file fallback chain priority in Magento 2 for modular files?
flashcards.answer: For modular files, the fallback priority from highest to lowest is: 1) app/design/frontend/<Vendor>/<theme>/<Module_Name>/web/ (theme override), 2) Parent theme's equivalent path (recursive through all parents), 3) vendor/<Vendor>/<Module>/view/frontend/web/ (module area-specific), 4) vendor/<Vendor>/<Module>/view/base/web/ (module base area, shared between frontend and adminhtml). SCD resolves this chain and copies the winning file to pub/static/.
flashcards.hint: Theme overrides come first, then parent themes, then module-specific, then the base area catch-all.

flashcards.question: What SCD-related flags can you use to limit deployment to specific themes, locales, and areas?
flashcards.answer: Use -t (--theme) to limit to specific themes (e.g., -t Magento/luma), locale codes as positional arguments (e.g., en_US fr_FR), or -l (--language) as an alternative for locales. Use -a (--area) to limit to frontend or adminhtml. Use --exclude-theme or --exclude-area to skip specific themes or areas. Use -j (--jobs) for parallel processing. These flags help speed up deployment by targeting only what changed.
flashcards.hint: Multiple filtering flags let you deploy only the specific theme/locale/area combination you need.

flashcards.question: Why is Grunt faster than SCD for local frontend development?
flashcards.answer: Grunt only recompiles the changed LESS files for a single theme (taking 2-10 seconds), while SCD recompiles everything across all themes and locales (taking 30 seconds to 10+ minutes). Grunt also supports a watch mode that auto-recompiles on file changes, eliminating manual commands. Grunt does not require the Magento PHP application — it uses Node.js only. However, Grunt is not suitable for production deployment, where SCD is required.
flashcards.hint: The scope of what gets recompiled and the presence of file watching make a big difference.

flashcards.question: What does the templates/ directory inside pub/static/ contain, and how is it different from PHTML templates?
flashcards.answer: The templates/ directories inside pub/static/ contain Knockout JS .html templates — these are static web assets used by the frontend JavaScript framework for UI components (like checkout steps, minicart, etc.), NOT PHP .phtml templates. PHTML files are never stored in pub/static/ — they remain in the filesystem and are processed by PHP. When SCD uses --no-html-minify, it affects .phtml files stored in var/view_preprocessed/, not these Knockout templates.
flashcards.hint: These are JavaScript template files for Knockout.js, not server-side PHP templates.

studyNotes.content:
# Adobe Commerce Cloud CLI & Frontend Tools
## Comprehensive Study Notes — Week 3: Admin Config, CLI & Final Prep

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Overview](#1-overview)
2. [The magento-cloud CLI Tool](#2-the-magento-cloud-cli-tool)
3. [Key CLI Commands for Frontend Developers](#3-key-cli-commands-for-frontend-developers)

## 1. Overview

Adobe Commerce Cloud is a managed Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) built on top of the open-source Magento codebase. It extends the standard `magento` CLI with a dedicated **`magento-cloud`** CLI tool that allows developers — including frontend developers — to interact with cloud environments, transfer files, manage deployments, and configure environment variables.

For frontend developers specifically, the critical workflow concerns are:

- How **Static Content Deployment (SCD)** works in a cloud pipeline
- When and where static assets are generated (build phase vs. deploy phase)
- How **Fastly CDN** serves, caches, and optimizes those assets
- How to use the CLI to access environments and sync files locally

```
+------------------+       magento-cloud CLI        +---------------------+
|  Local Machine   | -----------------------------> |  Cloud Environment  |
|  (Dev Workstation)|  ssh / mount:download / push  |  (Int / Staging /   |
+------------------+                                |   Production)       |
                                                    +---------------------+
                                                           |
                                                    [Fastly CDN Layer]
                                                           |
                                                    [pub/static/ assets]
```

## 2. The magento-cloud CLI Tool

### What Is It?

The `magento-cloud` CLI is the **official command-line interface** for Adobe Commerce on Cloud Infrastructure. It is separate from the standard `bin/magento` command and is used to manage *cloud-specific* operations.

### Installation

```bash
# Install globally via the Cloud CLI installer
curl -sS https://accounts.magento.cloud/cli/installer | php

# Verify installation
magento-cloud --version

# Authenticate with your Adobe Commerce Cloud account
magento-cloud auth:login
```

### Environment Hierarchy

```
Project (e.g., abc123xyz)
  |
  +-- Master / Production  (branch: master)
  |
  +-- Staging              (branch: staging)
  |
  +-- Integration 1        (branch: feature/my-theme)
  |
  +-- Integration 2        (branch: fix/checkout-styles)
```

**Exam focus:**
- The `magento-cloud` CLI is *separate* from `bin/magento` — it manages cloud infrastructure, not Magento application tasks
- You must `auth:login` before using project-specific commands
- Projects have hierarchical environments: Production > Staging > Integration

## 3. Key CLI Commands for Frontend Developers

### 3.1 `magento-cloud ssh` — Access Environment Shell

This is the primary command for gaining remote shell access to any cloud environment.

```bash
# SSH into the default (current) environment
magento-cloud ssh

# SSH into a specific environment by ID
magento-cloud ssh --environment=staging

# SSH into a specific environment with a shorthand flag
magento-cloud ssh -e staging

# SSH and run a single command without opening an interactive shell
magento-cloud ssh -e staging -- bin/magento cache:flush

# List available environments first
magento-cloud environments
```

**Use cases for frontend developers:**
- Running `bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy` manually
- Inspecting `pub/static/` directory contents
- Checking theme file presence after deployment
- Viewing environment variables set on the server

```bash
# After SSH-ing in, useful frontend commands:
# Check what themes are deployed
ls -la pub/static/frontend/

# Check SCD log
cat var/log/cloud.log | grep -i "static content"

# Manually trigger SCD for a specific theme/locale
bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_US --theme Vendor/Theme -f
```

**Exam focus:**
- `magento-cloud ssh` = remote shell access to the environment container
- Use `-e <environment-id>` to specify which environment to access
- Works across all environment types (Integration, Staging, Production)

---

### 3.2 `magento-cloud mount:download` — Sync Static Files Locally

Cloud environments use **writable mounts** for directories that need filesystem write access (`pub/static/`, `var/`, `pub/media/`, etc.). The `mount:download` command pulls files from these mounts to your local machine.

```bash
# Download pub/static/ from the current environment to local
magento-cloud mount:download --mount pub/static --target ./pub/static

# Download from a specific environment
magento-cloud mount:download \
  --mount pub/static \
  --target ./pub/static \
  --environment staging

# Download pub/media/ similarly
magento-cloud mount:download \
  --mount pub/media \
  --target ./pub/media \
  --environment production

# Common flags:
#   --mount    : The mount path on the remote server (relative to app root)
#   --target   : Local destination directory
#   --environment / -e : Which cloud environment to pull from
#   --delete   : Delete local files not present on remote (rsync --delete)
```

**Why frontend developers use this:**
- To inspect compiled CSS/JS/images that were generated by SCD on the server
- To debug mismatches between local and cloud deployed theme files
- To pull down production static assets for local performance analysis

```
Remote Cloud Environment
  [pub/static/frontend/Magento/luma/en_US/css/styles-m.css]
                    |
          magento-cloud mount:download
                    |
                    v
Local Machine
  [./pub/static/frontend/Magento/luma/en_US/css/styles-m.css]
```

**Exam focus:**
- `mount:download` uses rsync under the hood to transfer files efficiently
- The `--mount` flag references the *remote* mount path
- The `--target` flag is the *local* destination
- This is a **read** operation — it does NOT push changes to the cloud

---

### 3.3 `magento-cloud environment:push` — Deploy Frontend Changes

After committing your code locally (theme files, Less/CSS, JS, templates), you deploy to a cloud environment using `environment:push`.

```bash
# Push current branch to its corresponding cloud environment
magento-cloud environment:push

# Push to a specific environment (creates it if it doesn't exist)
magento-cloud environment:push --environment=feature-new-header

# Push and activate the environment immediately
magento-cloud environment:push --activate

# Push and set the parent environment
magento-cloud environment:push --parent=staging

# Force push (use with caution — bypasses confirmation)
magento-cloud environment:push --force

# Equivalent Git + CLI workflow:
git add app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/
git commit -m "Update homepage hero banner styles"
git push magento-cloud feature/homepage-hero
# OR using the CLI directly:
magento-cloud environment:push
```

**What happens after a push:**

```
git push / environment:push
        |
        v
  [Build Phase]
  - composer install
  - npm / grunt (if configured)
  - SCD (if SCD_STRATEGY targets build phase)
  - Assets compiled into read-only filesystem
        |
        v
  [Deploy Phase]
  - Site goes into maintenance mode
  - Database migrations run
  - SCD (if configured for deploy phase)
  - Cache warm-up
        |
        v
  [Post-Deploy Phase]
  - Cache flush
  - Search index updates
  - Site returns to live
```

**Exam focus:**
- `environment:push` triggers the full build-deploy pipeline, not just a file copy
- Frontend changes (theme files) must go through the build/deploy pipeline — you cannot just FTP files to production
- Static assets are **regenerated** during the pipeline according to SCD configuration

## 4. Cloud Deployment Architecture

Understanding *where* in the pipeline frontend assets are generated is critical for the exam.

### The Three Phases

```
+---------------+    +----------------+    +------------------+
|  BUILD PHASE  |    |  DEPLOY PHASE  |    | POST-DEPLOY PHASE|
+---------------+    +----------------+    +------------------+
| - Read-only   |    | - Maintenance  |    | - Site is live   |
|   filesystem  |    |   mode ON      |    | - Cache warm-up  |
| - No DB access|    | - DB access    |    | - Cron enabled   |
| - composer    |    | - Migrations   |    | - Indexing       |
|   install     |    | - SCD (option) |    |                  |
| - SCD (option)|    | - Deploy hooks |    |                  |
| - Build hooks |    | - Maintenance  |    |                  |
|               |    |   mode OFF     |    |                  |
+---------------+    +----------------+    +------------------+
      |                     |                      |
  pub/static/          pub/static/            No SCD here
  generated here       generated here
  (preferred)          (causes downtime)
```

### Why Phase Matters for Frontend

| Phase | SCD Allowed? | DB Available? | Site Down? | Recommended? |
|-------|:------------:|:-------------:|:----------:|:------------:|
| Build | Yes | No | No | **Yes** — minimizes downtime |
| Deploy | Yes | Yes | Yes (maintenance mode) | Avoid if possible |
| Post-Deploy | No | Yes | No | N/A |

**Exam focus:**
- Running SCD in the **build phase** is preferred because the site does NOT go into maintenance mode during the build phase
- Running SCD in the **deploy phase** increases downtime because the site is in maintenance mode while SCD runs
- SCD cannot run in the **post-deploy phase** (filesystem is read-only for pub/static/ by then in cloud context)

## 5. Static Content Deployment (SCD) on Cloud

### What SCD Does

SCD (Static Content Deployment) compiles all frontend theme assets:
- Merges and minifies CSS (from Less source files)
- Bundles and minifies JavaScript
- Copies images, fonts, and other static assets
- Generates locale-specific files for all configured locales
- Outputs everything to `pub/static/frontend/<Vendor>/<Theme>/<locale>/`

### SCD in Cloud Context

In cloud environments, `pub/static/` is a **writable mount** (not part of the read-only deployed codebase). SCD must explicitly run as part of the deployment pipeline.

```bash
# The underlying command that SCD runs (executed automatically by the pipeline):
bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy \
  --theme Magento/luma \
  --theme Vendor/custom-theme \
  en_US en_GB de_DE \
  -f
```

### Controlling SCD Phase via .magento.env.yaml

```yaml
# .magento.env.yaml
stage:
  build:
    SCD_STRATEGY: compact       # Run SCD in build phase
  deploy:
    SCD_STRATEGY: compact       # OR run in deploy phase (not both)
```

**Exam focus:**
- SCD generates files into `pub/static/` — this is a writable mount in Cloud
- Moving SCD to the **build phase** is the #1 way to reduce deployment downtime
- SCD behavior is controlled via environment variables, primarily in `.magento.env.yaml`

---

## 6. SCD_STRATEGY Configuration

`SCD_STRATEGY` is the most important SCD-related environment variable. It controls *how many* theme/locale combinations are deployed.

### The Three Strategies

#### 6.1 `compact` (Default)

```yaml
stage:
  build:
    SCD_STRATEGY: compact
```

- **Behavior:** Deploys static content using **fewer parallel processes**
- Generates a smaller number of theme/locale combinations, reusing shared files where possible
- **Speed:** Moderate
- **Disk usage:** Lower than `standard`
- **Best for:** Most production deployments

```
compact strategy:
  Theme A + en_US --> [shared base files] --> output
  Theme A + en_GB --> [shared base files] --> output (reuses base)
  Theme A + de_DE --> [shared base files] --> output (reuses base)

  Less redundant file copying = faster, smaller disk footprint
```

#### 6.2 `standard`

```yaml
stage:
  build:
    SCD_STRATEGY: standard
```

- **Behavior:** Deploys static content for **ALL theme × locale combinations** fully independently
- Every theme+locale gets a completely self-contained set of files
- **Speed:** Slowest (most thorough)
- **Disk usage:** Highest
- **Best for:** When you need guaranteed isolation between locale deployments

```
standard strategy:
  Theme A + en_US --> [full independent build]
  Theme A + en_GB --> [full independent build]
  Theme A + de_DE --> [full independent build]
  Theme B + en_US --> [full independent build]
  ...etc.

  Most complete but most resource-intensive
```

#### 6.3 `quick`

```yaml
stage:
  build:
    SCD_STRATEGY: quick
```

- **Behavior:** Optimized for **speed** — generates the minimum required files
- Uses symlinks and shared base packages aggressively
- **Speed:** Fastest
- **Disk usage:** Lowest
- **Best for:** Build phase optimization when deployment speed is critical

```
quick strategy:
  Generate base package ONCE
  Symlink/reference from all theme+locale combinations

  Fastest deploy, smallest build output
```

### Strategy Comparison Table

| Strategy | Speed | Disk Usage | Isolation | Best Use Case |
|----------|:-----:|:----------:|:---------:|---------------|
| `compact` | Medium | Medium | Medium | Default production |
| `standard` | Slowest | Highest | Full | Multi-locale, guaranteed isolation |
| `quick` | Fastest | Lowest | Lowest | Speed-critical builds |

**Exam focus:**
- `compact` is the **default** Cloud `SCD_STRATEGY` (note: the on-premise CLI `--strategy` flag defaults to `quick` — know both contexts)
- `standard` deploys **all themes × all locales** fully
- `quick` is the **fastest** strategy
- These are set under `stage.build` OR `stage.deploy` in `.magento.env.yaml`
- Setting `SCD_STRATEGY` under `stage.build` moves SCD to the build phase

---

## 7. SCD_ON_DEMAND

### What It Is

`SCD_ON_DEMAND` makes static content generated **on the first HTTP request** that needs it, rather than during the build or deploy phase. It is a lazy-generation approach.

```yaml
# .magento.env.yaml
stage:
  global:
    SCD_ON_DEMAND: true
```

### How It Works

```
First request for a static asset:
  Browser --> Fastly --> Origin (pub/static/file.css)
                              |
                    [File does NOT exist yet]
                              |
                    Magento generates it on-the-fly
                              |
                    File written to pub/static/
                              |
                    Response served to browser
                    (SLOW - generation overhead)

Subsequent requests for same asset:
  Browser --> Fastly --> [Cache HIT] --> Fast response
```

### When to Use SCD_ON_DEMAND

| Environment | Suitable? | Reason |
|-------------|:---------:|--------|
| Local development | Yes | Avoids running full SCD locally |
| Integration (Cloud) | Yes | Fast iteration, downtime not critical |
| Staging | Generally No | Should mirror production |
| **Production** | **NO** | First request is slow; poor user experience |

### Why NOT for Production

```
Production deploy without SCD_ON_DEMAND:
  Deploy -> SCD runs -> All assets ready -> Users get fast responses immediately

Production deploy WITH SCD_ON_DEMAND (WRONG):
  Deploy -> No SCD -> First user hits site
           -> Page needs styles-m.css
           -> Server generates CSS (takes 2-5 seconds)
           -> SLOW first response for real users
           -> User may see unstyled page briefly
```

**Exam focus:**
- `SCD_ON_DEMAND: true` = static files generated on **first request**, not during deploy
- This is **NOT suitable for production** — the first request after deploy is slow
- It is designed for **development/integration environments** only
- Setting `SCD_ON_DEMAND: true` effectively disables standard SCD

---

## 8. SKIP_SCD

### What It Is

`SKIP_SCD` completely bypasses the Static Content Deployment step during the pipeline.

```yaml
# .magento.env.yaml
stage:
  build:
    SKIP_SCD: true
```

### When to Use SKIP_SCD

The primary use case is when you are **using a CDN with pre-built assets** — meaning static files are already hosted externally and you do not need Magento to generate or serve them from `pub/static/`.

```
Without SKIP_SCD (standard flow):
  Build/Deploy -> SCD runs -> pub/static/ populated -> Magento serves assets

With SKIP_SCD (CDN pre-built flow):
  Build/Deploy -> SCD skipped -> pub/static/ empty/ignored
                                -> CDN serves all static assets
                                -> Faster deployment
```

### Scenarios Where SKIP_SCD Makes Sense

1. **External CDN with pre-published assets:** All CSS/JS/images are already on a CDN (e.g., Akamai, CloudFront) before deployment
2. **CI/CD pipeline that pre-builds assets:** Assets built and uploaded to CDN as a separate step
3. **Testing deployment speed:** Temporarily skip SCD to test non-SCD parts of the pipeline

### SKIP_SCD vs. SCD_ON_DEMAND

| Variable | SCD during deploy? | When assets generated | Use case |
|----------|:-----------------:|----------------------|----------|
| Neither (default) | Yes | Build or deploy phase | Standard production |
| `SCD_ON_DEMAND: true` | No | On first HTTP request | Dev/Integration only |
| `SKIP_SCD: true` | No | Pre-built / external CDN | CDN-served assets |

**Exam focus:**
- `SKIP_SCD: true` completely **skips** static content deployment
- Primary use case: **CDN with pre-built assets** where Magento doesn't need to generate static files
- Different from `SCD_ON_DEMAND` — there is NO on-demand generation; assets must already exist elsewhere

## 9. Fastly CDN & Static File Serving

### Fastly on Adobe Commerce Cloud

Fastly is the **included CDN and WAF** on Adobe Commerce Cloud (Starter and Pro plans). It is deeply integrated into the platform and serves as the primary edge layer for all traffic.

```
User's Browser
      |
      v
  [Fastly Edge Network]  <-- CDN / WAF / Image Optimization
      |
      | Cache HIT -> Serve cached response
      |
      | Cache MISS -> Forward to origin
      |
      v
  [Commerce Cloud Origin]
  (Nginx -> PHP-FPM -> Magento)
      |
      v
  [pub/static/ mount]
  (CSS, JS, images, fonts)
```

### How Fastly Serves pub/static/ Assets

In **production and staging** environments:
- Fastly **caches** all requests to `pub/static/` based on URL
- Cache TTL for static assets is very long (they are versioned by hash/timestamp)
- Assets are served from Fastly edge nodes globally — very fast

```
Request: GET /pub/static/version1234/frontend/Magento/luma/en_US/css/styles-m.css

Fastly checks cache:
  HIT  -> Return from edge (< 50ms globally)
  MISS -> Fetch from origin, cache it, return to user
```

### Cache Purge on Deploy

When a new deployment occurs and new static assets are generated, Fastly must be told to **purge its cache** so users get the new files.

```bash
# Cache purge happens automatically on deploy via:
# 1. Magento version hashing (new version number in static URLs)
# 2. Explicit Fastly API purge during post-deploy hooks

# URL versioning example:
# Before deploy: /pub/static/version1680000000/frontend/.../styles-m.css
# After deploy:  /pub/static/version1690000000/frontend/.../styles-m.css
# (Different URL = cache miss on Fastly = fresh content)
```

### Fastly in Development Environments

**Critical distinction:**

| Environment | Fastly Active? | pub/static/ Served By |
|-------------|:--------------:|----------------------|
| Production | Yes | Fastly CDN |
| Staging | Yes | Fastly CDN |
| Integration | **No** | Nginx on origin directly |
| Local Dev | **No** | Local web server |

**Exam focus:**
- Fastly does **NOT** serve `pub/static/` directly in **development/integration environments**
- Fastly is only active on **Staging and Production** environments on Cloud Pro
- Cache purge occurs on deploy through URL versioning and/or explicit Fastly API calls
- The static URL includes a version timestamp that changes each deploy, busting CDN cache

## 10. Image Optimization via Fastly

Fastly on Adobe Commerce Cloud includes **Fastly Image Optimization (IO)** — a real-time image processing service.

### Key Features

#### Automatic WebP Conversion

```
Browser request with Accept: image/webp header
          |
          v
     Fastly IO intercepts request
          |
          v
   Converts JPEG/PNG to WebP on-the-fly
          |
          v
   Returns WebP (30-80% smaller file size)

Browser WITHOUT WebP support:
   Returns original JPEG/PNG
```

#### Responsive Images

Fastly IO can serve **different image sizes** based on query parameters or viewport, without requiring Magento to pre-generate resized versions.

```
# Original image URL:
/media/catalog/product/image.jpg

# Fastly IO resized versions:
/media/catalog/product/image.jpg?width=800&height=600
/media/catalog/product/image.jpg?width=400&height=300&quality=85
/media/catalog/product/image.jpg?format=webp&width=800
```

#### Configuration in Magento Admin

```
Stores -> Configuration -> General -> Web -> Fastly Image Optimization
  - Enable Fastly Image Optimization: Yes
  - Enable WebP: Yes
  - Enable Deep Image Optimization: Yes
  - Default Image Quality: 85
```

### Fastly IO vs. Magento Image Resize

| Feature | Magento Native | Fastly IO |
|---------|:--------------:|:---------:|
| Resize images | Yes (pre-generated) | Yes (on-the-fly) |
| WebP conversion | No (requires extra module) | Yes (automatic) |
| Storage needed | High (all variants stored) | Low (generated at edge) |
| Server load | High | None (edge processing) |
| Cache | `pub/media/cache/` | Fastly edge cache |

**Exam focus:**
- Fastly IO provides **automatic WebP conversion** based on browser `Accept` header
- Responsive images are served via **query parameters** on the image URL
- Fastly IO reduces origin server load by processing images at the **CDN edge**
- This is separate from Magento's native image resizing (which writes to `pub/media/cache/`)

## 11. Frontend Performance Features on Cloud

Adobe Commerce Cloud includes several server-level performance features relevant to frontend developers.

### 11.1 Pre-Compression (gzip / brotli)

Assets in `pub/static/` are **pre-compressed** during the build/deploy phase.

```
SCD generates: styles-m.css  (200 KB uncompressed)
               styles-m.css.gz    (50 KB - gzip compressed)
               styles-m.css.br    (40 KB - brotli compressed)

Browser sends: Accept-Encoding: br, gzip
Nginx/Fastly:  Serves .br version (smallest)

Browser sends: Accept-Encoding: gzip
Nginx/Fastly:  Serves .gz version

Browser (old): No Accept-Encoding header
Nginx/Fastly:  Serves uncompressed .css
```

**Why pre-compression matters:**
- No CPU overhead at serve time (files already compressed)
- Brotli offers ~20% better compression than gzip for text files
- Reduces bandwidth and improves Time to First Byte (TTFB)

### 11.2 HTTP/2 Push

HTTP/2 Server Push allows the server to proactively send critical assets before the browser requests them.

```
Browser requests: index.html (the page)
                       |
        Server PUSHES (without being asked):
         -> styles-m.css        (critical CSS)
         -> styles-l.css        (layout CSS)
         -> require.min.js      (RequireJS)
         -> critical-images.jpg

By the time browser parses HTML and finds <link> tags,
the files are ALREADY in browser cache!
```

```
Without HTTP/2 Push:
  HTML -> Parse -> Find CSS ref -> Request CSS -> Parse CSS -> Render
  [---waterfall---waterfall---waterfall---]

With HTTP/2 Push:
  HTML + CSS (pushed simultaneously) -> Parse HTML+CSS -> Render
  [---much faster--]
```

### 11.3 Edge Side Includes (ESI) for Dynamic Blocks

ESI is an HTML markup standard that allows **portions of a web page to be assembled at the CDN edge**, enabling static and dynamic content to be mixed efficiently.

```html
<!-- Page template includes ESI tag for dynamic "Recently Viewed" block -->
<html>
  <head>...</head>
  <body>
    <!-- This part is CACHED by Fastly (static header) -->
    <header>...</header>

    <!-- This ESI tag is DYNAMIC — Fastly fetches it separately -->
    <esi:include src="/esi/cart-summary" />

    <!-- This part is CACHED (static footer) -->
    <footer>...</footer>
  </body>
</html>
```

**How ESI works with Fastly:**

```
User requests page:
  Fastly has page in cache BUT "Recently Viewed" block has ESI tag
        |
        v
  Fastly serves cached page FRAME from edge (very fast)
        |
        v
  Fastly makes SEPARATE request for ESI block /esi/recently-viewed
  (This request goes to origin, gets personalized content)
        |
        v
  Fastly assembles: [Cached frame] + [Dynamic ESI block]
        |
        v
  User gets: Full page with dynamic content, served at CDN speed
```

**Why ESI matters for frontend:**
- Allows full-page caching even with personalized/dynamic blocks
- Shopping cart, "Hello, Name" widgets, recently viewed — all served dynamically via ESI
- Configured via Fastly module in Magento Admin

**Exam focus:**
- **Pre-compression:** Assets compressed at build time (gzip + brotli), served instantly without CPU cost
- **HTTP/2 Push:** Server proactively sends CSS/JS before browser asks for them
- **ESI:** Enables caching of page frames while keeping personalized blocks dynamic
- ESI blocks are fetched by **Fastly** separately from origin — not by the browser

## 12. The .magento.env.yaml File

This is the primary configuration file for controlling deployment behavior on Adobe Commerce Cloud.

### File Location & Structure

```
project-root/
  .magento.env.yaml      <-- Environment variable overrides
  .magento/
    routes.yaml          <-- URL routing / redirects
    services.yaml        <-- Services (Redis, Elasticsearch, etc.)
  .magento.app.yaml      <-- Application container config
```

### Full SCD-Related Configuration Example

```yaml
# .magento.env.yaml

stage:
  global:
    # Variables that apply to all stages
    SCD_ON_DEMAND: false           # true = dev only, false = standard
    SKIP_SCD: false                # true = skip SCD entirely

  build:
    # Variables for the BUILD phase
    SCD_STRATEGY: compact          # compact | standard | quick
    SCD_COMPRESSION_LEVEL: 6       # gzip compression level (0-9)
    SCD_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME: 600    # Max seconds for SCD (default: 400)
    SCD_THREADS: 4                 # Parallel threads for SCD
    SKIP_SCD: false                # Can override globally here

  deploy:
    # Variables for the DEPLOY phase
    SCD_STRATEGY: compact          # If SCD runs in deploy phase
    UPDATE_URLS: true              # Update base URLs in DB on deploy
    CLEAN_STATIC_FILES: true       # Clear pub/static/ before SCD

  post_deploy:
    WARM_UP_PAGES:                 # Pages to warm cache after deploy
      - "/"
      - "/checkout"
      - "/catalog/category/view/id/1"
```

### SCD Phase Control

The *location* of `SCD_STRATEGY` determines which phase SCD runs in:

```yaml
# Option A: SCD runs in BUILD phase (RECOMMENDED)
stage:
  build:
    SCD_STRATEGY: compact
  deploy:
    SKIP_SCD: true    # Don't run SCD again in deploy

# Option B: SCD runs in DEPLOY phase (more downtime)
stage:
  build:
    SKIP_SCD: true    # Skip in build
  deploy:
    SCD_STRATEGY: compact   # Run in deploy instead

# Option C: SCD on demand (DEV ONLY)
stage:
  global:
    SCD_ON_DEMAND: true
```

### Important SCD Variables Summary

| Variable | Stage | Values | Purpose |
|----------|-------|--------|---------|
| `SCD_STRATEGY` | build/deploy | compact, standard, quick | Deployment strategy |
| `SCD_ON_DEMAND` | global | true/false | Lazy generation on request |
| `SKIP_SCD` | build/deploy | true/false | Skip SCD entirely |
| `SCD_THREADS` | build/deploy | integer | Parallel processing threads |
| `SCD_COMPRESSION_LEVEL` | build/deploy | 0-9 | gzip compression level |
| `SCD_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` | build/deploy | seconds | Timeout for SCD process |
| `CLEAN_STATIC_FILES` | deploy | true/false | Clear pub/static/ before SCD |

**Exam focus:**
- `.magento.env.yaml` is committed to the repository and **version controlled**
- Variables under `stage.build` affect the build phase, `stage.deploy` affect deploy phase
- `stage.global` variables apply to all stages
- To move SCD to build phase: put `SCD_STRATEGY` under `stage.build` and `SKIP_SCD: true` under `stage.deploy`

## 13. Tricky Exam Concepts & Common Pitfalls

This section covers the nuances most likely to appear on the exam.

### 13.1 SCD_ON_DEMAND is NOT for Production

```
WRONG approach for production:
  .magento.env.yaml:
    stage:
      global:
        SCD_ON_DEMAND: true   <-- DON'T DO THIS ON PRODUCTION

WHY IT'S WRONG:
  - First user to hit a page after deploy triggers static file generation
  - This can take 2-15 seconds per file
  - Users see slow pages or even unstyled content
  - High server load on first wave of post-deploy traffic

CORRECT approach for production:
  stage:
    build:
      SCD_STRATEGY: compact  # Generate during build phase
```

### 13.2 SCD in Build Phase Reduces Downtime

```
SCD in DEPLOY phase timeline:
  [Maintenance ON] --> [DB migrations] --> [SCD - 5 minutes] --> [Maintenance OFF]
  Total downtime: 5+ minutes

SCD in BUILD phase timeline:
  [Build - 5 minutes, site still UP] --> [Maintenance ON] --> [DB migrations] --> [Maintenance OFF]
  Total downtime: < 1 minute
```

**The key insight:** The build phase runs on a *separate build container* — the live site keeps serving traffic. Only the deploy phase triggers maintenance mode.

### 13.3 Fastly Not Active in Integration Environments

```
WRONG assumption:
  "I'll test Fastly CDN caching in my integration branch"
  -> This WON'T WORK — Fastly is not in the request path for integration envs

CORRECT understanding:
  Integration environments:
    Browser -> Nginx on origin -> Magento
    (No Fastly, no CDN caching, no image optimization)

  Staging/Production:
    Browser -> Fastly Edge -> (cache hit: done) or (cache miss: Nginx -> Magento)
```

### 13.4 mount:download is Read-Only (from Cloud perspective)

```
magento-cloud mount:download  = PULL from cloud to local (read)
magento-cloud mount:upload    = PUSH from local to cloud (write)

Common mistake:
  Developer edits a CSS file locally
  Runs mount:download hoping it will UPDATE the cloud
  -> This OVERWRITES local files with cloud versions!

Correct workflow for pushing frontend changes:
  1. Edit files locally
  2. git commit
  3. magento-cloud environment:push
  -> Pipeline runs -> SCD generates new CSS -> Deployed to cloud
```

### 13.5 Static Files Cannot Be Directly Uploaded in Production

In Cloud Production/Staging environments, `pub/static/` is a writable mount, but changes made via SSH or mount:upload are **ephemeral** — they will be overwritten on the next deploy when SCD runs again.

```
WRONG workflow:
  SSH into production -> Edit CSS in pub/static/ -> Changes lost on next deploy

CORRECT workflow:
  Edit Less/CSS source in app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/web/
  -> git commit
  -> git push (triggers pipeline)
  -> SCD regenerates pub/static/ from source
```

### 13.6 SKIP_SCD ≠ SCD_ON_DEMAND

| | SKIP_SCD | SCD_ON_DEMAND |
|--|---------|---------------|
| SCD runs during deploy? | No | No |
| Assets generated when? | Never (pre-built externally) | First HTTP request |
| Suitable for production? | Yes (with CDN) | No |
| Requires external CDN? | Yes (typically) | No |
| First-request performance | Fast (CDN serves) | Slow (generation overhead) |

**Exam focus:**
- Know all six tricky concepts above by heart
- The exam frequently tests: (1) SCD_ON_DEMAND not for production, (2) build phase = less downtime, (3) Fastly not in integration environments

## 14. Hands-On: Reviewing SCD Configuration Options

### Practical Exercise: Configure SCD for Build Phase

**Step 1:** Check your current `.magento.env.yaml`

```bash
# In your local project:
cat .magento.env.yaml
```

**Step 2:** Configure SCD to run in build phase

```yaml
# .magento.env.yaml
stage:
  global:
    SCD_ON_DEMAND: false
  build:
    SCD_STRATEGY: compact
    SCD_THREADS: 3
    SCD_COMPRESSION_LEVEL: 6
  deploy:
    SKIP_SCD: true
    CLEAN_STATIC_FILES: true
  post_deploy:
    WARM_UP_PAGES:
      - "/"
      - "/checkout/cart"
```

**Step 3:** Commit and push

```bash
git add .magento.env.yaml
git commit -m "Move SCD to build phase with compact strategy"
magento-cloud environment:push
```

**Step 4:** Monitor the deployment

```bash
# Watch the deployment log in real-time
magento-cloud activity:log --tail

# Or SSH in after deploy to verify static files
magento-cloud ssh -e integration
ls -la pub/static/frontend/
```

### Practical Exercise: Test SCD Strategies

```bash
# SSH into integration environment
magento-cloud ssh -e integration

# Time how long SCD takes with different strategies:

# Test compact (default)
time bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy \
  --theme Magento/luma en_US -f

# Clear pub/static and test quick
rm -rf pub/static/frontend
time bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy \
  --theme Magento/luma en_US -f \
  --strategy quick

# Clear pub/static and test standard  
rm -rf pub/static/frontend
time bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy \
  --theme Magento/luma en_US -f \
  --strategy standard
```

### Practical Exercise: Verify Fastly Integration (Staging)

```bash
# SSH into staging
magento-cloud ssh -e staging

# Check if Fastly module is active
bin/magento module:status Fastly_Cdn

# View Fastly configuration
bin/magento config:show fastly_cdn

# Check response headers from Fastly
curl -I https://staging.your-store.com/pub/static/version.../styles-m.css
# Look for:
#   X-Cache: HIT (served from Fastly cache)
#   X-Cache: MISS (fetched from origin)
#   Fastly-IO: (image optimization active)
```

### Reviewing the SCD Configuration Decision Tree

```
Is this a PRODUCTION environment?
  |
  +-- YES
  |     |
  |     v
  |   Is static content pre-built and on external CDN?
  |     |
  |     +-- YES --> SKIP_SCD: true (let CDN serve assets)
  |     |
  |     +-- NO  --> SCD_STRATEGY: compact/quick in BUILD phase
  |                 (not deploy phase, reduces downtime)
  |
  +-- NO (Integration/Dev)
        |
        v
      Iteration speed important?
        |
        +-- YES --> SCD_ON_DEMAND: true (generate on first request)
        |
        +-- NO  --> SCD_STRATEGY: compact in build or deploy phase
```
