## Quick-Reference Checklist

### magento-cloud CLI Commands
- [ ] `magento-cloud ssh` — Opens interactive shell on cloud environment
- [ ] `magento-cloud ssh -e <env-id>` — SSH into a specific environment
- [ ] `magento-cloud ssh -e staging -- bin/magento cache:flush` — Run single command remotely
- [ ] `magento-cloud mount:download --mount pub/static --target ./pub/static` — Pull static files from cloud to local
- [ ] `magento-cloud mount:download` uses rsync; `--delete` flag removes local files not on remote
- [ ] `magento-cloud environment:push` — Triggers full build/deploy pipeline for current branch
- [ ] `magento-cloud environments` — List all environments in the project
- [ ] `magento-cloud activity:log --tail` — Watch deployment logs in real-time

### SCD Strategies
- [ ] `compact` — Default Cloud `SCD_STRATEGY`; moderate speed; reuses shared base files (note: on-premise CLI defaults to `quick`)
- [ ] `standard` — Slowest; deploys ALL themes × ALL locales fully independently; most thorough
- [ ] `quick` — Fastest; minimum file generation; aggressive symlink/sharing
- [ ] Strategy is set via `SCD_STRATEGY` in `.magento.env.yaml` under `stage.build` or `stage.deploy`

### SCD Phase Control
- [ ] SCD in **build phase** = site stays UP during SCD = **less downtime** (preferred)
- [ ] SCD in **deploy phase** = site in maintenance mode during SCD = **more downtime**
- [ ] SCD cannot run meaningfully in post-deploy phase
- [ ] To move SCD to build: `SCD_STRATEGY` under `stage.build` + `SKIP_SCD: true` under `stage.deploy`

### SCD_ON_DEMAND
- [ ] Generates static files on **first HTTP request** (lazy generation)
- [ ] **NOT suitable for production** — first request after deploy is slow
- [ ] Designed for **development/integration environments** only
- [ ] Set via `SCD_ON_DEMAND: true` under `stage.global`

### SKIP_SCD
- [ ] Completely bypasses SCD during the pipeline
- [ ] Primary use case: **CDN with pre-built assets**
- [ ] Set via `SKIP_SCD: true` under `stage.build` or `stage.deploy`
- [ ] Unlike SCD_ON_DEMAND, there is NO on-demand generation — assets must be elsewhere

### Fastly CDN
- [ ] Fastly is included with Adobe Commerce Cloud (Starter and Pro)
- [ ] Fastly is **ONLY active on Staging and Production** — NOT on Integration environments
- [ ] Fastly caches `pub/static/` assets at edge nodes globally
- [ ] Cache purge on deploy occurs via URL versioning (timestamp in path changes)
- [ ] Fastly does NOT serve `pub/static/` directly in development/integration environments

### Fastly Image Optimization
- [ ] Automatic **WebP conversion** based on browser `Accept: image/webp` header
- [ ] **Responsive images** served via query parameters (`?width=800&quality=85`)
- [ ] Processing happens at CDN edge — no origin server CPU overhead
- [ ] Separate from Magento native image resizing (`pub/media/cache/`)

### Frontend Performance on Cloud
- [ ] **Pre-compression** — gzip + brotli versions of CSS/JS generated at build time; served without runtime CPU cost
- [ ] **HTTP/2 Push** — Server proactively sends critical assets (CSS/JS) before browser requests them
- [ ] **ESI (Edge Side Includes)** — Enables full-page caching while keeping personalized blocks dynamic
- [ ] ESI blocks are fetched separately by Fastly from origin; enables mixing cached frames with dynamic content

### .magento.env.yaml Key Variables
- [ ] `SCD_STRATEGY` — compact | standard | quick
- [ ] `SCD_ON_DEMAND` — true/false (true = dev only)
- [ ] `SKIP_SCD` — true/false (true = skip entirely)
- [ ] `SCD_THREADS` — integer (parallel processing threads)
- [ ] `SCD_COMPRESSION_LEVEL` — 0-9 (gzip compression)
- [ ] `SCD_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` — seconds (SCD timeout)
- [ ] `CLEAN_STATIC_FILES` — true/false (clear pub/static/ before SCD)
- [ ] `WARM_UP_PAGES` — list of URLs to cache-warm in post_deploy

### Critical Exam Traps
- [ ] **SCD_ON_DEMAND ≠ production-safe** — slow first request, dev/integration only
- [ ] **SKIP_SCD ≠ SCD_ON_DEMAND** — SKIP_SCD has NO fallback generation; requires external CDN
- [ ] **Fastly not in integration** — cannot test Fastly caching in integration environments
- [ ] **mount:download is a READ/PULL** — it does not push your local edits to cloud
- [ ] **Direct pub/static/ edits are ephemeral** — overwritten by next SCD run; always edit source files
- [ ] **Build phase = no maintenance mode** — moving SCD to build phase is the primary way to reduce deploy downtime
- [ ] **standard strategy ≠ compact** — standard deploys ALL theme×locale combinations independently; compact reuses shared files

flashcards.question: What is the magento-cloud CLI tool and how is it different from bin/magento?
flashcards.answer: The magento-cloud CLI is the official command-line interface for Adobe Commerce on Cloud Infrastructure, separate from bin/magento. It manages cloud-specific operations like SSH access to environments, file transfers, and deployments. bin/magento handles Magento application tasks (cache, SCD, module management). You must run magento-cloud auth:login to authenticate before using project-specific commands. Projects have hierarchical environments: Production > Staging > Integration.
flashcards.hint: One manages the cloud infrastructure and environments, the other manages the Magento application itself.

flashcards.question: What are the three deployment phases in Adobe Commerce Cloud, and in which phase should SCD run to minimize downtime?
flashcards.answer: The three phases are: Build (read-only filesystem, no DB access, site stays up), Deploy (maintenance mode ON, DB access, migrations run), and Post-Deploy (site is live, cache warm-up, indexing). SCD should run in the Build phase to minimize downtime because the build runs on a separate container while the live site continues serving traffic. Running SCD in the Deploy phase increases downtime since the site is in maintenance mode during that time.
flashcards.hint: Only one phase keeps the site available to users, and that is where long-running processes like SCD should execute.

flashcards.question: What is SCD_ON_DEMAND and why should it never be used in production?
flashcards.answer: SCD_ON_DEMAND (set to true in .magento.env.yaml under stage.global) makes static content generated on the first HTTP request that needs it, rather than during build or deploy. This is unsuitable for production because the first user after deployment triggers file generation, experiencing 2-15 second delays and possibly seeing unstyled pages. It is designed only for development/integration environments where fast iteration matters more than first-request performance.
flashcards.hint: Lazy generation saves deployment time but punishes real users who are the first to request each asset.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between SKIP_SCD and SCD_ON_DEMAND in Adobe Commerce Cloud?
flashcards.answer: SKIP_SCD completely bypasses Static Content Deployment with no fallback generation — assets must already exist elsewhere (typically on an external CDN). SCD_ON_DEMAND also skips SCD during deployment but generates assets lazily on the first HTTP request. SKIP_SCD is suitable for production when using a CDN with pre-built assets. SCD_ON_DEMAND is only suitable for dev/integration environments due to slow first-request performance.
flashcards.hint: One has a fallback mechanism for missing files, the other has no fallback at all.

flashcards.question: What does the magento-cloud mount:download command do, and what is the common mistake developers make with it?
flashcards.answer: mount:download pulls files from a cloud environment's writable mount to your local machine using rsync. For example: magento-cloud mount:download --mount pub/static --target ./pub/static. The common mistake is running mount:download expecting it to push local changes to the cloud — it actually does the opposite, overwriting local files with cloud versions. To push changes, use git commit followed by magento-cloud environment:push.
flashcards.hint: The 'download' direction goes FROM cloud TO local, and the only way to update cloud files is through the deployment pipeline.

flashcards.question: In which Adobe Commerce Cloud environments is Fastly CDN active, and what serves static files in environments where Fastly is not active?
flashcards.answer: Fastly CDN is only active on Staging and Production environments (Cloud Pro plan). On Integration environments and local development, Fastly is NOT in the request path — Nginx on the origin server serves static files directly. This means you cannot test Fastly CDN caching, image optimization, or ESI behavior in integration environments. Testing these features requires access to Staging.
flashcards.hint: The CDN layer only exists in certain environment types — others go directly to the web server.

flashcards.question: What are the three SCD_STRATEGY values in Adobe Commerce Cloud, and which is the default?
flashcards.answer: The three strategies are: compact (default on Cloud, moderate speed, reuses shared base files), standard (slowest, deploys all theme x locale combinations fully independently, highest disk usage), and quick (fastest, minimum file generation, aggressive sharing). Note that the on-premise CLI defaults to quick, while Cloud defaults to compact. The strategy is set via SCD_STRATEGY in .magento.env.yaml under stage.build or stage.deploy.
flashcards.hint: Cloud and on-premise have different default strategies — and the three options trade off speed vs. isolation.

flashcards.question: How does Fastly Image Optimization (IO) handle WebP conversion on Adobe Commerce Cloud?
flashcards.answer: Fastly IO intercepts image requests and checks the browser's Accept header. If the browser supports WebP (sends Accept: image/webp), Fastly automatically converts JPEG/PNG images to WebP on-the-fly at the CDN edge, achieving 30-80% smaller file sizes. Browsers without WebP support receive the original format. This processing happens at the edge with no origin server CPU overhead, and is separate from Magento's native image resizing that writes to pub/media/cache/.
flashcards.hint: The conversion happens at the CDN edge based on what the browser says it can accept.

flashcards.question: What is the .magento.env.yaml file and what SCD-related variables can be configured in it?
flashcards.answer: The .magento.env.yaml file is the primary configuration file for deployment behavior on Adobe Commerce Cloud, committed to the repository and version-controlled. Key SCD variables include: SCD_STRATEGY (compact/standard/quick), SCD_ON_DEMAND (true/false), SKIP_SCD (true/false), SCD_THREADS (parallel threads), SCD_COMPRESSION_LEVEL (0-9 gzip level), SCD_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME (timeout), and CLEAN_STATIC_FILES (clear pub/static before SCD). Variables under stage.build affect the build phase; stage.deploy affects the deploy phase; stage.global applies to all stages.
flashcards.hint: This YAML file is structured by deployment stages, with each stage having its own configuration scope.

flashcards.question: How do you move SCD from the deploy phase to the build phase in Adobe Commerce Cloud?
flashcards.answer: In .magento.env.yaml, set SCD_STRATEGY under stage.build (e.g., SCD_STRATEGY: compact) and set SKIP_SCD: true under stage.deploy. This ensures SCD runs during the build phase (when the site is still up) and is skipped during the deploy phase (when the site is in maintenance mode). This is the primary way to reduce deployment downtime — the build phase runs on a separate container while the live site continues serving traffic.
flashcards.hint: You need to configure two sections of the YAML — enable SCD in one phase and disable it in the other.

flashcards.question: What is Edge Side Includes (ESI) and how does it work with Fastly on Adobe Commerce Cloud?
flashcards.answer: ESI is an HTML markup standard that allows portions of a web page to be assembled at the CDN edge. Fastly serves the cached page frame (static header, footer, content) from its edge cache, then makes separate requests to the origin for dynamic ESI blocks (like cart summary, recently viewed, greeting widgets). This enables full-page caching while keeping personalized blocks dynamic. ESI blocks are fetched by Fastly, not by the browser — the user receives a fully assembled page.
flashcards.hint: The CDN serves most of the page from cache but fetches small personalized portions separately from the server.

flashcards.question: What happens to static files that are directly edited via SSH on a Cloud production or staging environment?
flashcards.answer: Direct edits to pub/static/ files via SSH on production or staging environments are ephemeral — they will be overwritten on the next deployment when SCD runs again. The correct workflow is to edit LESS/CSS/JS source files in app/design/frontend/Vendor/Theme/web/, commit the changes to Git, and push via magento-cloud environment:push. The deployment pipeline then regenerates pub/static/ from source files.
flashcards.hint: The deployment pipeline regenerates all static assets from source, so manual edits to the output directory are temporary.

flashcards.question: What frontend performance features does Adobe Commerce Cloud provide at the server/CDN level?
flashcards.answer: Adobe Commerce Cloud provides three key performance features: 1) Pre-compression — gzip and brotli versions of CSS/JS are generated at build time and served without runtime CPU cost, with brotli offering ~20% better compression than gzip. 2) HTTP/2 Push — the server proactively sends critical CSS/JS assets before the browser requests them, reducing waterfall delays. 3) ESI (Edge Side Includes) — enables full-page caching while keeping personalized blocks dynamic by having Fastly assemble pages from cached frames and fresh dynamic content.
flashcards.hint: These features work at the infrastructure level — compression, proactive delivery, and smart page assembly.

flashcards.question: How does Fastly CDN handle cache purging when new static assets are deployed on Adobe Commerce Cloud?
flashcards.answer: Cache purging occurs through two mechanisms: URL versioning and explicit API calls. Each SCD run generates a new Unix timestamp in pub/static/deployed_version.txt, which changes all static asset URLs (e.g., /pub/static/version1680000000/... becomes /pub/static/version1690000000/...). Since the URL changes, Fastly treats it as a cache miss and fetches the fresh file from the origin. Explicit Fastly API purge calls also happen during post-deploy hooks.
flashcards.hint: The URLs for static files contain a changing version number, which naturally causes the CDN to fetch new content.

flashcards.question: What does the magento-cloud environment:push command trigger, and why can't you just FTP files to production?
flashcards.answer: environment:push triggers the full build-deploy pipeline: Build phase (composer install, SCD if configured, asset compilation into read-only filesystem), Deploy phase (maintenance mode, DB migrations, SCD if configured, cache warm-up), and Post-Deploy phase (cache flush, search index updates). You cannot FTP files because production uses a managed pipeline — frontend changes must go through Git commits and the build/deploy process. Static assets are regenerated during the pipeline according to SCD configuration.
flashcards.hint: This command starts an entire automated pipeline, not just a file transfer.
